title: Operations Manager
descriptionHtml:
Job summary
Our WW Operations network delivers millions of packages and smiles to Amazon customers every day. We are looking for motivated, customer-focused individuals who want to join our team as an Operations Manager. In this role, you will lead and develop a team of salaried and hourly talent. You will be responsible for engaging your team during their shifts to maintain the highest levels of safety, quality, attendance, and performance. To achieve this, managers are expected to provide their team with the tools needed for success while driving improvements in productivity and efficiency through data-driven decisions and analytical problem-solving. You will also play a key role in maintaining our customer expectations to ensure customer orders are delivered at the right time, to the right location.

Our Operation’s workflow has three major components: First mile - where the product is housed and ready for order; Middle mile - where the order is hauled to your area; and Last mile - when the product is delivered to the customer’s door. Please note that all workflows have slight building variations, but one thing is constant: our vision and dedication to the customer.

Key Responsibilities and Job Elements:
- Support, mentor, and motivate your salaried and hourly workforce
- Lead large-scope projects with site and regional impact
- Build and execute productivity plans through forecast reviews, determining productivity requirements, and partnering with other Leaders to load balance
- Manage safety, quality, productivity, and customer delivery promises
- Collaborate with all support teams including Safety, Engineering, Loss Prevention, Quality Assurance, Human Resources to develop plans to meet business objectives
- Lift up to 49 pounds and frequently push, pull, squat, bend, and reach
- Stand/walk for up to 12 hours during shifts
- Work in an environment where the noise level varies and can be loud
- Work in an environment that is subject to variable temperatures and weather (delivery stations include outside loading departments)
- Continuously climb and descend stairs (applies to sites with stairs)
Our fulfillment network launches new Operations sites every year, providing various opportunities for your professional growth. We hire Operations Managers based on location preference and the business’ current openings.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of employee and performance management experience
- Bachelor's degree or equivalent, or 2+ years of Amazon (blue badge/FTE) experience
- Work a flexible schedule/shift/work area, including weekends, nights, and/or holidays

Preferred qualifications

- 1+ years of performance metrics, process improvement or lean techniques experience
- Experience managing a team of 2+ salaried employees and 70+ indirect employees
- Experience scoping, leading, and implementing process improvements through: Lean process, Kaizen, and/or Six Sigma.
- Demonstrated problem solving skills and analytical skills
- Excellent customer service skills, communication skills and interpersonal skills

title: Manager, Supplier Food Safety and Quality Assurance
descriptionHtml:
Senior Food Safety Manager is a role within the Food Safety & Quality organization, focusing primarily on WWGS Private Brands. This position is responsible for ensuring the safety, compliance, and continuous improvement of all food production sites that supply our private brand portfolio. The manager will lead a team focused on facility approvals, conduct rigorous due diligence and facility reviews, and manage corrective and preventive actions (CAPAs). The role requires deep collaboration with cross-functional teams and proficiency in multiple digital platforms, including Foodlogiq, CMX1, and internal Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) tools. Candidate must have a proven track record leading Food Safety Professionals, utilizing soft skills, effective decision making, and metrics to drive improvements across an organization.

Key job responsibilities
1. Leadership Presence
• Demonstrated ability to drive performance within a food safety team
• Cross-functional networking across stakeholder business units to champion food safety
• Ability to present metrics rich data to teams and persuade an audience to support proposals.
2. Facility Approval & Due Diligence
• New Facility Qualification: Perform the end-to-end qualification of new food production sites for WWGS Private Brands, ensuring all regulatory, hygiene, and safety standards are met before any product is released.
• Ongoing Due Diligence: Maintain and update due diligence documentation for all existing production sites, including audits, certifications, and compliance evidence.
• Risk Assessment: Perform periodic risk assessments to identify potential hazards and develop mitigation strategies.
• Onboarding Process: Optimize and implement an efficient supplier onboarding workflow that integrates food safety criteria, facility qualification, and system data entry.
• Stakeholder Collaboration: Work closely with Procurement, Supply Chain, Product Development, and Quality teams to align food safety requirements with procurement strategies and product launch timelines.
3. Facility Reviews & Inspections
• On-Site Reviews: Conduct comprehensive reviews at risk prioritized production sites to verify adherence to food safety standards, GMPs, and internal policies.
• Audit Leadership: Coordinate and lead internal and third party audits, incorporate findings, and ensure timely implementation of corrective actions.
• Supplier Scorecarding: Maintain a supplier scorecard system that captures performance metrics (e.g., audit results, CAPA closure rates, compliance status) and feeds into supplier selection and renewal decisions.
4. Systems & Tool Proficiency
• Platform Management: Become an expert user of Foodlogiq, CMX1, and internal Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) tools. Ensure all food safety data is accurately entered, maintained, and reported through these systems.
• Process Optimization: Advise on how to leverage these tools to streamline supplier onboarding, improve visibility into supplier performance, and automate routine due diligence tasks.
• Data-Driven Decision Making: Pull and analyze data from the platforms to generate insights, dashboards, and trend reports that support strategic decision-making.
5. Corrective & Preventive Actions (CAPA)
• Incident Management: Work closely with the Incident Management team to investigate and close out CAPAs resulting from food safety incidents, non-conformances, or audit findings.
• Root Cause Analysis: Lead root cause investigations, develop effective corrective actions, and verify effectiveness of preventive actions.
• CAPA Tracking: Maintain a centralized CAPA log within the appropriate system, ensuring timely closure and documentation of all actions.
6. Policy, Procedure & Compliance
• Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs): Develop, maintain, and enforce SOPs related to facility qualification, audit planning, and CAPA management.
• Regulatory Compliance: Ensure all activities comply with FDA, FSMA, USDA, and other applicable food safety regulations.
• Continuous Improvement: Champion a culture of continuous improvement through regular reviews of processes, metrics, and system capabilities.
7. Reporting & Communication
• Executive Reporting: Provide regular updates to senior leadership on key metrics (e.g., audit results, CAPA closure rates, supplier performance) through dashboards and written reports.
• Cross-Functional Updates: Deliver clear, data driven presentations to cross-functional teams to communicate risk status, audit findings, and improvement initiatives.

We build customer trust in our food safety and quality programs. We do this through our long term vision, operational excellence, partnership with business stakeholders, and commitment to technology.

descriptionHtml:
Transform network infrastructure by joining our dynamic team! You'll be at the forefront of developing innovative solutions that drive network stability and scalability, using your technical expertise to create automated systems that power global technological advancement.

Infra Delivery Install Technicians will collaborate with cross-functional teams, troubleshoot complex technical scenarios, and implement strategic solutions that keep our network running seamlessly. Expect to engage in hands-on technical work that requires creativity, precision, and a passion for technological innovation.

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

NOTE: Amazon does not sponsor for immigration, including for H-1B, TN, and other non-immigrant visas, for this role.

NOTE: Lump sum stipend will be provided to eligible candidates who relocate for this position.

Key job responsibilities
Key job responsibilities
- Moving and implementing large enterprise equipment
- Installing Fiber and Copper cabling and patching cabling between equipment
- Ensuring proper safety and security standards are maintained during cabling and rack installation,
- Following well established hardware installation procedures and break-fix activities
- Safely using material handling tools and equipment
- Traveling within and outside of the regional work area is required. You will be responsible for having a reliable personal vehicle and valid driver's license to travel within the regional work area, as company transportation will not be provided

Physical Requirements:
- Regularly lift and/or move up to 40 pounds; and participate in group lifts for 41+ pounds
- Ability to work in an environment that operates 24/7 with an ability to participate in primary responder rotation and provide after-hours support as needed
- Working in cramped and/or elevated and/or noisy environments
- Bending, lifting, stretching, reaching, standing and walking for up to 8+ hours a day
- Ascending and descending ladders, stairs, and gangways safely and without limitation

This role supports data centers in various operational stages. The position may be assigned to a facility still under development, which could require travel to established locations for training until your designated site becomes fully operational.

Essential Requirements:
- Ability to travel to or commute between data center locations as needed
- Willingness to temporarily work at alternative sites during training periods or until assigned facility is operational
- Travel frequency will vary based on business needs and operational status of assigned facility

Candidates must be able to travel (over 50 miles) or commute (less than 50 miles) to active data center sites as required by business needs.

Basic qualifications

- 1+ years of Computer Hardware Repair, Infrastructure Cabling, Network Deployment, or Data Center Operations experience, or experience in similar technical or vocational roles
- High School diploma or equivalent

Preferred qualifications

- industry standard certification (CompTIA, CCENT, or Network+)
- Experience with cabling infrastructure best practices and methodologies
- Knowledge of network cabling, optic types, and test equipment

descriptionHtml:

title: Software Development Engineer, Ads Campaign Management
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Advertising is one of Amazon's fastest growing and most profitable businesses, responsible for defining and delivering AI-powered solutions that transform how advertisers make strategic decisions. We deliver billions of ad impressions and process massive volumes of advertiser data every single day. You'll work with us to pioneer breakthrough approaches in how AI agents access and reason over real-time advertiser data at scale.

The Campaign Management team is responsible for capturing inputs for advertisers to control their advertising efforts. You can think of our team as the brain and nervous system of all the advertisements you see on amazon.com. We build large scale, high velocity distributed systems to service 100’s of millions of API requests per day, steam data at PB scale, process business logic on tight latency budgets, all while streaming and the data at high fidelity to 20+ other services to perform other critical advertising functions. We stand up world class CI/CD pipelines to deploy our service automating infrastructure provisioning, high volume load testing and first-rate monitoring so our engineers can keep their heads down inventing for our advertisers. Our problem space covers concurrent workflows across distributed systems (linearizability, eventual consistency), big data problems (propagation delay, ordering and hygiene) and performance (search optimization). Our team uses the latest AWS products and services to solve our problems including but not limited to: ECS, Fargate, EC2, EMR, Lambda, Kafka, Elastic Search, Dynamo DB, SQS, SNS, Cloud watch, CDK, Cloud Formation and many more.

We are using generative AI and agentic systems to help advertising agents provide instant, strategic advice to millions of advertisers. You will need to invent new techniques for global ads experience, agent orchestration, and context optimization to ensure we're delivering accurate, trustworthy insights with minimal latency and token consumption. You'll create feedback loops to ensure our solutions are constantly evaluating themselves and improving.

- Establish system design patterns and best practices for global ads experience at scale

title: Software Development Manager, Emerging Devices Software
descriptionHtml:
Join us in building the future of personal devices at Amazon!

Are you ready to shape the future of how people experience technology in their everyday lives? Join us in building the next generation of personal devices — where hardware, software, and AI converge to create experiences that feel like magic.

The Emerging Devices Software (EDS) organization is pioneering intelligent software solutions that power Amazon's Personal Devices, including Smart Eyewear and other emerging wearable categories. Our mission is to create seamless, AI-driven experiences that live at the intersection of hardware, software, and artificial intelligence — redefining how customers interact with technology in their daily lives. We're building the future of personal devices while maintaining Amazon's highest standards for quality, reliability, and customer obsession.

The personal devices challenge is a fascinating blend of real-world complexity and technological innovation. We're tackling multidimensional problems that span mobile applications, cloud services, on-device intelligence, and hardware integration — all while delivering best-in-class user experiences to customers around the world. From optimizing low-latency interactions on constrained wearable hardware to building scalable cloud backends and integrating ML/AI capabilities, every problem we solve pushes the boundaries of what's possible.

We are looking for a seasoned Software Development Manager to lead an engineering team within EDS, solving these intricate challenges. You'll work on software that span the mobile-cloud stack, own end-to-end delivery of features and experiences, and help shape the long-term technical direction of our products.

- Partner closely with product managers, UX designers, QA, and cross-functional engineering teams to define requirements and deliver high-impact features from concept to launch

- Set a high engineering bar through rigorous design reviews, code quality standards, and best practices across the software development lifecycle

- Identify and resolve technical risks, ambiguities, and complex issues spanning the device, mobile, and cloud layers of the stack

- Recruit, hire, and develop top engineering talent, building a diverse and high-performing team aligned to Amazon's Leadership Principles

- Communicate effectively with senior leadership and stakeholders on team progress, technical direction, and strategic priorities

- Contribute to the long-term technical roadmap of EDS, helping shape the future of wearable and personal device technology at Amazon

A day in the life
- Real-World Impact: Your team's code will power experiences used by customers every day — on devices they wear, carry, and rely on to stay connected to the world around them

- Scale That Matters: You'll build systems that serve customers globally, operating reliably across diverse environments, connectivity conditions, and device form factors

- State of the Art Tech Stack: You'll leverage the latest in AI, mobile development, and cloud computing to solve real-world problems at the intersection of hardware and software

- Innovation at Scale: You'll lead a team that isn't just implementing existing solutions — you'll be creating entirely new experiences for wearable and personal device experiences

- End-to-End Ownership: You'll own complete solutions from mobile application features to cloud services, from device integration to production operations

About the team
The SDEs in your team will:

- Design, implement, and maintain features for mobile applications (Android, iOS, React Native) and cloud services that power Amazon's Personal Devices

- Write and maintain high-quality, well-tested code for critical components of the device-mobile-cloud stack

- Be responsible for building and maintaining robust testing frameworks, monitoring system performance, and ensuring software operates reliably across diverse device and connectivity scenarios

- Work in an agile environment, participating in technical design discussions and code reviews while helping to establish best practices for software development across mobile and cloud

- Investigate and resolve complex issues spanning the device, mobile, and cloud layers of the stack

- Contribute to the continuous improvement of team processes, tools, and engineering practices as the product and platform evolve

And all this happens under the strong leadership of talented SDMs like you!

- 7+ years of engineering experience
- 3+ years of engineering team management experience
- 8+ years of leading the definition and development of multi tier web services experience

title: Sr. Applied Scientist - CV, Vulcan Stow
descriptionHtml:
Do you want to create the greatest-possible worldwide impact in Robotics? Amazon has the world's most exciting treasure trove of robotics challenges. At Amazon Robotics we build high-performance, real-time robotic systems that can perceive, learn, and act intelligently alongside humans—at Amazon scale. Amazon Robotics invents and scales AI systems for robotics in fulfillment. Our mission is to enable robots to interact safely, efficiently, and fluently high density real-world fulfillment centers. Our AI solutions enable robots to learn from their own experiences, from each other, and from humans to build intelligence that feeds itself.

We hire and develop subject matter experts in AI with a focus on 3D perception, computer vision, deep learning, and generative modeling. We target high-impact algorithmic unlocks in areas such as 3D scene understanding and completion, semantic occupancy prediction, multi-view 3D reconstruction, depth estimation, shape completion, and real-time inference - all of which have high-value impact for our current and future fulfillment networks.

We are seeking an passionate, hands-on, seasoned Senior Applied Scientist who will be deep in code and algorithms; who is technically strong in building scalable 3D perception systems across semantic scene completion, encoder-decoder and transformer architectures (e.g., VoxFormer, MonoScene), voxelized occupancy prediction, panoptic and instance segmentation, depth estimation, point cloud processing, and multi-view fusion. As a Senior Applied Scientist, you will contribute to the research and development of advanced 3D perception pipelines that enable robots to reason about occluded and partially observed environments; your work along with other top-notch scientists and engineers will deliver the world's most scalable and robust robotic perception systems. You will drive ideas to products using paradigms such as 3D generative models, query-based transformers, masked autoencoder-style completion, and scalable pseudo-ground-truth data generation.

As a Senior Applied Scientist, you will also help lead and mentor our team of applied scientists and engineers. You will take on challenging perception problems - such as completing 3D bin scenes from partial observations, integrating multi-camera inputs, and optimizing inference latency for edge deployment - distill requirements, and then deliver solutions that either leverage existing academic and industrial research or utilize your own out-of-the-box but pragmatic thinking. In addition to coming up with novel solutions and prototypes, you will directly contribute to implementation while you lead. A successful candidate has excellent technical depth in 3D computer vision, scientific vision, project management skills, great communication skills, and a drive to achieve results in a collaborative team environment.

You should enjoy the process of solving real-world problems that, quite frankly, haven't been solved at scale anywhere before. Along the way, we guarantee you'll get opportunities to be a disruptor, prolific innovator, and a reputed problem solver—someone who truly enables AI and robotics to significantly impact the lives of millions of consumers.


Key job responsibilities
Architect, design, and implement 3D perception models - including encoder-decoder networks, query-based transformers, and generative architectures- for semantic occupancy prediction and scene completion on robotic platforms.

Own the end-to-end model lifecycle: develop scalable training pipelines, optimize inference latency for ARM-based edge processors, and deploy production models that meet real-time performance targets.
Design and scale pseudo-ground-truth data generation pipelines - both heuristic-based and learning-based (e.g., SAM3D, shape completion) to produce curated training samples using SageMaker infrastructure.
Drive multi-view perception integration by fusing multiple view camera inputs for robust 3D reconstruction in partially observed and occluded bin environments.

Influence the team's technical strategy and contribute to the long-term vision and roadmap for 3D perception in fulfillment robotics.
Partner with cross-functional stakeholders across engineering, science, and operations teams to define requirements, iterate on system design, and deliver end-to-end solutions from research prototype to production deployment.

Maintain high standards by participating in design and code reviews, designing for fault tolerance and operational excellence, and creating mechanisms for continuous improvement.
Prototype and validate concepts through simulation, synthetic data evaluation, and live robotic workcell testing using 3D metrics (mIoU, IoU) and affordance-based evaluation frameworks.

Mentor applied scientists and engineers, raise the technical bar, and foster a culture of scientific rigor and rapid experimentation.

A day in the life
Amazon offers a full range of benefits that support you and eligible family members, including domestic partners. Benefits can vary by location, the number of regularly scheduled hours you work, length of employment, and job status such as seasonal or temporary employment. The benefits that generally apply to regular, full-time employees include:
1. Medical, Dental, and Vision Coverage
2. Maternity and Parental Leave Options
3. Paid Time Off (PTO)
4. 401(k) Plan

If you are not sure that every qualification on the list above describes you exactly, we'd still love to hear from you! At Amazon, we value people with unique backgrounds, experiences, and skillsets. If you’re passionate about this role and want to make an impact on a global scale, please apply!

Basic qualifications

- PhD, or Master's degree and 6+ years of applied research experience
- Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language

Preferred qualifications

- Experience with modeling tools such as R, scikit-learn, Spark MLLib, MxNet, Tensorflow, numpy, scipy etc.
- Experience with large scale distributed systems such as Hadoop, Spark etc.

title: Robotics Applied Scientist
descriptionHtml:
Amazon is seeking exceptional talent to help develop the next generation of advanced robotics systems that will transform automation at Amazon's scale. We're building robotic systems that combine frontier AI, sophisticated control, and advanced mechanical design to create adaptable automation capable of working safely alongside humans in dynamic environments. This is an opportunity to shape the future of robotics and automation at an unprecedented scale, working with world-class teams pushing the boundaries of what's possible in robotic manipulation, locomotion, and human-robot interaction.

We are seeking an Applied Scientist to develop tactile- and force-driven manipulation policies for highly dexterous, multi-fingered robotic hands and grippers. In this role you will research and build policy learning algorithms that enable robotic hands to perform grasping and in-hand manipulation in unstructured, real-world environments, using touch and force feedback as first-class signals rather than afterthoughts. Much of this work is grounded in reinforcement learning.

To be successful you need to be highly motivated, dive deep, and deliver to the highest standards. You will demonstrate strong working knowledge of modern policy learning methods, with expertise in taking algorithms from simulation onto real hardware. That means being comfortable working against real physical constraints and treating sim-to-real as a core research problem rather than optimizing for benchmark numbers alone. You will work across tactile signal processing, contact-rich manipulation, sim-to-real transfer, and multi-modal sensor fusion to build robust solutions for autonomous grasping, dexterous re-orientation, and fine motor control. You will bring the desire to learn from new challenges, and the problem-solving and communication skills to work within a highly interactive and experienced team.

Key job responsibilities
- Design and train manipulation policies that leverage tactile and force feedback for dexterous grasping, in-hand manipulation, and contact-rich tasks, using reinforcement learning, imitation learning, or hybrid approaches.
- Drive sim-to-real transfer, closing the gap between simulated and physical performance on real robotic hands.
- Shape objectives and control strategies with the hardware in mind, accounting for how motors and actuators actually behave: transmission ratios, torque versus power, backdrivability, and thermal limits.
- Build simulation-based and on-robot evaluation frameworks, with benchmarks and metrics that make tactile perception and policy performance systematically comparable across iterations.
- Own scientific and technical projects within the tactile sensing and manipulation workstreams, driving from research concept through deployment on physical robotic systems — and, at the senior level, set direction across a workstream.
- Collaborate with hardware, mechanical design, firmware, and controls teams — and with partner applied science organizations — to translate research advances into deployable robotic capabilities, and to inform sensor and actuator design decisions with policy-level requirements.
- Publish at top-tier venues and build collaborations with the external research community.
- Contribute to a strong scientific bar on the team through code and design review, and mentor engineers and interns working on real-world manipulation and sensing problems.

A day in the life
Your morning might start with a standup alongside hardware and controls engineers reviewing overnight sim-to-real training runs on a multi-finger gripper, debugging why a grasp policy that worked in simulation is slipping on a real sensor array. Mid-morning you join the weekly tactile sensing workstream to align on sensor integration milestones and share early results from a contact-state estimator you have been prototyping. After lunch you spend a focused block iterating on a reinforcement learning reward formulation, testing variations in simulation before queuing runs on the cluster. Later you pair with a mechanical engineer to review sensor placement trade-offs on an upcoming gripper revision, then wrap the day by drafting a short experiment write-up and sketching next steps for a conference submission.

No two days look exactly the same: one week you may be collecting teleoperated demonstrations on the physical robot to seed an imitation learning pipeline; the next you could be deep in a codebase refactor to support a new tactile modality. Throughout, you balance hands-on research — writing algorithms, running experiments, analyzing data — with cross-team collaboration and mentoring. The common thread is moving from research insight to working capability on real hardware, with a tight feedback loop between simulation and the physical world.

About the team
Our is developing next-generation manipulation capabilities for highly dexterous multi-fingered grippers and hands. Our work spans tactile sensor development, manipulation policy learning, and the tight integration of sensing hardware with intelligent control software. We are building systems that can feel, adapt, and manipulate with human-level dexterity.

You will join a team working at the frontier of tactile sensing and contact-rich manipulation, helping define how robots perceive and interact with objects through touch. Because we build the hands as well as the policies that drive them, you will have a direct line to the sensor, actuator, and mechanism designs your algorithms depend on — and real influence over how they evolve. This is an opportunity to solve hard problems across perception, learning, and physical interaction alongside a team of scientists and engineers building toward real-world deployment.

Basic qualifications

- Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language
- Research or applied experience in one or more of: tactile sensing, manipulation policy learning, contact-rich manipulation, dexterous grasping, or multi-modal perception for robotics
- Experience deploying learned policies or control algorithms on physical robotic hardware

Preferred qualifications

- Experience leading technical initiatives and key deliverables
- Experience bridging research with practical engineering implementation in physical robotic systems
- Hands-on experience with modern tactile sensing hardware and tactile signal processing
- Strong publication record at major robotics/ML venues (e.g., RSS, CoRL, ICRA, IROS, NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR), including impactful first-author work in tactile sensing or dexterous manipulation
- Experience developing manipulation policies using reinforcement learning, imitation learning, or foundation models for contact-rich tasks
- Demonstrated experience with sim-to-real transfer for tactile-enabled manipulation
- Familiarity with both learned and classical approaches to contact dynamics, including impedance and admittance control
- Experience with force and torque control, and with proprioceptive force estimation on torque- or current-controlled actuators
- Experience with robotics simulation stacks (e.g., Isaac, MuJoCo) and robot modeling (URDF)
- Experience with teleoperation and demonstration-collection pipelines for dexterous hands
- Familiarity with multi-finger or multi-contact gripper platforms

title: Operations Supervisor, ATS
descriptionHtml:
Las operaciones son la esencia de todo lo que hacemos en Amazon. Los artículos se procesan y envían a tiempo a nuestros clientes gracias a la eficacia de las operaciones. Ser supervisor/a de operaciones te da la oportunidad de ver cómo funcionan sus distintas etapas y de intervenir para que todo vaya sobre ruedas.

Serás la primera persona de contacto para los miembros del equipo durante su turno y les ayudarás a seguir los procesos establecidos por tus superiores. Se trata de un puesto muy práctico, que te aportará experiencia en el uso de las herramientas y los sistemas que garantizan el éxito de nuestras operaciones.

Para esta posición es necesario tener disponibilidad para trabajar en turnos rotativos que pueden incluir fines de semanas y noches.

- Medir y supervisar los flujos de trabajo, controlar la productividad en el centro y proporcionar información clave sobre los turnos a los/las responsables de primera línea para garantizar la excelencia operativa.
- Brindar apoyo y formar al personal para que pueda prestar un gran servicio y supervisarlo en sus tareas diarias.

- Colaborar con otros departamentos en la búsqueda de soluciones a problemas comunes o garantizar el rendimiento en áreas clave.
- Identificar formas de optimizar la seguridad, la calidad y la productividad mediante el análisis de datos.

A day in the life
Como supervisor/a de operaciones tu sitio estará en uno de nuestros centros operativos. Ayudarás a tu responsable de turno/área a ejecutar el plan establecido para cada turno. Para ello, desempeñarás un papel fundamental en las reuniones de equipo celebradas antes de cada turno y supervisarás los procedimientos para asegurarte de que todo el mundo sigue las normas de seguridad, los procesos de calidad y el plan de prioridades de cada día.
Si detectas algún problema, se lo comunicarás a tu superior, pero a veces serás la persona más veterana del turno y el encargado de dar a los demás las instrucciones necesarias para que realicen sus tareas. En otras ocasiones, ayudarás a tu responsable de área a organizar los turnos para garantizar una cobertura de personal suficiente durante las horas punta.

Sin nuestro equipo de transporte Amazon Transportation Service (ATS), no podríamos garantizar entregas tan rápidas. Al incorporarte a ATS, formarás parte de un equipo diverso que desempeña una labor fundamental para el éxito de la empresa. Nuestro equipo recopila datos, que utiliza para tomar decisiones. Algo fundamental para hacer de Amazon una empresa más innovadora y eficiente.

Priorizamos la seguridad ante todo, ya que nuestra gente es lo primero. Además, aprovechamos la experiencia de nuestro personal para que los paquetes lleguen a su destino de forma rápida, cómoda y sostenible.

title: Data Center Controls Engineer, Data Center Capacity Delivery - Controls
descriptionHtml:
Are you passionate about keeping critical infrastructure running at massive scale? As a Data Center Controls Engineer on the global controls team, you will troubleshoot complex issues, manage projects, and maintain the building management system (BMS) and electrical power monitoring system (EPMS) that govern the mechanical and electrical systems powering Amazon data centers. You will develop new processes and standards while finding creative ways to improve controls across a rich ecosystem of generators, uninterruptible power supplies, switchgear, power distribution units, variable frequency drives, transfer switches, chillers, pumps, cooling towers, heat exchangers, and air handling units. These components interact through open and proprietary communications protocols, and you will be at the center of ensuring they operate reliably and efficiently.

Key job responsibilities
- Design, configure, validate, commission, and maintain BMS and EPMS systems while training internal stakeholders on their operation and best practices.
- Plan and execute BMS and EPMS improvement projects end-to-end, defining scope, schedule, budget, and coordinating with partner teams and vendors to deliver on time.
- Troubleshoot high-complexity controls issues, review and iterate on sequences of operation, and develop or modify controls logic programming and graphical user interfaces.
- Serve as a technical escalation point for in-service data centers, participating in the global on-call rotation and guiding less experienced engineers through risk mitigation during emergent situations.
- Develop risk assessments and operational dashboards, review quarterly maintenance results, and drive corrective actions to continuously improve equipment reliability.

A day in the life
Your morning may start with a review of overnight BMS alerts and coordination with the on-call team to prioritize open items. From there, you could be on-site at a data center validating a controls sequence change alongside a vendor, then shifting to a project planning session where you scope an EPMS upgrade with partner engineering teams. Preferred qualifications

- Demonstrated understanding of engineering documentation, electrical and mechanical diagrams, and standard operating procedures.
- Ability to manage multiple stakeholder deliverables, requirements, and navigate difficult situations.

Amazon Ads Support Products & Services is looking for a skilled Instructional Designer/Curriculum Developer with a track record of success in supporting ad agencies. You'll work with a highly collaborative team of learning and performance professionals to build the skills of our programmatic support specialists and managers.

This is a great opportunity to support a growing team with your talents as a programmatic advertising expert, instructional designer, and communicator. You'll be responsible for the full lifecycle of learning, from needs analysis through reporting of outcomes to senior leadership. You'll lead training with teams globally, helping to scale the knowledge across the team and drive better outcomes for advertising customers.

Our team is committed to creating dynamic, engaging, effective learning content that scales and generates results—while having fun and learning from each other.


Key job responsibilities
* Work backwards from agency customer and with business stakeholders to identify needs for training and upskilling
* Design innovative learning solutions that focus on behavioral outcomes
* Develop sophisticated learning content using advanced multimedia tools
* Proactively identify performance gaps and propose learning interventions
* Share expertise in programmatic advertising, eLearning and Instructional Design with more junior team members

About the team
Support Products & Services provides robust customer services for advertisers ranging from small business owners to deeply experienced traders at large global ad agencies. Our associates must be able to not just resolve day-to-day issues, but also see around corners to provide strategic advice to ensure our advertisers get the most impact from their marketing budgets.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree
- Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
- 8+ years of professional experience at a media agency or in-house advertising team
- 2+ years of programmatic advertising experience (in any capacity)
- Experience designing learning solutions that focus on behavioral outcomes

Preferred qualifications

- Experience leading creative development of innovative creative from concept to delivery
- Experience managing multiple projects and meeting aggressive deadlines
- Experience with eLearning authoring tools and other design programs including: Storyline/Rise 360, Vyond, Adobe Creative Suite, and Camtasia
- Experience with Learning Management Systems (LMS), or experience with multimedia content creation

title: Data Center Infrastructure Delivery Manager
descriptionHtml:
Transform the backbone of digital infrastructure by leading a dynamic team that builds and maintains the critical networks powering global technology. In this role, you'll drive operational excellence, optimize data center deployment strategies, and create seamless connectivity solutions that support Amazon's massive technological ecosystem.

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we're the people who keep the clouds running. We support all AWS data centers and all the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we're looking for talented people who want to help.

You'll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You'll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you'll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Key job responsibilities
The ideal candidate will possess a technology background that enables them to understand the complexities of the sophisticated network architecture of Amazon data centers. To be a qualified candidate for this role you must have experience operating in large-scale data center or a background in telecom networks and display a demonstrated ability to think broadly and strategically, as this is needed to align the future of Infrastructure Delivery with the larger objectives of the business.
You will be responsible for managing a group of technicians who are installing and building server rack capacity for our customers. You must be passionate about Customer Experience, think and act globally and want to contribute to innovations in Data Center Infrastructure.
Managing and developing teams of technicians and engineers, providing both technical and leadership expertise and ensuring the highest levels of performance.
Delivering capacity to existing Data Centers
Helping build and bring online new Data Centers
Constantly improving all our processes and procedures. We believe there is nothing we cannot improve
Assisting & managing relationships with external vendors & contractors
Liaising with internal teams & management groups
Ensuring we adhere to and exceed local Health & Safety standards in all our Data Centers
Creating and maintaining metrics on all aspects of our Data Centers and utilizing those metrics to drive positive changes
Assisting in implementing service methodologies including incident management, problem management, change management, capacity management, etc.
This role supports data centers in various operational stages. The position may be assigned to a facility still under development, which could require travel to established locations for training until your designated site becomes fully operational.

Essential Requirements
Ability to travel to or commute between data center locations as needed
Willingness to temporarily work at alternative sites during training periods or until assigned facility is operational
Travel frequency will vary based on business needs and operational status of assigned facility
Candidates must be able to travel (over 50 miles) or commute (less than 50 miles) to active data center sites as required by business needs.

Basic qualifications

- 2+ years of data center experience, or experience in similar technical or vocational roles
- 2+ years of TCP/IP networking, network cabling, fiber, optic types, and test equipment experience
- 2+ years of management/team lead function experience

Preferred qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in an IT-related field (e.g., Computer Science, Network Engineering), or experience in professional or military IT-related roles
- Knowledge of network hardware and packet forwarding architectures
- certification in a relevant field (CCENT - Cisco Certified Entry Networking Technician, Network+, or CCNA - Cisco Certified Network Associate)
- Work a flexible schedule including weekends, nights, and holidays
- Experience conducting behavioral interviews and hiring

title: Construction Manager , AMER SE
descriptionHtml:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we're the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we're looking for talented people who want to help.

You'll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You'll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you'll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

As a Data Center Construction Manager, you will be part of a creative, diverse team tasked with solving fascinating problems in constructing Amazon Data Centers. Our data centers are industry-leading examples of energy-efficient, cost-effective designs. You will work alongside partner teams such as Operations, Networking, Controls, Security, and Commissioning to build Data Centers that directly support our Customers.

As our Data Center Construction Manager, you will build some of the most interesting electrical and mechanical systems in the world. You will be on the construction site daily, interacting with the construction trades as Amazon's owner's representative. You will be directly responsible for driving cost, schedule, and quality while managing construction vendors and contractors building data centers.

At Amazon, we are all Owners and leverage unique opportunities presented to us by owning everything from design review to construction bidding to construction execution and final hand-off to our customers. We are a diverse, upbeat, creative team of engineers and managers working daily to develop innovative data centers for our Customers.

Key job responsibilities
The Data Center Construction Manager will be responsible for construction project management and oversight of construction-related activities as they relate to new builds or general capital projects. This includes ownership of the project scope, quality, schedule, and budget.

Some of the typical daily tasks of the Construction Manager:

-Direct interface with construction general contractors during the bidding, award, execution, and project closeout/punch list phases.

-Conduct negotiations with general contractors and evaluate bids/proposals with detail and accuracy.

-Create construction project scope and requests for proposals.

-Perform financial analysis of construction.

-Manage construction projects for specific initiatives aimed at increasing the resiliency of our data centers.

-Conduct constructability reviews of electrical and mechanical designs associated with the construction of new data centers or optimization of existing data centers.

-Manage construction documents including submittal review, RFIs, change orders, and invoicing.

-Ensure construction project quality control.
Record and report key construction metrics to team members and management.

-Drive teams to perform troubleshooting and root-cause failure analysis associated with equipment failures.

-Be a leader within the group as well as within internal and external teams that support the data center.

A day in the life
**Why AWS**
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

*Diverse Experiences*
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

*Work/Life Balance*
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

*Inclusive Team Culture*
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (gender diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

*Mentorship and Career Growth*
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

- Experience carrying new design concepts through exploration, development, and into deployment or mass production

descriptionHtml:

title: Senior Product Designer, Kiro
descriptionHtml:
Agentic development is redefining how software gets built, and Kiro is at the center of it. Kiro is an agentic AI from AWS that turns prompts into structured requirements, designs, and sequenced tasks, then implements them with parallel agents that verify correctness. It's available as a desktop IDE, a CLI, a web app, a mobile app, and Kiro Crew (an open-source persistent development workspace), all powered by one unified agent harness.

We're looking for a Senior UX Designer to help shape this experience. You'll initially focus on Kiro IDE, a surface with distinct design challenges and significant room to define the experience. You'll build deep understanding of the developer audience while leading hands-on design work: concept framing, interaction patterns, and shipping real improvements that inform longer-term product direction.

The design challenges here are unlike traditional developer tools: How should a developer setup their agentic workflows? How do we improve spec-driven development? How do you build trust in AI that writes and validates code on your behalf?

You excel in the early, ambiguous stages of design: concept modeling, ecosystem mapping, user story development, and framing the experience before pixels are ever pushed. You know how to set up a problem space so that the right solutions emerge. You are equally strong in execution, iterating rapidly and prototyping in whatever tool fits the moment. You adapt your approach based on the problem, the timeline, and the team. We value designers who bring their own perspective and working style. What matters is the quality of thinking and the impact of the outcome, not conformity to a single methodology.

You will collaborate with product teams, engineering teams, and executive leadership to identify and execute on opportunities, serving as the voice of the developer with senior leadership.

If you want your design work to shape how millions of developers build software with AI, we'd love to hear from you.

Key job responsibilities
- Go deep on audience understanding: conduct and synthesize research to build rich mental models of how developers think, work, and adopt agentic tools
- Lead concept design and early-stage framing: ecosystem maps, concept models, user stories, journey frameworks, and experience principles that set the foundation for product direction
- Own and drive the end-to-end design process for major features
- Shape the UX of agentic workflows including spec-driven development, autonomous mode, parallel agents, hooks, and correctness verification
- Iterate rapidly and prototype at the right fidelity, from paper sketches and concept storyboards to high-fidelity interactive prototypes, choosing the right tools and methods for each challenge
- Partner with product management and engineering to influence strategy through strong design rationale and customer advocacy
- Mentor junior designers and define scalable design patterns that raise the bar across the team

About the team
You'll join a team of designers and researchers embedded directly in the Kiro product organization. We sit alongside product and engineering as one team, which means design has a seat at the table from strategy through shipping. We have dedicated UX research support and work in close collaboration with our researchers, so design decisions are grounded in real customer insight, not assumptions.

Our team covers the full Kiro product suite: IDE, CLI, Web, Mobile, Kiro Crew, the Kiro agent, and platform capabilities. We support each other's growth, share work openly, and believe that the best design comes from people who bring diverse perspectives and their own way of working. If you thrive in an environment where you have real ownership, close partnership with research, and the autonomy to choose how you approach a problem, you'll feel at home here.

Basic qualifications

title: Data Center IT Support Manager, Rack Lifecycle Team
descriptionHtml:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

We are looking for a hands-on, operationally focused Rack Lifecycle Team Manager to join our Infrastructure Operations team, owning the day-to-day execution of rack lifecycle operations within data center sites. This role is responsible for the full continuum of rack operations — from demand intake and rack landing, through Late Binding cabling, rack installation and handoff, to end-of-life decommissioning — at the site level.

You will lead a team of data center technicians, translating organizational capacity goals into executed deliverables on the floor. As a tactical leader, you are the single accountable owner for ensuring every rack needed for customer capacity lands on time, is cabled and installed to standard, has no install blockers at handoff, and is decommissioned safely and compliantly at end-of-life.

Your work directly supports AWS's ability to deliver infrastructure capacity to customers reliably and at the lowest possible cost, while maintaining the highest standards of safety, security, and environmental compliance.


Key job responsibilities
Rack Delivery & Installation
- Lead planning and execution of network deployments including rack installs, structured cabling, fiber trunks, and MMR/CFA builds to meet committed customer capacity dates
- Coordinate site readiness, RSPC readiness (Rack Space Power Cooling); ensure racks are landed, cabled, and ready for cabling patching and install per standards
- Proactively identify and drive resolution of blockers across permits, site access, facilities, power, cross-connects, and vendor dependencies
- Drive cross-team coordination with DCO, DCEO, LOG, security, CDP, Supply chain, Transport and GND during deployment waves, running escalation touchpoints and daily stand-ups as needed
- Ensuring rack installations are as per MOP/SOP and documenting the handovers for later refences and improvements

Cabling Infrastructure (Late Binding)
- Own scope for fiber/copper cabling, patching schedules, and labeling standards for the site
- Validate OTDR/power testing and as-built documentation; ensure cabling meets quality standards and capacity requirements before handoff
- Maintain cabling infrastructure governance including CMDB accuracy and port map integrity post-installation
- Identify systemic cabling quality gaps and implement corrective actions to improve cycle times and first-pass quality

Supply Chain & Logistics
- Track rack, cable, optics, and network BOM from PO to site; monitor lead times, logistics, customs clearance, and site inventory levels
- Flag supply chain risks to schedule early and coordinate with procurement, logistics, and vendor partners on mitigation plans
- Ensure material availability aligns with deployment timelines; maintain site-level inventory accuracy

Stakeholder Management & Blocker Removal
- Serve as the single point of contact for internal customers, DC Ops, facilities, transport, and vendors for site-level rack lifecycle activities
- Run daily and weekly war rooms during deployment waves; provide timely status updates and escalate blockers to senior leadership as needed
- Build effective working relationships with cross-functional partners to ensure alignment and uninterrupted delivery execution

Rack Decommissioning (Decom)
- Own the site-level decommission pipeline for EOL racks; coordinate with Capacity Planning, Network Operations, and DCLM/ALM teams to schedule graceful shutdowns with zero service impact
- Lead physical decommission activities — device wipe, media destruction, cable removal, power disconnect, asset de-tagging, and rack removal — ensuring full MOP and EHS compliance
- Track and recover reusable assets (optics, cables, PDUs, hardware); coordinate RMA, liquidation, or secure disposal per AWS Reverse Logistics and Environmental policies
- Validate that reclaimed power, cooling, and U-space is accurately returned to the available pool; drive re-use to defer new builds and improve TCO
- Ensure data hygiene post-decom including DCIM/CMDB updates, IPAM releases, port map reconciliation, and circuit/cross-connect documentation

Governance, Metrics & Reporting
- Track and report on site-level KPIs including: racks landed vs. plan, Late Binding cabling completion %, capacity ready dates, received vs. installed cycle time, decom backlog vs. flightpath goal, and shipment achievement %
- Define and enforce site-level policies, SOPs, and governance frameworks aligned with AWS standards and industry best practices across all rack lifecycle phases
- Provide accurate, data-driven reporting on delivery performance, blockers, and improvement initiatives to the Cluster Manager and senior leadership
- Champion adoption of tooling (e.g., Boost, MARS, ALM/DCLM) to reduce manual effort, improve data accuracy, and accelerate delivery cycle times

Handover & Documentation
- Ensure clean, documented handoffs to Data Center Operations teams with updated CMDB/DCIM records, port maps, test results, and completed workflow sign-offs — with zero blockers at handoff
- Maintain accurate and current records in DCIM/CMDB, IPAM, and related systems throughout all lifecycle phases
- Ensure all as-built documentation, cabling records, and workflow completions are captured and auditable
Team Leadership & Operations Management
- Lead, coach, and develop a team of data center technicians; manage staffing, scheduling, and day-to-day workforce planning for the site
- Conduct regular team meetings, drive performance accountability, and ensure appropriate training and skill development across all lifecycle functions
- Translate organizational goals into actionable team objectives; manage sprint planning, team output quality, and SLA compliance
- Participate in recruiting, onboarding, and performance management; make staffing recommendations in partnership with manager and HR
- Foster a high-performance, inclusive, and safety-first team culture

A day in the life
As the Rack Lifecycle Team Manager for your site, no two days are the same.
You might start your morning reviewing the site's daily rack landing dashboard, checking in with your technicians on an active cabling wave, and triaging a supply chain delay flagged overnight. By midday, you could be on the data center floor coordinating a rack placement with facilities, validating a power sign-off checklist before a network device install, or running a decom stand-up to confirm MOP readiness for an EOL rack removal. In the afternoon, you might be updating CMDB records following a completed handoff, reviewing your team's KPI performance ahead of a weekly operations review, or coaching a technician on structured cabling standards.

Your role is tactical and hands-on — you execute with your team, remove blockers in real time, and hold the line on quality and schedule at the site level.

About the team
Why AWS
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

Inclusive Team Culture
AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.

Mentorship and Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

- 3+ years of direct people management, including managing managers or senior individual contributors experience
- 3+ years of data center engineering or operations experience

Preferred qualifications

- 2+ years of data center, critical environment, computer hardware repair, infrastructure cabling, network deployment, or data center operations experience, or experience working in a data center environment (racking and stacking gear, cable management, hot/cold aisle containment)
- 2+ years of network cabling, fiber optics, and test equipment including VFL, power meter, and OTDR experience, or experience related IT

title: Supply Planning Manager, Technology Materials Planning
descriptionHtml:
Amazon's technology supply chain supports a complex and rapidly evolving portfolio of infrastructure, end-user equipment, and technology products across thousands of locations globally. As the business scales, disciplined and responsive supply planning is critical to ensuring material availability, managing inventory investment, optimizing procurement execution, enabling network efficiency, and delivering predictable outcomes for customers.

We are seeking a Manager, Supply Planning to lead the supply planning capability within Supply Chain Planning. This leader will manage a team responsible for developing and continuously improving supply plans across the existing customer business segments, while establishing scalable mechanisms that can support new businesses, products, and fulfillment models.

The successful candidate will build a supply planning organization that combines strong planning fundamentals with data, technology, and automation. This includes improving material requirement plan quality, integrating demand signals with supply constraints and lead times, optimizing network topology through hub-and-spoke and regional distribution strategies, identifying structural sources of supply risk and excess inventory, and partnering with Product, Data, Analytics, and Technology teams to reduce manual planning activity and enable increasingly intelligent supply planning capabilities.

The ideal candidate combines strong supply chain expertise, analytical depth, customer orientation, business judgment, and people leadership. They must be comfortable challenging assumptions, navigating incomplete or conflicting signals, and influencing stakeholders across Supply Chain, Finance, Technology, Operations, Procurement, and customer organizations.

Key job responsibilities
• Lead, coach, and develop a team responsible for supply planning across Launch, KTLO, and Programs.
• Own the end-to-end supply planning mechanism, including material requirement plan (MRP) creation and execution, order management, inventory performance measurement, and continuous improvement.
• Translate demand plans, supply constraints, lead times, funding availability, and inventory positions into executable material requirement plans at the appropriate product, geographic, and time horizons.
• Establish clear accountability for supply inputs and challenge assumptions, overrides, and changes that are not supported by measurable business signals or supply data.
• Define and improve supply availability, inventory health, Days of Cover, excess and obsolescence, order accuracy, and other metrics that distinguish true supply variability from process, data, and system defects.
• Lead capacity planning efforts to ensure supplier and network capacity aligns with demand forecasts, proactively identifying and mitigating capacity constraints across the planning horizon.
• Design and optimize hub-and-spoke distribution and network topology strategies to improve fulfillment speed, reduce transportation costs, and support regional inventory positioning across global sites.
• Partner with Demand Planning and Enterprise S&OP to incorporate demand uncertainty, quantify supply risks, and support scenario and trade-off decisions.
• Develop segmented planning approaches appropriate for different supply patterns, including new site launches, steady-state replenishment, and program-driven procurement, incorporating network optimization principles to determine optimal stocking locations and replenishment flows.
• Partner with Product, Data, Analytics, and Technology teams to automate material requirement plan generation, order validation, exception management, and planner workflows.
• Advance the use of optimization models, machine learning, and AI to improve supply plan quality and reduce dependence on manual reconciliation and judgment.
• Simplify fragmented supply processes and data sources, with a long-term goal of connecting Planning more directly to real-time inventory positions, supplier capacity, network capacity utilization, and procurement execution.
• Build scalable mechanisms that support new products, businesses, regions, and planning paradigms without creating parallel planning processes.
• Communicate supply outlook, inventory risks, capacity constraints, network optimization opportunities, funding gaps, procurement constraints, and recommended actions clearly to senior stakeholders.


A day in the life
In this role, you may begin the day reviewing inventory positions and open order status with your team, determining whether a supply gap reflects a true constraint or a defect in the underlying data or process. You may evaluate hub capacity utilization and assess whether regional inventory positioning is aligned with current demand patterns.

You may work with Demand Planning to understand the implications of a forecast change on the material requirement plan, partner with Procurement to resolve a supplier lead time or capacity issue, or support Enterprise S&OP with scenarios where supply constraints, network bottlenecks, or funding gaps require a broader business decision.

You may also spend time with Product or Technology teams improving how material requirement plans are generated, automating a repetitive planner workflow, optimizing network flows across hub-and-spoke distribution points, or defining how optimization models and AI can augment planner judgment.

The role balances near-term supply performance with the longer-term objective of creating a scalable, technology-enabled supply planning capability where planners spend less time collecting and reconciling information and more time managing supply risk, optimizing network and inventory investment, and improving the quality of the plan.

Basic qualifications

- Experience working cross functionally with tech and non-tech teams
- Experience in team management
- Experience in cross functional project delivery
- Experience in program or project management
- Experience in supply chain
- Experience defining program requirements and using data and metrics to determine improvements

Preferred qualifications

- Experience managing, analyzing and communicating results to senior leadership

descriptionHtml:
Sr. Inventory and Asset Management role is responsible for leading the development, implementation, and sustainability of an innovative and scalable AR-wide inventory management framework. This role involves collaborating closely with internal supply chain teams, external partner teams (Deployment, Field IT, RME, and Shared Services), and SC supported customer business units (AMZL, ATS, GCF, and GSF) to ensure alignment and successful execution across all stakeholders. They lead the strategic development and deployment of a system-driven inventory audit and cycle count process across a network of over 5,000 sites. A key component of this framework is the implementation and maintenance of data-driven inventory thresholds for more than 12,000 distinct IT products, managing $950MM inventory across 5000+ sites and approximately $600 MM inventory across 13 Rapid Asset Deployment (RAD) centers. Leveraging their analytical expertise, they integrate diverse, multifaceted data sources such as item-specific site-type Bill of Materials (BOM), operational criticality, cost, lead time, and historical demand patterns (including ad-hoc, peak/prime, and ARMA) to drive the dynamic ABC classification across IT product catalogue and define their optimal threshold levels across IT hubs and RAD centers. The role also leads the strategic management of inventory levels for Amazon-owned inventory stored at RADs, VARs, and 3PLs along-side the Field IT Hubs. It involves establishing and executing a standardized process to systematically reduce excess and obsolete (E&O) inventory, valued at over $50+ MM across the Field IT Hubs along-with the implementation of robust controls to ensure the available inventory across the network is effectively leveraged and consumed in accordance with the established policies. In pursuit of cost optimization for Amazon, the role entails the critical task of repurposing, returning, or reselling inventory, guided by stringent eligibility criteria established within the inventory management framework and in alignment with contractual obligations delineated in VAR/OEM agreements. They build and define the business-essential tier-1 and tier-2 inventory and asset metrics which include Optimal Inventory Thresholds (inventory health), Inventory Accuracy Percentage, Asset Shrinkage Percentage, Inventory Availability (Days of Cover), Aged Inventory (slow-moving), Net Book Value reporting, and Excess/Obsolete Inventory as a percentage of total inventory. These metrics determine and advise SC partners and customers on optimal ordering timing for 2.9MM infrastructure and 14.9MM end-user equipment, ensuring orders are placed under lead times, create funding predictions, inventory requirements/rebalancing in the network to support 30+ demand streams encompassing 350+ new site launches, 18+ customer programs, and 27+ lifecycle initiatives, enabling SC to provide an insight-based & data-driven service to customers to operate their business

- 5+ years of supply chain experience

- Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership

Preferred qualifications

title: Sr Data Center IT Specialist , Data Center Infrastructure Delivery
descriptionHtml:
At AWS, we are working to be the most customer-centric company on earth. To get there, we need exceptionally bright, talented, and driven people. If you would like to help us build, this is your chance to make history.

The Infrastructure Delivery team is responsible for the scaling and physical deployment of new Data Center Infrastructure. We are looking for a motivated and enthusiastic trainee to join the growing team. The ideal candidate is highly motivated individual with a willingness to learn and upskill. The candidate must be able to perform repetitive tasks and adhere to standard processes and best practices. The successful candidate will be working in a team environment and must be able to communicate and promote cross-team functionality.
This position has a physical component and may require working in cramped spaces or elevated locations.

Key job responsibilities
- Adhere to security and safety best practices in the Data Center.
- Installation and testing of copper and Fiber Optic cabling.
- Basic build and troubleshooting of network devices.
- Creating/attaching labels and barcodes.
- Regularly work at heights and from ladders/EWP
- Managing inventory of related materials.
- Adhering to defined escalation processes and standard operating procedures.
- Work in noisy areas with hotter and colder temperatures than standard office environmental conditions.
- Ability to travel within geographical work area is required, some travel outside traditional work area may be requested.
- Understanding of cabling procedure.

Physical requirements
- Regularly lift or move up to 18 kg (about 40 lb), and participate in group lifts for heavier loads
- Work in cramped, elevated, or noisy environments, including regular work at heights and from ladders
- Bending, lifting, stretching, reaching, standing, and walking for 8 or more hours a day
- Ascend and descend ladders, stairs, and gangways safely and without limitation
- Ability to work in a 24/7 environment, participating in the primary response rotation and providing after-hours support as needed
- Valid Australian driver's license and ability to travel between MEL data center sites as required

A day in the life
A normal day involve working inside a Data Center installing network equipment and cables, managing vendors, and negotiating deadlines with program managers. You will be responsible for running multiple projects at the same time

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. - 2+ years of Computer Hardware Repair, Infrastructure Cabling, Network Deployment, or Data Center Operations experience, or experience in similar technical or vocational roles

- Working knowledge of structured cabling and port-allocation processes
- Ability to lead installs and guide less-experienced technicians

- Experience with cabling infrastructure best practices and methodologies
- Knowledge of network design, protocols and Layer 1/2 troubleshooting
- Project management skills, including planning, coordinating, and tracking concurrent installs through to delivery

- Certificate IV or Diploma in a relevant field (networking, IT, electrotechnology) or equivalent experience
