title: Healthcare Strategic Lead, UK Public Sector Healthcare
descriptionHtml:
AWS is seeking an experienced healthcare technology leader to drive long-term proposition development for the NHS. This is not a traditional sales role — it is a strategic, outward-facing position that combines deep NHS domain expertise with the ability to shape and architect cloud-enabled solutions that address the systemic challenges facing the health service.

You will act as the bridge between NHS clinical/operational reality and AWS's technology capabilities — translating policy intent into deliverable cloud propositions, working 12–36 months ahead of procurement cycles to shape demand, and ensuring AWS is positioned as the strategic platform of choice when buying decisions crystallise.

This role is ideal for someone with a CTO, CDIO, or senior digital leadership background in the NHS who wants to apply that expertise at national scale — shaping propositions that will transform care delivery across the system.

Key job responsibilities
1/ Develop and own long-term (2–5 year) cloud propositions aligned to NHS strategic priorities
2/ Translate NHS policy (10-Year Health Plan, NHSE mandates, ICS strategies) into actionable AWS account plans
3/ Engage at CIO, CDIO, CCIO, and Medical Director level as a credible peer — understanding clinical workflows, operational pressures, and governance constraints from first-hand experience
4/ Shape NHS procurement criteria and architecture standards ahead of formal tender processes
5/ Lead proposition development for complex, multi-stakeholder initiatives
6/ Work with AWS Solutions Architects, Partner teams, and ISVs to build reference architectures, business cases, and proof-of-concept designs
7/ Represent AWS at national policy forums, NHS boards, and industry bodies — contributing thought leadership on cloud-enabled health system transformation
8/ Advise the AWS UK Healthcare leadership team on NHS strategic direction, emerging opportunities, and competitive positioning
Build relationships across the NHS ecosystem: NHSE, DHSC, ICSs, NHS Trusts, Royal Colleges and regulators

A day in the life
No two days in this role are the same. On any given day, you might start the morning preparing a cloud business case for a Trust CFO and spend the afternoon on-site with a CDIO walking through their digital roadmap.

You'll balance strategic account planning with tactical deal execution — one moment you're working with a Trust's to shape their infrastructure strategy, the next you're navigating a procurement framework. You'll join internal working sessions with Solutions Architects to design a resilient architecture for a clinical workload, then brief your leadership on pipeline progress.

You'll attend NHS industry events and ICS board meetings and host innovation days that bring clinicians face-to-face with AI and data tools. Some weeks you'll be deep in a complex multi-stakeholder procurement; others you'll be running a proof-of-concept that demonstrates measurable productivity gains.

What stays constant: you will be at the centre of the UK's most significant healthcare transformation, working with senior leaders who are making technology decisions that will shape patient care for the next decade. The pace is high, the impact is real, and the team around you is exceptional.

Basic qualifications

- Experience solving problems with technology in the Healthcare/Life Sciences Industry
- Experience working with Data & AI related technologies, including, but not limited to, AI/ML, GenAI, Analytics, Database, and/or Storage
- Experience building strategic relationships with stakeholders, including communicating and collaborating across teams and functions
- Evidence a background of working in or with the NHS on digital transformation projects
- Evidence of engagement across C Suite within NHS

Preferred qualifications

- Experience implementing a cloud-based technology solution, or experience architecting/operating solutions built on AWS
- Experience in C-level NHS leadership or Go-To-Market, Business Development, Sales, or Consulting

title: Software Development Engineer, Alexa Connections
descriptionHtml:
Do you want to shape how people stay connected across calls, text, and email? Alexa Connections is building a trusted communication agent that understands intent, context, and relationships, then acts on a customer's behalf to make every interaction feel natural. As a Software Development Engineer on this team, you'll design and deliver the software systems behind a context-aware assistant that grows more helpful over time. You'll work across the full software development lifecycle — from understanding customer problems, through system design and implementation, to deployment and operations — building privacy-first solutions that serve tens of millions of daily communication events.

Key job responsibilities
- Design and implement software services that model each customer's personal connections graph, a privacy-first representation of relationships and communication patterns used to power context-aware assistance.
- Build and operate scalable backend systems that integrate large language models and agentic reasoning to anticipate who, when, and how a customer wants to connect across calls, text, and email.
- Collaborate with scientists, product managers, and peer engineering teams to translate research advances in personalization and memory into reliable, production-grade features.
- Contribute to the full software development lifecycle — scoping, design, code review, testing, deployment, and operational support — while coaching teammates through constructive code reviews and documentation.
- Identify and resolve root causes of operational issues, and continuously improve system reliability, maintainability, and performance.

A day in the life
Your morning might start with a design review for a new personalization feature, working through tradeoffs in scalability and data privacy with senior engineers and applied scientists. After lunch you could be writing and testing code for a service that ranks a customer's most relevant contacts, then pairing with a teammate on a code review. You'll regularly join standups with product managers and scientists to align on priorities, and you'll rotate through on-call responsibilities to keep the systems you build running smoothly.

About the team
The Alexa Connections team is growing, so you'll join early and help shape its engineering culture from the ground up. You'll work alongside experienced engineers and scientists who are invested in your growth, with mentorship and the chance to own meaningful problems. Our mission is to make communication effortless and trustworthy for customers worldwide, and we're focused on building intelligent, privacy-first systems that redefine how people stay in touch.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- Experience programming with at least one software programming language

Preferred qualifications

- 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
- Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent

descriptionHtml:
Do you want to help shape how the world's most advanced AI models get built? AWS is hiring a Principal Go-To-Market (GTM) Specialist for Amazon FSx for Lustre, the high-performance file system behind some of the most demanding compute workloads on the planet. FSx for Lustre is a core part of the AWS Generative AI strategy. It feeds data to accelerated compute at the speed needed for training, fine-tuning, and inference at scale.

In this role, you will work with frontier model providers, fast-growing AI startups, and global enterprises as they build and scale their AI and HPC infrastructure on AWS. You will set the worldwide GTM strategy for FSx for Lustre and create and run programs, initiatives, research, and enablement at scale for our WW sales, specialist, partner, and cross-functional teams. Your work will directly shape how customers choose AWS as the place to build, train, and deploy AI.

To succeed in this role, you need a proven track record of building and executing GTM and sales programs at scale with measurable results, along with a strong understanding of HPC and AI/ML infrastructure.

In this role, you will be accountable for:

- Setting the WW GTM strategy for FSx for Lustre. Define strategic program direction and oversee execution of insight-driven programs that grow FSx for Lustre adoption and AWS market share with frontier model builders, AI-native startups, and enterprise AI and HPC customers.
- Driving GenAI and HPC workload adoption. Use your business judgment to drive revenue, build sales plays, and find new markets and opportunities across model training, fine-tuning, inference, and traditional HPC workloads such as genomics, EDA, seismic processing, financial simulation, and autonomous vehicle development.
- Working directly with the most demanding customers. Engage with leading AI labs, model providers, and enterprises to understand their performance, scale, and data pipeline needs, and turn them into product feedback, customer wins, and repeatable patterns.
- Partnering across AWS. Work with Compute (accelerated instances and UltraClusters), Amazon SageMaker HyperPod, Amazon EKS, Amazon S3, the Startups and Generative AI teams, industry teams, and service teams to align on joint GTM motions and find the workloads that drive FSx for Lustre growth.
- Mapping technology to business outcomes. Help customers understand how high-performance storage speeds up time to train, improves accelerator utilization, and lowers the total cost of AI and HPC infrastructure.
- Building enablement and evangelizing the platform. - Use excellent written and verbal communication skills to build sales enablement tools, reference architectures, and customer-facing content. -- - Represent FSx for Lustre with customers, partners, analysts, at industry events, and as the primary Executive Briefing Center voice for high-performance storage.
- Building the partner ecosystem. Work with ISVs, system integrators, and AI and HPC partners to create joint solutions and co-sell motions that scale adoption.
- Advising with data. Act as a trusted business advisor. Dive deep into pipeline, consumption, and win/loss data, create high-impact programs, track progress, and adjust to hit goals.

title: Engineering Operation Technician (Night Shift)
descriptionHtml:
Join our dynamic team and become a critical guardian of technological infrastructure! As a Data Center Engineering Technician, you'll play a pivotal role in maintaining the heartbeat of mission-critical technology infrastructure, ensuring seamless operations that power global digital experiences. Your expertise will directly contribute to maintaining an extraordinary 99.999% uptime, keeping the digital world running smoothly and efficiently.

Engineering Technicians are Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment troubleshooting. They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot, Data Center Operation’s Mission Critical Facilities, which includes stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, as well as three phase electrical systems such as: switch gear, UPSs, PDUs, wet cell batteries and associated systems, CRAC, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers/water chemical system, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, & motors.

We are seeking experienced Engineering Operations Technicians to join our data center operations team, specifically focusing on liquid cooling infrastructure and water distribution systems. This role is vital in maintaining the continuous operation of our advanced cooling systems that support critical data center operations.

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

NOTE: Amazon does not sponsor for immigration, including for H-1B, TN, and other non-immigrant visas, for this role.

NOTE: Lump sum stipend will be provided to eligible candidates who relocate for this position.

Key job responsibilities
- Daily building rounds to monitor and record information from electrical, mechanical, and fire/life safety equipment to ensure 24/7 reliability and availability

- Monitor Building Management Systems (BMS) and Electrical Power Management System (EPMS)

- Assist in troubleshooting of facility and rack-level events within internal Service Level Agreements (SLA)

- Perform rack installs and rack decommissioning within internal SLA

- Perform PM, troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and repair of electrical and mechanical equipment

- Technical writing to support change management program

- Monitor daily work requests and manage to resolution, and execute projects from conception to completion

- On-site support of contractors, sub-contractors and vendors, ensuring that all work performed is in accordance with established practices, procedures & local legislation

- Work schedule changes depending on specific site needs. Shifts can be up to 12 hours and may rotate on a predefined schedule. Some locations have on-call rotations.

- Role may support more than one location/site.

Physical Requirements:

- Willingness and demonstrated ability to work in the following physical conditions with reasonable accommodations:

- Regularly lift and/or move up to 39 pounds independently

- Participate in group lifts for 40+ pounds

- Maintain balance and perform construction tasks while on a ladder

- Regularly walk, use hands and fingers, handle or feel, reach with hands and arms, stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl, climb stairs, twist, bend, work above shoulders, grasp, carry, push and pull objects into position

- Work in an environment requiring provided ear protection

- This role supports data centers in various operational stages. The position may be assigned to a facility still under development, which could require travel to established locations for training until your designated site becomes fully operational.

Essential Requirements:

- Ability to travel to or commute between data center locations as needed

- Willingness to temporarily work at alternative sites during training periods or until assigned facility is operational

- Travel frequency will vary based on business needs and operational status of assigned facility

- Candidates must be able to travel (over 50 miles) or commute (less than 50 miles) to active data center sites as required by business needs.

A day in the life
This role acts as Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment preventative maintenance (PM) and troubleshooting, reporting to a site’s Data Center Facility Manager (FM). They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot mission-critical data center facility equipment including stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, 3 phase electrical systems such as switchgear, UPS units, PDUs, and wet cell batteries and associated systems. Mechanical equipment includes CRAHU units, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers, water systems, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, and motors. Additional support equipment is included in the scope of the role which includes fire/life safety equipment, building automation systems, and general facilities equipment.

Basic qualifications

- 2+ years of electrical and mechanical facilities maintenance, or 2+ years of electrical facilities maintenance and 1+ years of mechanical facilities maintenance experience
- 2+ years of Microsoft Office products and applications experience
- Work flexible schedule including weekends, nights, and holidays

Preferred qualifications

- 2+ years of data center engineering experience
- Experience reading and writing procedures, technical documents, and engineering drawings
- vocational/technical training or an associate degree or above, or 4+ years of military experience

About the team
Unser Wartungs- und Instandhaltungsteam (Reliability Maintenance Engineering Team oder RME-Team) sorgt dafür, dass unsere Geräte und Ausstattung jederzeit optimal funktionieren. title: Software Development Engineer II, AFT Sortation, AFT Mansort
descriptionHtml:
Have you ever wondered how Amazon delivers millions of customer orders with exceptional speed and reliability? Behind every fast and on-time delivery is a complex network of software, infrastructure, robotics, and operational processes engineered to work seamlessly at scale.

Amazon Fulfillment Technologies (AFT) builds the software and infrastructure that power Amazon's world-class fulfillment centers. Our systems integrate with warehouse automation, machines, and human associates to orchestrate critical fulfillment processes across a global network. These technologies enable the movement of millions of inventory units and support billions of transactions, ensuring that customers receive the products they want, when they expect them.

About the Mansort Team

The Mansort team owns the manual sortation layer of Amazon's fulfillment network. Our systems determine where packages should be routed after packing and before reaching the outbound dock, enabling accurate and efficient movement of shipments through fulfillment centers.

We build and operate software responsible for sort plan generation, chute and destination assignment, and scan-and-sort workflows used by warehouse associates. Our systems operate on the fulfillment center floor across hundreds of buildings worldwide, where reliability, performance, and correctness directly influence operational efficiency and customer delivery promises.

Mansort operates in a technically demanding environment characterized by high transaction volumes, stringent low-latency requirements, and the need for continuous availability despite connectivity disruptions or upstream dependency failures. Correctness is equally critical: every sortation decision must accurately direct a package to its intended destination to prevent operational errors and missed transportation cutoffs.

Manual sortation complements Amazon's automated sortation capabilities by providing the flexibility and scalability needed to handle peak demand, support new geographies and fulfillment center formats, and accommodate diverse operational requirements that cannot always be addressed through fixed automation.

As Amazon continues to expand its global fulfillment network and introduce new supply chain capabilities, delivery models, and customer experiences, the Mansort team has an opportunity to solve challenging engineering problems, modernize existing systems, and build scalable, resilient solutions that support the future of fulfillment operations.

Key job responsibilities
Design and develop scalable systems by owning the architecture, design, implementation, testing, and deployment of distributed software systems operating in live fulfillment center environments.

Build high-throughput, low-latency services that meet stringent performance, scalability, and availability requirements.

Ensure operational reliability and correctness through robust sortation workflows, data integrity, routing accuracy, fault tolerance, and graceful degradation.

Solve complex business and technical problems using pragmatic engineering decisions, innovative solutions, and modern technologies.

Drive operational excellence by improving observability, monitoring, troubleshooting, and recovery mechanisms to minimize disruptions.

Collaborate with product managers, operations teams, process engineers, and partner engineering teams to improve fulfillment efficiency and customer experience.

Influence technical direction by contributing to architecture, engineering standards, and technical strategy within the team and broader organization.

Maintain high engineering standards by writing clean, maintainable, well-tested code and ensuring software quality, performance, security, and reliability.

Mentor engineers through knowledge sharing, design discussions, code reviews, and technical guidance to strengthen team capabilities.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- Experience programming with at least one software programming language

Preferred qualifications

- 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
- Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent

title: Quality Assurance Engineer II, Amazon Robotics Systems Quality and Performance Engineering
descriptionHtml:
Are you passionate about quality and robotics? Do you thrive on solving complex problems that span hardware, software, and system integration? Amazon Robotics is looking for a Quality Assurance Engineer II to own quality for robotic systems deployed across Amazon's fulfillment network.

In this role, you won't just execute test plans — you'll define them. You'll take ambiguous product requirements and turn them into comprehensive test strategies covering functional, integration, and performance testing. You'll work hands-on with robotic systems on our test floors, validating that releases meet the quality bar before they reach production sites. When you find problems, you won't just file a bug — you'll trace the root cause across system boundaries and give developers the evidence they need to fix it fast.

You'll also build tools and automation that make the whole team more effective — scripting repeatable test scenarios, developing methods to evaluate release quality, and creating documentation that lets teammates run your tests independently. Your work will multiply the impact of everyone around you. You'll collaborate daily with software engineers, hardware engineers, and systems engineers, representing quality in design reviews, release decisions, and cross-team discussions.

This is a hands-on role based at our BOS27 facility in Westborough, MA. If you want to work at the intersection of robotics, quality engineering, and real-world impact, we'd love to hear from you.

Key job responsibilities
Own end-to-end test strategy for robotic features and systems — defining what to test, how to test it, and what infrastructure is needed, even when requirements are ambiguous or evolving.
Create and execute test plans for complex test scenarios including system integration, robotic workcell validation, and safety-critical functionality across hardware, software, and firmware boundaries.
Design and build automated test solutions that are maintainable, reusable, and reliable — enabling other engineers to run and extend them independently.
Develop test strategies for non-functional areas such as performance, reliability, and regression detection to ensure product quality is measured objectively.
Isolate, document, and validate defects with detailed evidence and root-cause analysis, enabling development teams to triage and resolve issues efficiently.
Represent quality assurance in cross-functional discussions including design reviews, release readiness decisions, and retrospectives — advocating for quality at every stage of the development lifecycle.
Collaborate with software developers, hardware engineers, and systems engineers to understand technical architecture and assess how changes impact test scope and product behavior.
Mentor junior engineers, interns, and contractors — training them on products, test methodologies, and tools, and creating documentation that reduces tribal knowledge.
Execute testing on physical test floors to qualify releases prior to production deployment, working directly with robotic systems and workcells.
Proactively identify quality risks, propose solutions, and take on projects that improve testing processes or more accurately measure product quality.

A day in the life
Your day starts with a team standup where you and your fellow QA engineers level set on priorities, blockers, and what's happening across active test campaigns. From there, your day might look different depending on where you are in a release cycle.

Some days are heavily hands-on — you're on the test floor at BOS27 running test scenarios against robotic workcells, capturing logs, and investigating unexpected behavior. You'll troubleshoot across hardware, software, and firmware boundaries, pulling data from multiple sources to build a clear picture of what went wrong and why.

Other days are more collaborative — you're in design reviews with software and hardware engineers, asking the questions that shape how a feature gets tested. You might be scoping a test strategy for a new capability, defining what "done" looks like when the requirements are still evolving, or presenting release analysis to stakeholders who need a clear verdict on whether a build is ready for production.

In between, you're building — writing test cases, developing automation that your teammates can pick up and run, creating documentation that eliminates the need for someone to tap you on the shoulder every time. You'll also spend time mentoring junior engineers and contractors, helping them ramp on products and test approaches.

You'll regularly collaborate with software development engineers, systems engineers, hardware engineers, and program managers. Your internal customers are the development teams who depend on your test results to make release decisions, and the operations teams who rely on the quality of what ships to fulfillment sites.

In this role you will work at the intersection of machine learning and physical robotics hardware. You will collaborate with hardware engineers to evaluate how your models perform on real sensors and edge compute, run experiments that directly influence what gets built next, and validate perception systems alongside robotics program teams. You will push the boundaries of computer vision for robotic applications while seeing your work deploy on real robots in real fulfillment centers. This is applied science with immediate, measurable impact at a scale no other robotics company can offer.

Amazon offers a full range of benefits that support you and eligible family members, including domestic partners. Benefits can vary by location, the number of regularly scheduled hours you work, length of employment, and job status such as seasonal or temporary employment. The benefits that generally apply to regular, full-time employees include:

About the team
The Amazon Robotics Quality Assurance Engineering team is a group of approximately 20 engineers supporting a broad portfolio of robotic products and solutions — from manipulation systems and autonomous mobile robots to sortation, storage and retrieval, and outbound dock automation. Our work spans first mile, middle mile, last mile, and outbound dock operations across Amazon's fulfillment network.

We operate across three major test sites in Massachusetts — BOS12 (North Reading), BOS27 (Westborough), and BOS33 (Woburn) — where we maintain dedicated test floors with real robotic workcells and integration environments. We are a mix of hands-on testers, automation builders, and quality strategists who work closely with software, hardware, and systems engineering teams to make sure what ships to production actually works. We are growing and looking for curious, technically strong people who want to make a real impact on how robotics technology serves customers worldwide.

Basic qualifications

- 4+ years of quality assurance engineering experience
- Experience in automation testing
- Experience in manual testing
- Experience as QA lead on medium to large sized projects

Preferred qualifications

- Experience with at least one automated test framework like Selenium or Appium
- Experience in gathering test requirements to create detailed test plans and defining quality metrics to measure product quality
- Experience troubleshooting and debugging technical systems
- Experience developing high quality test plans, test designs, test strategies, and test execution
- Experience of using test case management tools (e.g. Test Rail, TestLink) and issue management tools (Jira)
- Experience working closely with development and business teams to communicate problem impacts and to understand business requirements

title: Cloud Systems Engineer II, ADC System Security Engineering, ADC System Security Engineering
descriptionHtml:
Come join a security team who focuses on ease of use and delighting our customers to build and support security services, used across all of Amazon, that secure our internal systems and networks.

At Amazon Web Services (AWS), Security is our highest priority. Our team is responsible for inventing, scaling, and operating the foundational security services used across Amazon to secure our systems, processes, and data. We build authentication, authorization, and enforcement services that are used across our diverse internal teams as they build and deliver services for our customers. We support all of Amazon.com and AWS with our services, and need solution-oriented thinkers who are passionate about solving problems at scale, thinking through edge cases, and iterating quickly to delight our customers.

Are you a good fit for our team?
You’ll love the ADC System Security Engineering team if you are passionate about security, and curious how we design security into the cloud and Amazon infrastructure from the minute a server hits our data center through how we securely administer and operate services. At Amazon, we are looking for engineers who know how to think through a problem, be creative, and who think outside the box in ways that benefit our customers. The intense focus we have on our customers is why we are one of the world’s most beloved brands – it is part of our company DNA.

Our Engineers (you!) are obsessed with customer trust, building solutions that address real world risks, and thinking deeply about how humans use security systems to build elegant security that users love to use. We are looking for people who bring diverse perspectives, ask a lot of questions, and challenge the status quo. We are a team of out-of-the-box thinkers, who iterate quickly, and think deeply about how to build secure systems that are easy to use.

This position requires that the candidate selected must currently possess and maintain an active TS/SCI security clearance. The position further requires that, after start, the selected candidate obtain and maintain an active TS/SCI security clearance with polygraph or commensurate clearance for each government agency for which they perform AWS work.

Key job responsibilities
In this role you will join an established and rapidly growing DevOps engineering team who is maintaining an existing security service while expanding the deployment, features, and capabilities to address significant new initiatives across the company.

The ADC System Security Engineering Team works across the company on services that are always-on; the company depends on us. To perform our best, we value work/life harmony, flexible schedules, and unscheduled time to brain storm. We support established, and rapidly growing services, with a DevOps model, so you will be part of an on-call rotation every couple of months.

Our challenges and goals are ambitious, often ambiguous, and we sometimes try things that don’t work. We embrace the learnings from failure and iterate quickly. We emphasize shipping rapidly, using automated releases and testing to deploy frequently, and deeply root causing issues to ensure that we stay fast. On a typical day, we are together in the office collaborating around a whiteboard, planning over coffee, or playing a video game during downtime.

A day in the life
- Build, deploy, and maintain security services that are used internally to support the US intelligence community.
- Mentor other Systems and Systems Development Engineers in their career growth.
- Work backwards from the customer to ensure our services are developed with features that meet the needs of our end users.

About the team
Why AWS
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

AWS Infrastructure Services (AIS)
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Mentorship and Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

title: Sr Software Development Manager, Managed Agents, AWS
descriptionHtml:
Running AI agents in the cloud is an exciting, quickly-evolving area, and successfully deploying them at scale can be difficult. An agent runs for minutes or hours, calls tools, writes and runs code, and keeps state across many turns. It has to do all of that inside a customer's security boundary, with the same trust, reliability, isolation, and auditability that customers expect from any other AWS service. Our team builds the managed services that makes this possible. Customers define their agent definitions, and we run them as a fully managed AWS service: provisioning, sandboxed execution, session state, identity, observability, and scaling.

The service covers the whole agent lifecycle. It creates and configures agents, runs long-lived sessions with durable state, executes tools and code in isolated environments, connects to customer data and systems with appropriate identity, and gives customers the logs, metrics, and controls they need to run agents in production. We work closely with leading model providers to bring their agent experiences to AWS customers. That means our engineers solve problems at the boundary between AWS customers, frontier labs, and AWS cloud infrastructure.

As Sr. SDM for Managed Agents, you will lead a team of senior engineers building one of the newest and fastest-growing areas of AWS. You will own the technical strategy and roadmap for the service, partner with model providers and AWS service teams, and be responsible for all aspects of its end-to-end engineering, operations, and growth. This is an early-stage service. You will set the engineering bar, hire and grow the team, and make architectural decisions that influence how enterprises run AI agents for years to come.

Basic qualifications

- 5+ years of engineering team management experience
- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science (or related field) or equivalent work experience
- 10+ years' experience in the development of mission-critical system software, with experience working on distributed systems, machine learning infrastructure, or large-scale data platforms

Preferred qualifications

- Experience building or operating services that run untrusted or customer-supplied code, such as serverless compute, container platforms, or sandboxed execution environments
- Experience developing and deploying cloud-based AI/ML technology, particularly LLM inference, agent frameworks, or tool-use and orchestration systems

- Experience leading technical partnerships with external companies, especially co-developing a product with a partner

title: Senior Software Dev Engineer, Route 53 Health Checks and Console Core
descriptionHtml:
Build the service that checks the health of millions of endpoints around the world every few seconds, and the consoles customers rely on to run DNS and route traffic at global scale. As a Senior SDE on the Amazon Route 53 Health Checks and Console Core team, you will own the technical direction for the team and drive the plan with leadership, lead how we use AI to design, build, test, and operate software, and grow the engineers around you. You will own the distributed health checking infrastructure and the public API in front of it, build the AI tooling every Route 53 service team depends on, and launch new AI services for DNS and Route 53. You will help define what our customers use next.

We are based in Vancouver, BC. We own Route 53 Health Checks, a highly available endpoint monitoring service that helps Route 53 DNS, Amazon Elastic Load Balancing, Amazon RDS, Amazon S3, and many other AWS services maintain high availability for their customers. We also own the core tooling, standards, and shared infrastructure that every Route 53 console is built on. This is a full stack role. You will design and operate the services and APIs behind Route 53 Health Checks, and you will take our console tooling from something our team uses to something every Route 53 service team builds on, while we hold the quality bar on what ships. Your work will reach across more than 10 service teams and the product managers, designers, and engineers you partner with throughout AWS networking.

AI is central to how we work and what we build. As a senior engineer on the team, you will own how we work with it. You will define the AI development process the team runs on across coding, testing, and operations, decide which tools and practices we adopt, measure whether they make us faster and safer, and roll what works out to the service teams that build on our platform. You will own the results of the team, not only your own code. You will drive our yearly plan, turn goals into projects with milestones and estimates, sequence the work across the team, and track it to delivery. When a plan slips or a risk shows up, you raise it early and change the plan. You will lead projects that span several engineers, drive the designs behind them, and mentor engineers through design reviews and code reviews.


Key job responsibilities
- Own the technical direction and the roadmap for the team, and lead projects that span several engineers from requirements to launch.
- Drive the yearly plan for the team with leadership, break goals into projects with milestones and estimates, and recommend what the team builds first
- Track delivery across the team, raise risks early, and adjust the plan when priorities or dependencies change.
- Define and run the AI development process for the team across coding, testing, and operations, and roll it out to service teams across Route 53.
- Mentor and grow the engineers on the team, and raise the bar through design reviews, code reviews, and operational reviews.
- Design, build, and operate the distributed health checking infrastructure and public API behind Route 53 Health Checks.
- Build and vend the AI tooling that service teams across Route 53 use to design and build their own console changes, and hold the quality bar on what they ship.
- Own and build new AI services and capabilities for DNS and Route 53, from idea to launch.
- Operate what you build. Take part in on call, own metrics and alarms, and drive root cause analysis on production issues.
- Work with product managers, designers, and engineers across more than 10 service teams in AWS networking.
- Turn requirements that are ambiguous and change quickly into products customers rely on.
Our health checking stack is primarily Java and Linux, with lots of interaction with public AWS services and Amazon internal tools. Our console stack is TypeScript and React. We do not expect you to know all of it, but we do expect you to be excited to learn it.

A day in the life
Our customers are the developers and businesses who use Route 53 to manage DNS and route traffic for their applications around the world, and our job is to make that easy, reliable, and fast. No two days look the same. You might start the morning reviewing a design with an engineer you mentor, then work with the team on a new AI practice to cut the time from idea to production. After lunch you might review a change a service team submitted and hold the bar on the console patterns and the design guidelines, then spend the rest of the afternoon on the health checking infrastructure itself, on the checkers that monitor millions of endpoints or the public API in front of them. Some days you go deep on a distributed system, other days you are building tooling or trying out a new AI tool and deciding whether the team should adopt it. You drive the plan for what the team builds next with leadership, track how it is going, and partner with service teams across AWS networking to ship features that reach customers everywhere. When a hackathon idea grabs you, there is room to chase it.


About the team
We are a tight knit team that cares about our customers and about running a highly available platform on the Internet. We like to experiment and to learn out loud, whether that is a hackathon, a demo of something you just built, or a session digging into a new AI tool together. We are good at making sense of ambiguity and shipping products people rely on, and we welcome bold ideas and give you the ownership to take them all the way. And when we are not building, we make time to have fun together with regular team outings.

If you want to lead hard problems at scale, help shape the plan for a team that builds with AI, and help decide where an AWS service goes next, we would like to hear from you.

Basic qualifications

- 7+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
- 7+ years of leading design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- 7+ years of highly scalable systems experience
- Experience as a mentor, tech lead or leading an engineering team

Preferred qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent

title: HR Specialist, People Foundations, Amazon Leo
descriptionHtml:
Have you ever wanted to be part of a team building industry-changing technology? At Leo, we are building a low Earth orbit satellite network that will deliver broadband connectivity to unserved and underserved communities. Come join one of Amazon's most ambitious bets, scaling fast toward commercial launch with a workforce that spans hourly 24/7 production operations and corporate teams.

We are seeking an HR Specialist to serve as the programmatic owner for building, shaping, and onboarding Leo onto the people systems and mechanisms that HRPs, managers, and employees rely on. This role exists to unlock HRPs and managers by making sure the platforms, content, and listening mechanisms that serve Leo actually fit Leo's workforce, not configurations built for other populations. This role is a rethink of how the work gets done. You will work AI-native from the start, using AI to drive a step change in your approach and maximize output across programs, not just to do the same work faster.

You will own the work end-to-end, turning business requirements into configured, working solutions and driving them through the central teams that own the platforms. That includes standing up mechanisms that give leaders a real-time read on workforce sentiment and culture risk, getting Leo-specific content and policy into the right places while removing what does not apply, and locking in the right survey questions and definitions for both the hourly and corporate populations.

This is a portfolio and influence role. You will operate as an independent strategic owner, not a conduit. You will set the prioritization criteria that determine which requirements get resourced, build the intake and road mapping mechanisms the function runs against, and secure Leo's position in central roadmaps. Leo is smaller by headcount but outsized in business criticality, so it does not always compete for roadmap space on size alone. Your job is to make sure both populations are reflected in the systems that serve them, so HRPs and managers are not left to absorb the gaps.

This role is net-new. You will stand up the inaugural charter, mechanisms, and standards based on customer needs rather than inheriting an established playbook. While Leo is the primary portfolio, this role reports to the Sr. HRP Manager for Leo, Entertainment, Ads/IMDb/Grand Challenge, and Devices & Services (LEAD) and is designed to extend this programmatic muscle across LEAD business lines where similar people-systems needs exist.

Key job responsibilities
- Own the People Systems and Mechanisms Portfolio End-to-End. Own the work to build, shape, and onboard Leo onto its people systems and mechanisms. Run intake, set the criteria that determine which requirements get dedicated resources, and make capacity tradeoffs across active workstreams so the highest-leverage needs land first. Partner with the Leo HRBP team on central efforts like compensation and time systems.
- Build and Onboard Listening and Sensing Mechanisms. Partner with central science teams to stand up the mechanisms that give leaders a real-time read on workforce sentiment and site-level culture risk. Configure them so the signal is accurate and leaders get a self-serve asset, not one that requires HRP interpretation.
- Build AI-Native Mechanisms. Build AI into the portfolio's core mechanisms rather than treating it as an add-on. Set the standard for how AI-enabled workflows scale this work across LEAD, keeping human judgment on the tradeoffs and decisions.
- Configure Content and Policy Across the Central Platforms. Get Leo-specific content and policy into the right places and remove what does not apply, so self-service actually fits the workforce and directly unlocks HRPs and managers.
- Ensure the Mixed Workforce Is Correctly Represented. Lock in the right survey question sets for both the hourly 24/7 and corporate populations, and codify durable definitions the HRP role runs against, including how proximity is defined and applied.
- Own Portfolio Health and Surface Systemic Risk Early. Build the metrics and status mechanisms that show whether requirements are landing as working solutions, not post-launch defects. Spot systemic vulnerabilities in the intake-to-delivery pipeline before they become compliance exposure or business disruption and drive them to resolution through the owner teams you influence but do not manage.
- Lead Change Management and Write the Strategic Narratives. Roll out delivered solutions with the business and the HRP team, build scalable mechanisms and standards for intake and change, author the PR/FAQs and MBR/QBR inputs that articulate decision points and tradeoffs, and own inputs into OP1 and OP2.
- Extend Programmatic Capabilities Across LEAD. Scale this work across the broader LEAD business lines where similar needs exist, rather than solving them one by one. That includes thinking through hourly-population needs across business lines together, or owning scoping and implementation for shared tool rollouts, so one build serves many.
- Contribute to Initiatives Beyond the Core Portfolio. Take on work that requires programmatic execution, including people-systems integration for acquisitions and preparation for new site buildouts. Sequence the mechanisms so they are operational before the complexity lands.

title: Site HR Partner Manager, Amazon Leo
descriptionHtml:
Have you ever wanted to be part of a team building industry-changing technology? At Leo, we are building a low Earth orbit satellite network that will deliver broadband connectivity to unserved and underserved communities. Come join one of Amazon's most ambitious bets, with customers like Delta Airlines, JetBlue, AT&T, and others already committed ahead of commercial launch.
We are seeking an HRP Manager to lead the Site HR Partners who serve Leo's Production Operations (ProdOps) organization. You will own the standards the team operates against and the forward-looking model for how site HRP partnership evolves as the business grows. Every satellite is a one-way-door decision, and the pace demands manager excellence as a precondition to mission success.
This is not a standard corporate HR role. ProdOps is 24/7 aerospace manufacturing, where technicians build every satellite the business pushes to Launch Services, and where the managers your team serves are navigating the intersection of Amazon's people culture with the operational discipline of building satellites. Many are external hires with deep technical expertise who are still building fluency in how Amazon develops people, or Amazon veterans encountering manufacturing realities for the first time. Site HRPs deliver capabilities not found in traditional corporate HRP roles: proactive sentiment reading through weekly floor walks and Gembas, time-sensitive labor relations work in a high ER/LR environment, round-the-clock shift coverage, and direct coaching on how to lead where the stakes are measured in millions of dollars per week.
In this role, you will directly manage a team of Site HRPs across the production sites and shifts, and you will own their development end to end: coaching their strategic judgment, functional skill, and advisory craft so they operate as independent partners rather than conduits. You will think ahead of the business, anticipating what the workforce and the Site HRP model need to look like at scale and building toward that before the demand arrives. As the network grows to establish dedicated presence across sites, extends into evening and overnight coverage, and absorbs net-new facility stand-ups, your central charge is to make sure the team on the floor is developed, consistent, operating to one standard, and ready for what comes next.
This role reports to the Sr. HRP Manager (Leo), who owns the integrated Corp, Site, and Launch Services HRP delivery model and the multi-year ProdOps HRP strategy. You own the site HRP strategy, how the team is developed, and how the model scales within that framework. The role requires regular travel to production sites to work alongside your team, understand evolving business challenges, and maintain strong relationships with operational leadership.


Key job responsibilities
• Lead and Develop the Site HRP Team. Directly manage a team of Site HRPs supporting the hourly manufacturing workforce across production sites and shifts. Demonstrate a clear understanding of the performance and leadership bar and apply it to hiring and talent decisions. Provide regular coaching and feedback that grows each HRP’s strategic judgment, functional skill, and leadership capability, and build a team that delivers with increasing independence as the network scales.
• Own Site HRP Ways of Working and the Standard of Excellence. Define and run the frameworks, mechanisms, and quality standards the Site HRP team operates against, including how floor walks, Gembas, structured listening, and case work are delivered consistently across every site and shift. Build the inspection mechanisms that ensure advisory quality, sound judgment, and timely closure across the team’s portfolio.
• Deliver Consistent, High-Quality Manager Guidance Across Sites and Shifts. Own the Site HRP team’s metrics and the manager customer experience. Review the guidance and case work the team handles to ensure quality, sound judgment, and timely closure, and coach the team to synthesize inputs into action and communicate risk proactively. The scope of guidance spans performance management, employee relations, talent decisions, compensation guidance, policy consultation, and crisis support.
• Build Manager Capability Through Scalable Mechanisms. Design and run scalable mechanisms that build manager capability over time (manager enablement, structured coaching such as Seek to Understand, and proactive insight tools) so ProdOps managers lead effective teams with growing confidence and self-sufficiency, strengthening the manager population rather than resolving one case at a time.
• Partner on Employee Relations Strategy and Prevention. Partner with GCER and Legal and provide guidance and oversight to the team on ER cases, ensuring sound judgment, timely closure, and adherence to a high bar on ER metrics. Set the standard for how the team navigates complex workplace investigations and uses embedded floor presence to resolve concerns before they escalate into formal cases.
• Scale the Site HRP Model Without Ground-Up Rebuilds. As the Site network grows (dedicated presence across sites, extended evening and overnight coverage, and net-new facility stand-ups), build the onboarding, coverage, and ways-of-working standards that absorb growth without rebuilding from scratch, ensuring coverage and development are operational ahead of each new site’s first technicians.
• Measure, Inspect, and Advance AI-First Delivery. Translate operational data into systemic insight through dashboards and trend analysis that surface employee-experience signal before it becomes escalation, and champion AI-first ways of working (for example Amazon Quick and self-service through Aza) that shift team capacity from reactive case handling toward proactive, capability-building advisory work.

- 2+ years of management experience implementing processes and delivering core HR solutions in large-scale and complex environments
- Experience coaching and developing HR professionals and building team capability

title: Signal Integrity Engineer, Amazon Devices
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Lab126 is an inventive research and development company that designs and engineers high-profile devices like the Kindle family of products. Lab126 began in 2004 as a subsidiary of Amazon.com, Inc. Since then, we have worked to produce best-selling e-readers and tablets, as well as new inventions like Echo line of products, Fire TV and Fire phone. What will you help us create?

Key job responsibilities
As a Signal Integrity Engineer, you will be part of Validation team that is exploring new hardware designs to improve our devices. In this role, you will be responsible for Signal Integrity aspects, compliance, and interoperability of package substrate, PCB, Cable solutions and system-level SI for interfaces like PCIe, DDR, Clocks etc. You will also be responsible for contributing to package and platform design guideline development.

You will work closely with multi-disciplinary groups including Board Design, System Architects, IP developers, and Design Engineering, to verify and deliver complex, high volume SoCs that enable development of world-class hardware devices. In this role, you will be:
• Responsible for defining the design guidelines for internal and external design teams and delivering reference simulation docs for customers
• Performing modeling of package substrate/PCB channels elements in 3D/2D EM simulation tools.
• Working with silicon designers, platform designers, package designers, electrical validation teams, etc. to support interconnect and interface performance requirements.
• Reviewing and evaluating package and board design and providing review feedback.
• Responsible for providing power delivery solutions across platform, package and SOC level
• Definition of worst-case currents and voltage drop scenarios, MIM/decoupling allocation, grid choices and analysis, droop control, SOC ESD compliance, On-die droop detectors, usage of on-die delivery solutions like VR, LDO, and Power gates.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or a related field
- 4+ years of hardware design and validation of components, subsystems and systems experience
- High speed serial interface analog building blocks, protocol, specifications and test methods
- Familiarity with Simulation tools (ADS, HFSS, PowerSI, PowerDC, Hyperlynx) to execute SI-PI simulations is required.
- Experience with performing measurement, and correlating measurements to simulations.
- Experience with modeling and simulation of high-speed interface interconnects/channel.
- Excellent analytical and problem solving skills

Preferred qualifications

- Master's degree in Electrical or Communications Engineering or a related field
- Understanding of Power & signal integrity concepts such as differential impedance, jitter, insertion loss, return loss, termination, etc.
- Scripting experience in any programming language (C++, Python, PERL, MATLAB) to develop automation scripts is a plus.
- Experience in Analog IP Characterization (SerDes, PLL, DDR) is desirable.
- Good understanding of High-Speed Analog/Digital Circuits, VLSI, semiconductor physics

title: Digital Sovereignty Specialist Solutions Architect
descriptionHtml:
AWS is hiring a Digital Sovereignty Specialist Solutions Architect for Spain, Portugal, Italy, and Southern Europe. You will help customers and public sector organizations move workloads to AWS when sovereignty, security, and regulatory requirements decide what can run in the cloud.

Organizations in highly regulated industries and the public sector across Southern Europe are deciding now how to meet their sovereignty requirements. You will be their technical counterpart for the AWS European Sovereign Cloud and for the sovereignty controls available in AWS Regions. You will also build on the work AWS has done with national cybersecurity authorities in the region, such as secure configuration guidance and landing zone templates aligned with national security frameworks.

Specialist Solutions Architects are part of the AWS sales organization. They bring deep domain expertise to customers with complex problems and work closely with account teams, AWS Professional Services, and Partners to help customers get to production.

This role is based in Madrid, Lisbon, or Rome. Native or professional proficiency in Spanish and professional proficiency in English are required. Italian and Portuguese are highly valued.

Key job responsibilities
- Advise customers, partners, and public sector organizations in Spain, Portugal, Italy, and Southern Europe on running workloads with sovereignty requirements on the AWS European Sovereign Cloud and in AWS Regions
- Lead the technical response to RFIs and RFPs that include sovereignty, security, and compliance requirements
- Work with national cybersecurity authorities, together with AWS security assurance and public policy colleagues, on cloud security guidance, secure configuration guides, and landing zone templates
- Deliver briefings, workshops, and architecture reviews for customers and partners, and speak at industry events
- Bring customer requirements to AWS service teams and turn field experience into whitepapers, blogs, and reusable content

A day in the life
Most weeks combine customer and partner meetings, time for focused work, and collaboration with colleagues across EMEA. A typical week might include a working session with a bank's security leaders on their sovereignty requirements, a review of the technical answers in a public sector tender with the account team, and preparation for a workshop with a national cybersecurity authority. You also set aside time to write, whether that is a secure configuration guide, a blog post, or feedback to an AWS service team based on what you hear from customers.

About the team
The Sovereignty Technology team helps customers, partners, and public sector organizations across EMEA adopt AWS. We cover the AWS European Sovereign Cloud and sovereignty controls in AWS Regions, and we work with regulated enterprises, software vendors and system integrators building sovereign offerings, national regulators, and EU institutions. Team members are based in several European countries.

In this role you will build expertise in European security and sovereignty frameworks, work directly with AWS service teams on the features customers ask for, and represent AWS with regulators and at industry events. You will have access to mentorship, knowledge sharing, and other career resources to help you grow.

Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, has not followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, do not let it stop you from applying.

Basic qualifications

- Experience communicating across technical and non-technical audiences, including executive level stakeholders or clients
- 5+ years in a technical role involving cloud architecture, security, or infrastructure
- 2+ years architecting or operating solutions on AWS
- Experience with security, compliance, or regulatory requirements for cloud workloads (e.g. ISO 27001, SOC 2, ENS, C5)
- Professional proficiency in Spanish and English

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in infrastructure architecture, database architecture and networking
- Experience working with end user or developer communities
- Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, mathematics or equivalent
- Experience working with national regulators, cybersecurity agencies, or standards bodies on cloud security guidance, accreditation, or certification
- Knowledge of digital sovereignty and cloud security frameworks in the EU (e.g. ENS, CPSTIC, EUCS, C5)

title: Technical Infrastructure Project Manager - Networking, Network Deployment - Fulfilment Center Technology
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Network Deployment Services owns the planning, delivery, and lifecycle management of network infrastructure supporting Amazon's global fulfillment, transportation and grocery, sites. Our infrastructure enables reliable connectivity for Amazon's operations at scale and plays a critical role in supporting business growth, operational efficiency, and customer experience. The team is responsible for delivering network infrastructure programs across the full lifecycle, including hardware deployment, upgrades, capacity expansion, technology refresh, optimization, and decommissioning. We work closely with Engineering, Finance, Supply Chain, Field Deployment, Operations, and external vendors to deliver scalable, reliable, and cost-effective infrastructure solutions across Amazon's global network.
We are seeking a Technical Infrastructure Program Manager (TIPM) to lead large-scale network hardware deployment and lifecycle programs. The successful candidate will own program planning and execution, drive financial and commercial approvals, coordinate hardware procurement and field deployments, and ensure programs are delivered on time and within budget. This role requires strong program management fundamentals, the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously, and experience delivering complex infrastructure programs across cross-functional teams.


Key job responsibilities
• Program Ownership and Execution: Own end-to-end planning and delivery of network hardware lifecycle programs, including technology refresh, infrastructure upgrades, capacity expansion, and hardware replacement. Manage multiple programs in parallel, ensuring delivery against agreed schedules, budgets, and business requirements.
• Financial Planning and Approvals: Partner with Finance and business stakeholders to develop project cost estimates, prepare and secure Capital Authorization Request (CAR) approvals, track budget utilization, and manage financial risks and changes throughout the program lifecycle.
• Vendor and Commercial Management: Work with hardware vendors, suppliers, and internal procurement teams to obtain quotes, negotiate pricing, evaluate commercial proposals, and drive cost-effective procurement while meeting program timelines and technical requirements.
• Project Planning and Deployment Coordination: Develop detailed project plans, milestones, resource requirements, and deployment schedules. Coordinate with field deployment teams, engineering teams, vendors, and site stakeholders to ensure hardware deployments are executed as planned and dependencies are addressed proactively.
• Risk and Dependency Management: Identify delivery risks, technical dependencies, resource constraints, and schedule deviations early. Establish mitigation plans, drive issue resolution, and escalate blockers to the appropriate stakeholders to protect committed timelines.
• Stakeholder Management and Communication: Build strong working relationships across Engineering, Finance, Procurement, Supply Chain, Field Deployment, Operations, and external vendors. Provide clear and regular program updates to stakeholders and senior leadership, highlighting progress, risks, financial status, and decisions required.
• Metrics and Operational Excellence: Establish scalable mechanisms to track program milestones, deployment progress, financial performance, vendor commitments, and delivery risks. Use metrics to improve visibility, identify bottlenecks, reduce deployment cycle times, and drive continuous improvement.
• Process Improvement and Standardization: Identify opportunities to simplify program execution, standardize deployment processes, improve planning accuracy, and reduce manual effort across hardware lifecycle programs. Develop repeatable mechanisms that support increased deployment volume and operational scale.

- • Experience coordinating field deployment teams across multiple sites or geographic regions.
- • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple complex programs simultaneously in a fast-paced environment.

title: Robotics Data Collection Tech Lead, Frontier AI & Robotics (FAR)
descriptionHtml:
Are you interested in solving the most critical operations problem behind cutting-edge robotics development? Interested in fast dynamic environment? Amazon's Frontier AI & Robotics (FAR) team is building advanced robotic systems through frontier foundation models, and high-quality data collection is a core input to that research.

Key job responsibilities
Own the technical execution and continuous improvement of early-stage data collection for advanced robotics. Partner with researchers to translate research objectives into reliable collection workflows, improve data quality, and shorten policy training iteration cycles. Work independently within agreed priorities, providing hands-on technical guidance to data collectors and coordinating execution across research, engineering, and operations.

In this role, you will
- Own end to end collection iterations for assigned research tasks, from requirements and station readiness through pilot data collection, quality review, and delivery of training-ready data. Coordinate dependencies and resolve blockers to meet agreed quality and turnaround goals.

- Partner with researchers to develop and refine SOPs, translating task objectives, failure modes, and evaluation feedback into clear collection instructions and acceptance criteria. Maintain version control and ensure collectors adopt changes consistently.

- Serve as the technical subject matter expert for assigned data collection workflows, equipment, and tools. Independently diagnose complex issues involving robotics hardware, sensors, calibration, collection software, and data integrity; engage engineering partners when resolution requires deeper expertise.

- Provide daily technical direction and coaching to data collectors. Demonstrate correct execution, calibrate collectors against quality standards, and develop their troubleshooting skills and judgment.

- Assess operational and technical risks, including equipment readiness, unsafe conditions, data loss, and quality degradation. Determine when to continue, pause collection, or escalate, and coordinate recovery within established safety and technical boundaries.
- Coordinate technical and nontechnical stakeholders, including researchers, engineering, operations, and annotation partners. Communicate priorities, trade-offs, risks, and decisions clearly, and escalate issues that threaten delivery commitments.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree or above in Operations Research, Statistics, Applied Mathematics, Engineering, Computer Science or related field, or experience working in Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics (STEM)
- Demonstrated ability to deliver independently within defined objectives, coordinate multiple partner teams, and resolve operational blockers with limited guidance
- Experience diagnosing hardware, software, or process issues, using evidence to identify root causes and implement corrective actions
- Strong problem-solving and systems-thinking skills, including the ability to assess risks and make sound technical decisions with incomplete information
- Working understanding of how collection quality, task coverage, and consistency affect model training and evaluation, with the ability to translate research requirements into executable procedures and quality checks
- Demonstrated ability to train and mentor others and communicate complex information clearly to technical and nontechnical audiences, including remote teams and colleagues who use English as a second language

Preferred qualifications

- 2+ years of experience in technical operations, engineering, technical project management, or a related role involving hands-on ownership of complex systems or workflows
- Experience developing SOPs, technical documentation, performance metrics, and process improvements, and ensuring their adoption
- Experience with robotics, teleoperation, egocentric video, or multimodal sensor data
- Experience supporting ML/AI data collection, annotation, quality assurance, or model evaluation workflows
- Familiarity with sensor calibration, timestamp synchronization, pose tracking, and data integrity checks
- Experience using vibe coding agents to build and maintain lightweight operational tools
- Experience taking an experimental workflow from initial pilot through repeatable execution across multiple stations or teams

descriptionHtml:

Qualified candidates will have stock plan compliance or mobility taxation experience.

The ideal candidate is highly organized and analytical, works effectively with internal and external contacts, and has a proven ability to manage critical projects concurrently and through to successful completion. title: Global Process Manager, AWS GFO, AWS Global Field OPerations (GFO)
descriptionHtml:
Do you love fixing how work gets done, not just writing it down? Help AWS make operational processes simpler, safer and faster for field teams supporting infrastructure in places most people never see.

As a Global Process Manager, you'll own a set of global processes from start to finish and lead improvement projects that measurably change how teams around the world work. This isn't a documentation role. You'll find where work slows down, fix it with the people doing it, and use AI tools to keep processes current, so your time goes into improvement.

In this role you will:
- Lead improvement projects from workflow mapping to measurable results
- Own and continuously improve global operational processes
- Help new programs design their ways of working from scratch
- Partner with field technicians, program managers, operations leaders, and safety and security teams
- Use AI tools to cut manual effort and keep processes up to date

Key job responsibilities
- Lead process improvement projects from start to finish: map the current workflow, find the waste, run workshops with the people doing the work, and follow actions through to measurable results.
- Own a portfolio of global operational processes and keep them accurate, simple and easy to follow.
- Review and act on incoming change requests from field technicians, program teams and partners, and spot the patterns that point to a bigger problem.
- Design processes from scratch for new programs and customers, working with their teams to get them ready to launch.
- Use AI tools to draft, update and maintain process documentation, cutting manual effort so your time goes into improvement.
- Set improvement targets for your processes, track them with data, and report progress to operations leaders.
- Work with safety, security and quality partners so processes meet safety and compliance standards.
- Step in quickly when a field issue needs a procedure changed, and make sure the fix sticks.
- Share what works across teams, including supporting teams that don't have their own process expertise.

A day in the life
Your main focus is making global operational processes work better. Most weeks you're running an improvement project: mapping a workflow with the team, running a workshop to find waste, then following up on the actions until they're done and the results show up in the data.

You also own a set of processes from start to finish. You'll handle change requests from technicians and program teams around the world, talk with the people who use your processes, and update them yourself with AI tools, so your time goes on improving things rather than paperwork.

Some days you'll help a new program build its processes from scratch, or step in when something in the field needs a fast fix.

About the team
We support AWS infrastructure outside the traditional data center: at customer sites, partner locations and new programs around the world. Our mission is to give these customers the best end-to-end support, safely and reliably, wherever the work happens.

You'll join a small global process team that gives field technicians, coordinators and partner vendors clear, simple ways of working. You'll work with operations leaders, program managers, safety and security partners, and the people doing the work on site.

The problems you'll solve are real and visible: steps that slow technicians down, handoffs that break between teams, and new programs that need processes built from scratch. We're growing quickly, so there's more work than people, and plenty of room to shape how we operate.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of program or project management experience
- 3+ years of defining and implementing process improvement initiatives using data and metrics experience
- Knowledge of Excel (Pivot Tables, VLookUps) at an advanced level and SQL
- Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
- Experience working cross functionally with tech and non-tech teams

Preferred qualifications

- 3+ years of driving end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership experience
- 3+ years of driving process improvements experience
- Experience building processes, project management, and schedules
- Experience in stakeholder management, dealing with multiple stakeholders at varied levels of the organization
- 2+ years of communicating with and presenting to executive and senior audiences experience
- Experience with six sigma tools and Lean techniques

title: Procurement Category Manager, OneMHS Procurement & Supply Chain
descriptionHtml:
Amazon installs a significant quantity of new buildings every year. The historical model has been to allow each integrator to use their own equipment, controls, subsystems, and methodologies. While that has allowed Amazon to be successful to this point, the variability between buildings has proven difficult to support and scale. One MHS’ charge is to build partnerships to focus on consistency and scalability across our network of the future. We will be partnering with key suppliers to help them scale up their manufacturing capabilities to keep up with our needs, as well as refining their designs to drive innovation and operational uptime and better meet the specific needs of Amazon’s operational environment. In partnership with WWDE, OMHS will challenge the status quo on our Gen14 AR sortables building by focusing on critical equipment, controls, and system implementation methods.
