title: Onsite Medical Representative
descriptionHtml:
Join Amazon’s mission to become Earth’s safest place to work! At Amazon, we’ve set the ambitious goal to become the benchmark of safety excellence across all industries in which we operate. The Amazon Workplace Health & Safety (WHS) team sets the strategic direction to provide resources, best practices, and safe environments to proactively manage the health and wellbeing of our workforce. To support these goals, Amazon is seeking an experienced and dynamic Onsite Medical Representative (OMR) to join our team. In this position, you will work closely with the WHS Site Manager, WHS Specialist, and occasionally the Injury Prevention Specialist (IPS). This includes attending weekly associate safety committee meetings, greeting all new hires for the site or through daily one-on-one interaction. Additionally, the OMR will participate in weekly case management review meetings as necessary.

As an OMR, you will independently assess and administer first aid as well as offer guidance to Amazon Associates (AAs) on both occupational and non-occupational injuries or illnesses. You should be passionate about learning and advocating health and wellness principles to consistently support AAs on a daily basis. You will refer care to outside medical providers as needed, and learn about OSHA regulations, risk, and analysis.

The OMR will function as a part of the larger team onsite, assisting with all first aid needs and support safety operations as needed.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:
- Provide first aid support and make referrals to outside medical providers as necessary.
- Minimize the AA risk of injury through awareness, education, and proactive engagement.
- Maintain all records of care provided to AAs.
- Coordinate and maintain the workers’ compensation and return to work programs for AAs with work-related injuries.
- Provide daily activity logs and end of shift reports.
- Engage with AAs and leadership on operations floor to provide coaching regarding observed at-risk work habits.
- Maintain a clean working environment and ensure appropriate medical supply inventory is maintained.
- Participate in training and certification to facilitate first aid, CPR and AED certifications classes.
- Maintain all first aid, CPR, AED credentials.
- Work flexible shifts which could include days, nights, holidays, and/or weekends.
- Assist with random saliva drug testing protocols.
- Maintain effective care delivery in emergencies and assist emergency response at the site.

Additional Job Elements include:
- Lift up to 49 pounds and frequently push, pull, squat, bend, and reach
- Stand/walk for up to 12 hours during shifts
- Work in an environment where the noise level varies
- Work in an environment that is subject to variable temperatures and weather (delivery stations include outside loading departments)
- Continuously climb and descend stairs (applies to sites with stairs)

For those that do not have an adult First Aid, CPR, AED certification from the American Heart Association or American Red Cross, must obtain within 3 weeks of start date.

Basic qualifications

- High school or equivalent diploma
- Current valid Basic Life Support (BLS) certification by an approved emergency cardiac care (ECC) provider; AND must have one of the following:
- Current valid Emergency Medical Technician (EMT) OR Paramedic Certification from the Department of Health OR the National Registry of Emergency Medical Technicians (NREMT); OR
- Current active Athletic Trainer Certification, by either the Board of Certification (BOC) or equivalent State Certification.

Preferred qualifications

- Certified to teach first aid, CPR, and AED training from American Heart Association or American Red Cross
- Proficient in Microsoft Office
- Experience with an industrial wellness program
- Experience managing musculoskeletal disorders, ergonomics, and coaching on body mechanics
- Demonstrated work experience with OSHA regulations and Workers Compensation
- Proficient in digital recordkeeping
- In the last year, six months job experience in the Military as a Combat Medic (U.S. Army), Field Medic (U.S. Army), Healthcare Specialist (U.S. Army), Hospital Corpsman (U.S. Navy), or Aerospace Medical Service Technician (U.S. Air Force)

title: Forward Deployed Engineer (Model Customization and Optimization), AWS Forward Deployed Engineering
descriptionHtml:
As a Forward Deployed Engineer II (FDE II) on the Custom Model and Optimization team, you embed directly with strategic customers to build, optimize, and run custom generative AI models in production alongside their engineering teams. You own complete model workstreams end-to-end from defining the evaluation bar and preparing data, through training and inference optimization, to production deployment.

FDE IIs on this team works at the intersection of models and systems. They customize state-of-the-art open-weight and foundation models for new domains, languages, and modalities; migrate and optimize training and inference workloads on AWS Trainium and operate those models as production services. They are autonomous contributors who take on projects where the business goal is clear, but the path is not. They make design trade-offs with appropriate guidance, limit short-term workarounds, coach others on producing high-quality code, and train new team members.

Key job responsibilities
Embed within customer ML and engineering teams: Understand the customer's business, data, model stack, and operational constraints. Translate ambiguous goals into a measurable evaluation bar and a technical plan for your workstream such as model selection, customization approach, and serving architecture. Requires up to 25% travel.

Customize and post-train models. Adapt open-weight and foundation models to customer domains through continued pre-training, supervised fine-tuning, preference optimization, and reinforcement learning (including RLHF, RL with verifiable rewards, and multi-turn agentic RL). Build the data pipelines, synthetic data generation, and evaluation harnesses that prove a customized model out performs the baseline on the customer's own quality, latency, and cost bar. Apply these techniques to high-value patterns such as coding agents, domain foundation models, and multi-adapter serving.

Build large-scale training and inference systems. Design and implement distributed training and RL post-training pipelines using frameworks such as PyTorch FSDP2, Megatron-LM, Miles, and verl. Build RL interaction harnesses using NeMo Gym or OpenEnv to connect agent workflows, tools, environments, and reward functions to training. Develop production inference stacks with engines such as SGLang and vLLM, and optimize throughput, latency, memory footprint, and cost per token through quantization, parallelism, speculative decoding, and batching.

Optimize models on AWS chips. Migrate and tune training and inference workloads for AWS Trainium using the AWS Neuron SDK. Profile performance, close accuracy-parity gaps against GPU baselines, and develop custom kernels where needed. Benchmark rigorously and turn results into decisions customers can act on.

Accelerate impact beyond the engagement. Codify reusable fine-tuning recipes, evaluation frameworks, benchmarking tools, and optimization patterns that accelerate future deployments. Feed field learnings back to AWS service teams, including Amazon Bedrock, Amazon SageMaker AI, and AWS Neuron. Identify opportunities to expand model customization and optimization within your customer engagement.


About the team
ABOUT AWS:
 
Diverse Experiences
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.
 
Why AWS
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud. 

Inclusive Team Culture
AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.

Mentorship and Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional. 

Team
The Custom Model and Optimization team, part of the Forward Deployed Engineering team partners with enterprises, AI-native startups, and foundation model providers to build, customize, and optimize generative AI models at scale. Our work spans domain foundation models, post-training of open-weight models, and moving training and inference workloads onto AWS Trainium. As embedded engineers within the AWS Forward Deployed Engineering motion, we bring deep model and optimization expertise to customers' most strategic AI workloads, and we turn what we learn into tooling and patterns that scale across AWS.

- Experience programming with at least one modern language such as Java, C++, or C# including object-oriented design
- 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience

- Hands-on experience with generative AI technology, such as LLMs, vision-language models, or speech models
- Experience with AI tools: eval frameworks, agent tooling, RAG pipelines, and prompt engineering
- Experience communicating technical concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences

Preferred qualifications

- Experience with full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations

descriptionHtml:

Amazon devices started with originally creating the best-selling Kindle family of products. Since then, we have produced devices like Fire tablets, Fire TV, and Amazon Echo. Amazon reliability team aims to develop reliable and robust products that delight our customers. In this role, as a Sr. Hardware Reliability Engineer, you will be responsible for the reliability engineering of our new and emerging robotic devices.

As a Senior Hardware Reliability Engineer, you will engage with an experienced cross-disciplinary staff and outside partners to drive key aspects of product definition, execution and test. You must be responsive, flexible and able to succeed within an open collaborative peer environment. You will be responsible for the test and validation of robotic devices. - Identify and validate product risks, including but not limited to electrical system, mechanical system, and work with design teams to mitigate them

Our team speaks the language of our industry customers, which means that we focus on business outcomes and industry use cases on behalf of our customers, whether that is how we build products and solutions, how we sell, how we deliver, or how we partner.
If you are excited about the prospect of using your cloud architecture experience to assist our most valuable customers, tackling challenging problems, have a hand in shaping the future of cloud adoption, enhancing and growing your own skills, and having fun, then we would love to hear from you.

You will be a critical partner to our customers, leveraging your experience with large scale cloud transformations and helping shepherd them through their stages of AWS adoption. Guiding the customer through the operational, educational, and governance aspects of a successful AWS cloud journey.

You will interface with customer and AWS leadership, driving collaboration between the other core account groups (Sales, Support, Solutions Architecture, and Professional Services), product/engineering teams, and customer teams, planning and supporting major workload migrations. You will translate strategic initiatives in the account plan into executable actions, working backwards from our customers key milestones. You will manage cadence by leading the reporting and tracking functions along the way. The execution of education plans, roadmap to business outcome alignments, Executive Briefing Sessions, and go-live events and transitions are a few items owned by the CSM that are critical to the success of our customer’s cloud journey.

You are encouraged to think big, invent and take ownership on customer challenges. You will not only bring the best of AWS/Amazon to our customers, you will proactively help solve the customer’s challenges through new ideas, tools and mechanisms.

Successful candidates will have a strong technical background, be aware of details that matter, have excellent problem-solving abilities, and be exemplary communicators both at the executive and project team level. You will be a peer leader, have the ability to gain stakeholder buy-in, negotiate and lead virtual teams. Your enterprise cloud experience and operational excellence will influence the team’s decisions, provide insight, and help drive secure and robust solutions.
You will evangelize AWS services and influence customers for adopting them. You should be passionate about delivering a great customer experience by deploying AWS solutions and driving innovation, and also be obsessed with contributing to the day-to-day management of customers’ successful migration to AWS.
Key job responsibilities

You will establish a deep understanding of your customer’s business vision, culture and processes, and evangelize AWS services and influence customers to adopt the right solution at the right time.

Customer Solution Managers (CSM) are responsible for four focus areas:
1/Accelerating AWS Adoption through Delivery and Execution
2/Identify & Align on Strategic Opportunities: CSMs work with the Customer Account team to work backwards from the customer to identify and pursue strategic cloud opportunities. These strategic cloud opportunities can include but are not limited to large-scale migrations, GenAI, data and analytics, digital innovation, high performance computing, product innovation, and business agility.
3/Customer Enablement, you will serve as the customer’s cloud journey coach and be the voice of the customer within AWS, evangelizing customer needs to AWS leadership, product, and engineering teams.
4/Implement governance structures to effectively govern both our partnership with the customer, and the customer’s adoption of AWS.

These interconnected focus areas will enable CSMs to effectively drive cloud adoption, pursue strategic growth opportunities, and empower customer success - all of which are critical to achieving the Automotive & Manufacturing IBU’s objectives. By aligning CSM activities, goals, and opportunities under these focus areas, the Automotive & Manufacturing CSM team can ensure a disciplined, customer-centric approach that maximizes business impact and revenue realization for AWS.

CSMs play a critical role supporting account teams/customers throughout the sales process, and the customer's cloud transformation journey, whilst consistently demonstrating measurable value to the customer regardless of engagement model.

CSMs are able to effectively coordinate cross-functional resources, drive disciplined project delivery, and quantify the tangible business benefits that customers realize through their cloud transformation initiatives. This holistic approach to customer engagement, coupled with the CSM's deep understanding of the Automotive & Manufacturing Industry and AWS capabilities; positions CSMs as trusted advisors who can guide customers through every stage of their cloud journey - from initial strategy and planning to migration, modernization, and ongoing optimization.

This position requires 15% - 30% travel across the calendar year to the customer.

title: Senior Product Manager, Technical, Identity
descriptionHtml:
Do you want to define the future of how hundreds of millions of Amazon customers prove who they are? AI-powered attacks are making passwords and legacy multi-factor authentication increasingly vulnerable, and our Identity team is responding by building the next generation of authentication — passkeys, digital IDs, phishing-resistant phone-number verification, and more. As a Senior Product Manager, Technical on this team, you will own the end-to-end product lifecycle for these new authentication experiences, from problem discovery through launch and optimization, across surfaces including desktop, mobile, TV, and smart-home devices.

You will combine deep customer empathy with rigorous metrics analysis to understand how customers sign in, where friction exists, and what solutions will earn their trust. You will partner with engineering, design, legal, and cross-functional stakeholders to ship experiences that protect customers while keeping interactions simple and intuitive. If you are energized by solving complex security challenges at massive scale and want your work to be felt every time a customer interacts with Amazon, we would love to hear from you.

Key job responsibilities
- Define and evolve the authentication product strategy — assess customer needs, market trends, and emerging threats to set a clear vision for passwordless and phishing-resistant experiences across your area of ownership.
- Own the product roadmap from concept to launch, prioritizing initiatives based on customer impact and business value while managing cross-functional dependencies with engineering, design, and legal teams.
- Write detailed product requirements, user stories, and success criteria; partner with designers on prototypes and with engineers on architecture reviews to ensure solutions are scalable, secure, and intuitive.
- Analyze adoption metrics, customer behavior data, and performance indicators to identify optimization opportunities, root-cause issues, and inform roadmap investments.
- Collaborate with senior leaders, partner teams, and stakeholders across the company to build alignment on new authentication initiatives and influence organization-wide priorities.

A day in the life
Your morning might start by reviewing authentication success-rate dashboards and digging into an anomaly you spotted in passkey enrollment metrics. After a design review for a new digital ID verification flow, you join your engineering team's sprint planning to refine acceptance criteria and discuss technical trade-offs. In the afternoon, you draft a product requirements document for a phishing-resistant verification feature, then meet with a partner team to align on an upcoming launch across multiple device surfaces. Between meetings, you connect with customers through usability studies and support-ticket analysis to keep your roadmap grounded in real needs.

About the team
Our Identity Services team owns one of the most highly trafficked experiences at Amazon — the moment a customer signs in. We support products like Retail, Alexa, Prime Video, and Amazon Pay across every device type, and our mission is to make authentication secure, simple, and invisible. We are dedicated to mentorship and career growth. Our team has a broad mix of experience levels, and we pair new members with one-on-one mentors and thoughtful document reviews so everyone develops into a well-rounded product manager ready to take on increasingly complex challenges.

Basic qualifications

- 5+ years of product or program management, product marketing, business development or technology experience
- Bachelor's degree
- Experience with feature delivery and tradeoffs of a product
- Experience owning/driving roadmap strategy and definition
- Experience with end to end product delivery
- Experience contributing to engineering discussions around technology decisions and strategy related to a product
- Experience managing technical products or online services
- Experience in representing and advocating for a variety of critical customers and stakeholders during executive-level prioritization and planning

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in using analytical tools, such as Tableau, Qlikview, QuickSight
- Experience in building and driving adoption of new tools

title: Software Development Engineer II, Amazon Leo
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Leo is building a global e-commerce experience for Internet Service Provider (ISP) customers, and we need a Software Development Engineer II. You will build the backend-for-frontend layer, the service that sits directly behind the customer-facing surfaces and orchestrates over the many backend systems that make satellite internet work: ordering, payments, billing, equipment and network provisioning, and support.

The job is to shape what the frontend needs, route and orchestrate requests across those systems, translate between them, and compose their responses into reliable operations the customer experience can depend on. The core of the work is integration: calling many APIs, handling partial failures gracefully, mapping between different service models, and keeping latency and reliability high across a lot of moving parts. Much of this is built zero-to-one and expanding into new countries, so you will move from ambiguous problems to working products. You will own the full development lifecycle and work closely with frontend, product, and partner service teams.

Export Control Requirement:
Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Key job responsibilities
- Design and build backend gateway APIs in Java that route and orchestrate requests across many downstream services, from concept through deployment and operation.
- Integrate with ordering, payments, billing, equipment and network provisioning, and support services: calling their APIs, translating between their models, and composing their responses.
- Handle the realities of a distributed system: partial failures, retries, timeouts, error translation, and keeping latency and reliability high across many dependencies.
- Work with product managers, frontend engineers, and partner service teams, and help the platform expand into new countries.
- Use agentic development workflows and generative AI tools to deliver faster, and improve the system with AWS native services.
- Review code, give feedback, and coach teammates on service integration patterns and well-tested code.
- Document your team's software and train new team members on how it is built, tested, and operated.

About the team
We build the e-commerce experience for a global ISP customer base at Amazon Leo. Our team owns the backend-for-frontend layer: the single API the customer-facing app talks to, and the orchestration behind it that connects to the systems provisioning and running satellite internet. We work hand in hand with the frontend team, shaping our APIs around what their experiences need. We are scaling the team and investing in AI-based development and operational workflows.

Basic qualifications

- 5+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
- 5+ years of programming using a modern programming language such as Java, C++, or C#, including object-oriented design experience
- Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field
- Experience testing back end services

Preferred qualifications

- 6+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
- 5+ years of contributing to new and current systems architecture and design (architecture, design patterns, reliability and scaling) experience
- Experience with test-driven development
- Experience with dependency injection, API modeling, and clean layering (separating API endpoints, business-logic orchestration, and downstream service clients)
- Experience building API gateway, orchestration, or backend-for-frontend services that integrate many downstream dependencies

title: Principal, Senior, Distinguished Engineer, AWS Foundational Data & Storage Services, AWS Foundational Data & Storage Services
descriptionHtml:
We are hiring Principal, Senior, and Distinguished Engineers to join AWS Foundational Data & Storage Services.


AWS Foundational Data & Storage Services is redefining how the world stores, serves, and reasons over data in the age of AI. Our vision is to make every byte of enterprise data instantly durable, infinitely scalable, and intelligent by default — so that organizations of any size can turn their data into insight and action. We pair decades of hard-won operational experience with relentless curiosity to build the foundational services the rest of the cloud is built on: object storage (Amazon S3), block storage (Amazon EBS), archival storage (Amazon S3 Glacier), analytics and database engines (Amazon Redshift, EMR, SageMaker), and the ultra-high-performance caching layers that make generative AI and analytics fast and trustworthy at enterprise scale. We're hiring Principal and Senior Principal Engineers across the org to own technical direction for some of our hardest problems: building a new cache product purpose-built for GenAI and analytics — delivering ultra-low-latency, ultra-high-throughput access to S3 data at exponential scale; setting architecture for S3 storage at the exabyte tier; and driving the engineering direction of SageMaker, Redshift, EMR, and AWS Database Services. These are deep, high-ownership systems roles — some remote-eligible, others anchored to hubs like Seattle, Irvine, and Berlin — for engineers who have led org-wide technical strategy and want to see it run in production. If you want to build systems that operate at planet scale — where durability, availability, latency, and failure-mode ownership are first-class concerns measured in eleven nines — this is the team.

What You'll Do

This is a rare chance to own and ship the foundational services the rest of the cloud is built on — not features on top of a platform, but the storage, data, and caching layers that everything else depends on, operating at a scale no one else in the industry touches. You'll architect systems that store and serve exabytes of the world's most critical data, where a single design decision ripples across hundreds of millions of customers and millions of applications.

The problems here are unlike anywhere else. How do you deliver eleven nines of durability while adding net-new capabilities to a service that already stores hundreds of trillions of objects? How do you build a new cache product that serves S3 data at ultra-low latency and ultra-high throughput for GenAI and analytics workloads growing exponentially? How do you evolve block, object, and archival storage — and the analytics and database engines on top of them — without ever compromising the durability, availability, and latency guarantees customers have bet their businesses on? These are deep systems challenges solved in production, at a scale where the usual playbooks break down. You help write the new ones.

The systems you build here don't sit in a backlog — they're load-bearing for the internet: S3, EBS, and Glacier storing the data behind modern AI and analytics; Redshift, EMR, and SageMaker turning that data into insight; and the next generation of high-performance caching making all of it fast. You'll have direct influence over technical choices, minimal layers between you and decisions, and the opportunity to define what foundational data infrastructure looks like in the AI era.

Key job responsibilities
Deliver strategic technical projects and design new storage, data, and caching systems at massive scale

Lead architecture and engineering strategy for foundational services across S3, EBS, Glacier, and the analytics and database layer (Redshift, EMR, SageMaker, AWS Database Services)

Mentor and guide engineers while solving the hardest durability, availability, and latency problems hands-on

Work cross-functionally with Principal Engineers and teams across AWS Foundational Data & Storage Services

Scout and recruit top technical talent, actively growing the engineering community

Drive a strong engineering excellence and operational culture across all services and teams

Shape technical direction for systems where correctness, durability, and failure-mode ownership are first-class, measured in eleven nines

Balance deep systems expertise with strong analytical skills to make informed architectural decisions at scale

Basic qualifications

-10+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
-Knowledge of object-oriented design, data structures, and algorithms

Preferred qualifications

descriptionHtml:

As a Systems Development Engineer on EC2 Core Platforms Engineering, you'll lead the technical direction for how we launch new compute platforms, keep the core fleet healthy at massive scale, and automate the way we build, working at the seam between hardware and software.

We own the quality, performance, and reliability of the platforms that host EC2 instances, from lab bring-up through general availability. You'll lead the bring-up and validation of new EC2 server platforms, driving the technical plan across Nitro firmware, operating systems, and provisioning. You'll also set the approach for diagnosing and reducing failures across the core fleet, working to eliminate whole classes of failure rather than individual instances. A big part of the role is defining the architecture for the automation, including AI-driven tooling, that makes platform launches faster, safer, and more repeatable, and driving its adoption across the team and our partners.

You'll partner with hardware engineering, Annapurna, and the Nitro component teams, working on some of the largest compute fleets in the world, where a single improvement in reliability or build automation compounds across millions of hosts. Key job responsibilities

descriptionHtml:

As AWS continues its global expansion, we are making significant investments in energy procurement to ensure our data centers operate reliably, sustainably, and at scale. We take pride in building the right controllership from day one — and that means hiring specialists who raise the bar.

In support of AWS's continued growth to build out and energize data centers, we are seeking an ASC 815 subject matter expert with strong expertise in derivative identification, valuation, and accounting within the power and utility industry to join our Energy Accounting team.

This role is a key member of the Energy Accounting team, supporting technical evaluations for derivative accounting. Operating in an environment where strategy may not be fully defined, the individual will use expertise and judgment to select the right stakeholders, determine goals, and drive resolution of complex accounting questions. The individual will:
- Support the evaluation of complex power purchase and energy supply agreements for derivative features under ASC 815
- Identify embedded and freestanding derivative features within energy contracts and clearly articulate which provisions give rise to derivative accounting
- Propose non-derivative structuring alternatives to business stakeholders — proactively advising on contract terms that avoid derivative classification or qualify for the Normal Purchases and Normal Sales (NPNS) scope exception
- Partner with business stakeholders and customers during contract negotiation to provide real-time ASC 815 guidance, ensuring accounting implications are understood and addressed before execution
- Assess NPNS scope exception eligibility, including documentation of designation, probability of physical delivery, and evaluation of optionality and penalty provisions
- Evaluate regulatory approval considerations under ASC 815-10-15-59(e) and their impact on derivative classification


Key job responsibilities
- Serve as a member of the Energy Accounting team, supporting the derivative assessment process for new and modified energy agreements
- Identify embedded derivative features within host contracts and determine bifurcation requirements
- Evaluate contracts for the NPNS scope exception, including documentation of physical delivery probability, optionality analysis, and penalty term assessment under ASC 440
- Assess regulatory approval requirements and their implications for derivative classification
- Partner with business and finance stakeholders during the negotiation of power purchase and energy supply agreements, providing proactive ASC 815 guidance
- Work directly with stakeholders and counterparties to understand contract terms and propose structuring alternatives that achieve business objectives while managing accounting complexity
- Propose non-derivative alternatives — advise on contract modifications, structuring options, and term adjustments that avoid derivative classification or enable NPNS election
- Draft technical GAAP accounting position papers addressing complex topics, including derivatives/financial instruments (ASC 815), fair value measurement (ASC 820), leasing (ASC 842), consolidation (ASC 810), and commitments (ASC 440), consulting with accounting policy as appropriate
- Research and document complex accounting concepts in clear, concise, and unambiguous language that critically supports proposed conclusions
- Continuously reevaluate existing accounting positions to ensure consistency with the evolving business and regulatory environment
- Support the period-end close process by ensuring accurate and timely completion of all derivative-related accounting entries, reconciliations, and analytical reviews
- Implement, maintain, and test internal controls over derivative identification, measurement, and reporting processes
- Collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders to produce transaction flows and implement simplification projects
- Identify, validate, and lead opportunities for standardization of processes across teams
- Drive productivity by simplifying processes, engaging emerging technology, and/or implementing innovative solutions

Basic qualifications

- 7+ years of finance technology, forecast & budgeting, or other finance-focused competency experience
- 12+ years of finance, accounting, or related analytical field experience
- Experience with Tableau, Python, SQB, Quicksight, Cognos or or other BI packages

Preferred qualifications

- MBA, or CPA
- Knowledge of one or multiple accounting frameworks (including US GAAP, IFRS, or local GAAP frameworks), with the ability to apply them in day-to-day financial activities
- Experience in a leadership position managing finance, accounting and operational processes
- Experience working cross-functionally with a wide breadth of stakeholders, users, engineers, and leaders to generate buy-in

title: Sr Pre-Construction Manager, GES NA, Design and Construction
descriptionHtml:
As a Senior Preconstruction Manager within Global Engineering Services (GES) North America (NA) Design & Construction (D&C), you are Amazon's senior owner's representative during the preconstruction phase — responsible for autonomously managing complex, cross-functional industrial building projects from site selection through design completion, permitting, and contract execution across your assigned region. Preconstruction services refers to the planning of a construction project before actual construction begins.

You will partner with internal and external stakeholders to ensure scope, budget, and schedule definition are established, including timely receipt of building and site permits. You are responsible as the senior project manager to lead planning, design, and preconstruction projects — including new built-to-suit industrial buildings, tenant improvements, extensions of existing facilities, and renovation projects — serving major business customers within your region.

You execute deliverables with limited oversight, using advanced professional concepts to resolve complex issues in creative and effective ways. You deliver a mix of tactical and strategic initiatives (60% tactical / 40% strategic) that impact multiple teams and/or geographies in support of significant business objectives. You own project budgets, oversee design management, select external vendor partners, and lead project procurement — and you are accountable for the full performance of your external project teams. You show excellent judgment when driving project escalations and make difficult trade-off decisions between short-term and long-term needs, defending those decisions to internal stakeholders.

Beyond project delivery, you guide preconstruction managers in best practices in stakeholder management and project delivery, contribute to developing Amazon's internal and external construction networks, and are learning to force multiply — elevating the performance of the teams and partners around you. You write effective narratives and present complex decisions and trade-offs to Directors and VPs. You actively recruit, mentor, and develop other preconstruction managers.

This role requires 60% regional travel on a yearly basis. When not traveling, you must have availability to work from a corporate office. Candidates should either live near or be willing to relocate within a reasonable commuting distance of one of the corporate office locations listed. Relocation assistance may be provided.

Key job responsibilities
Safety & Compliance
- Own and enforce Amazon's safety programs and standards across all internal and external project teams during the planning and preconstruction phases; set the standard for safety culture on complex projects
- Lead coordination with Authorities Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) to ensure regulatory compliance, smooth permitting execution, and timely approvals
- Review noise, traffic, and environmental studies; understand and apply zoning, planning, fire code, and building code requirements for assigned projects
- Proactively identify and eliminate compliance risks before they become project roadblocks

Preconstruction & Project Management
- Autonomously manage complex, cross-functional industrial preconstruction projects from site selection through design completion, permitting, and contract execution; contribute to significantly complex projects as part of a team
- Lead site selection and validation, scope development, and design management — overseeing design teams in developing site plans and composite floor plans in compliance with Amazon's design standards and operational requirements
- Oversee design management end-to-end, including design evaluations, design conformance reviews, and value engineering assessments
- Manage multiple concurrent large industrial projects across various locations simultaneously, leading a region or program with limited management oversight
- Keep scope under control and accelerate progress by driving crisp, timely decisions, identifying and clearing blockers, and managing escalations with excellent judgment
- Identify and resolve upstream issues proactively to support a clean handoff to the Construction Manager; remain a key support resource and authority on project issues for the construction team throughout the project lifecycle
- Monitor project performance metrics, anticipate roadblocks and risks, manage escalations, and ensure corrective actions are taken
- Resolve complex issues and find a path forward in difficult situations; make and defend trade-off decisions between short-term and long-term needs
- Assess project performance through Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) for safety, quality, cost, schedule, and sustainability; deliver solutions that meet standards for customer satisfaction, efficiency, stability, and operational excellence
- Maintain a broad perspective — understand how project components drive successful programs, business portfolios, and not just individual projects

Budget, Schedule & Contract Management
- Own project budgets and oversee spend approvals across all assigned preconstruction projects
- Perform conceptual estimating and pricing reviews for scope inclusions and exclusions; lead negotiations on the cost of work with developers, general contractors, and design consultants
- Lead external partner selection, contract negotiations, and project procurement functions; ensure contracts are fit for purpose, cost-effective, and incorporate appropriate service level agreements
- Review and analyze design and construction contracts, related exhibits, and lease agreements; provide detailed analysis and approvals of technical matters and site-specific deal structures and terms
- Review additional reports including noise and traffic studies and environmental assessments
- Partner with the Transaction team and developers to optimize schedule and strategy for entitlements and long-lead procurement
- Identify and solve factors that may impede a successful permitted project handover to Amazon stakeholders; make trade-offs between short-term and long-term needs

Stakeholder & Vendor Management
- Work with internal and external teams — including Real Estate, Design Engineering, Entitlements, Construction, Finance, Launch/Startup, architects, engineers, permitting agencies, developers, and landlords — to secure resources, scope infrastructure builds, set priorities and milestones, and drive delivery to meet deadlines
- Drive results through communicating, weighing risks, making decisions, leading, and influencing; serve as an authority on project issues across diverse audiences
- Select external vendor partners and manage delivery from external service partners to drive delivery with efficient use of resources and technology
- Lead large cross-functional teams to complete preconstruction projects; skillfully motivate and focus people of all levels to deliver complex projects
- Drive significant communication across departments, from front-line to executive-level managers; achieve high-level alignment and consensus with internal and external stakeholders across diverse teams (legal, regulatory, operations, engineering, finance, external industry groups)
- Act as the primary escalation point for project team members; own and track issues to ensure they are addressed, documented, and resolved
- Support crucial relationships and lead negotiations of agreements with customers, suppliers, and external partners
- Contribute to developing Amazon's internal and external construction networks

Communication & Reporting
- Write effective narratives and present complex decisions, trade-offs, and potential solutions to Directors and VPs
- Translate technical documents and information into end-to-end stories providing detailed risk analysis for leaders and customers
- Communicate budgets, schedules, project status, and priorities clearly to internal teams and external partners
- Run preconstruction meetings effectively — putting the right people in the room, driving detailed discussions, and achieving high-level alignment and consensus
- Utilize Amazon's information systems to record and update schedule, budget, and other key project developments
- Represent Amazon's interests in weekly Architect, Owner, and Contractor (AOC) meetings; provide input on root causes and corrective actions

Process Improvement, Best Practices & People Development
- Drive continuous improvement and create sustainable, repeatable processes and playbooks for the team and region
- Contribute to process improvement ideas; develop tools and procedures that improve project efficiency and delivery across the organization
- Drive efficiencies, streamline workflows, and mitigate excess process and risk
- Learn to force multiply — drive adoption of best practices and elevate the performance of teams and partners
- Recommend improvements to the way projects are scoped, permitted, and executed across the region or organization
- Guide preconstruction managers in best practices in stakeholder management and project delivery; frequently serve as an expert resource on complicated technical, jurisdictional, or regulatory issues
- Actively recruit, mentor, and develop other preconstruction managers within your organization and location
- Assist leadership in building internal and external talent networks
- Participate in the interview process and help train new team members
- Support Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion as fundamentally right for all employees by fostering a culture where inclusion is the norm
- Insist on the highest standards from self and others; drive accountability for results

A day in the life
Each day, you represent GES NA Design & Construction as Amazon's senior owner during the preconstruction phase — executing autonomously, leading with no authority, and influencing the best project decisions across your region. You are 60% tactical and 40% strategic, planning your projects with limited management oversight and frequently called upon as an expert resource. Your day may include:
- Leading design reviews and providing strategic direction to architects, engineers, and design consultants on complex projects
- Negotiating contract terms with developers, general contractors, and consultants while driving adherence to schedules and budgets
- Presenting project status, risks, and trade-off decisions to senior leadership (Directors and VPs)
- Coordinating with AHJ on permitting status, zoning, fire code, and building code requirements
- Monitoring project performance metrics and driving corrective actions with external partners
- Partnering with Real Estate and Transaction teams on entitlement strategy and long-lead procurement
- Mentoring PCMs and contributing to team development and best practices
- Developing or updating process playbooks based on lessons learned from current projects
- Leveraging project management principles and analytics to identify, avoid, or correct issues before they become roadblocks

About the team
At Amazon, the GES North America Design & Construction team is a diverse group of engineers, construction managers, and preconstruction professionals who deliver the physical infrastructure behind Amazon's logistics network. We are employee owners who take pride in delivering high-quality, innovative facilities — on time and on budget — for our internal customers and the communities we serve. We are committed to being Earth's best employer and to building a more sustainable future through every project we deliver.

Basic qualifications

- 7+ years of project management, real estate development, architecture/design experience
- Bachelor's degree in Architecture, Construction Management, Engineering, or a related field
- 7+ years of experience as an Architect, Engineer, Construction Manager, Development Manager, Owner's Project Management Representative, or in a related commercial development or construction discipline
- 7+ years of project management experience from design phase through implementation and operation, including negotiating construction, procurement, and labor contracts
- Experience within packaging, processing, or logistical facilities with complex equipment, or comparable experience
- Position includes travel up to 60% (Nationwide). Travel involves air travel to regional airports and driving to site locations. A valid driver's license is required due to project assignments in areas with limited public transportation and rideshare options.

Preferred qualifications

- Advanced degree or certification in Architecture, Engineering, Construction Management, or Business Administration
- Experience operating across at least two disciplines within the construction industry (e.g., General Contracting, Owner's Representation, Commercial Development, Engineering & Design, or Owner's Project Management)
- Demonstrated capability in planning, design review, implementation, and project management/control of new structures and enhancement of existing facilities
- Experience managing multi-disciplinary design incorporating industrial automation, robotics, or similar
- Strong influencing and negotiating skills; demonstrated ability to lead with no authority and build consensus across diverse stakeholder groups
- Demonstrated success communicating complex decisions and trade-offs to senior leadership (Director/VP level)
- Experience developing and implementing preconstruction processes, playbooks, or best practice frameworks
- Experience mentoring and developing junior preconstruction professionals
- Knowledge of Building Information Modeling (BIM)
- CMIT/CMAA or PMP certification or equivalent

title: Pre-Construction Manager, GES NA, Design and Construction
descriptionHtml:
As a Preconstruction Manager within Global Engineering Services (GES) North America (NA) Design & Construction (D&C), you are Amazon's owner's representative during the preconstruction phase — responsible for independently managing difficult, cross-functional industrial building projects from site selection through design completion, permitting, and contract execution across your assigned region. Preconstruction services refers to the planning of a construction project before actual construction begins.

You will partner with internal and external stakeholders to ensure scope, budget, and schedule definition are established, including timely receipt of building and site permits. You are responsible as the project manager to lead planning, design, and preconstruction projects — including new built-to-suit industrial buildings, tenant improvements, extensions of existing facilities, and renovation projects — supporting Amazon's logistics network infrastructure.

You work independently within your assigned region, using your knowledge of construction and project management concepts to decide which actions to take to complete projects, and seeking guidance as needed on strategic components. You are tactical with some strategic components, utilizing well-defined processes and best practices to facilitate delivery of high-quality results. You make trade-offs between time, quality, and resources to keep projects on track.

Key competencies of this position include ensuring that contracted resources deliver work product in support of project durations, permitting, key performance indicators (KPIs), and quality documentation; managing project teams (developers, design engineers, professional consultants); influencing internal teams (Design Engineering, Amazon Robotics); contract management governance; conceptual estimating and budget oversight; and managing multiple large industrial projects in various locations simultaneously. Translating technical documents and information into clear, concise narratives with detailed risk analysis for leaders and customers is essential.

This opportunity combines construction engineering, planning, project management, real estate development, design validation, site visits, understanding of local building and fire code issues, utilities, sustainability, multi-disciplinary design management, and contract management. The Preconstruction Manager is responsible for the planning and design of scope, budget, and schedule prior to handing off to the Construction Manager — focusing on taking ownership to resolve upstream issues and supporting the construction team throughout the process.

This role requires 60% regional travel on a yearly basis. When not traveling, you must have availability to work from a corporate office. Candidates should either live near or be willing to relocate within a reasonable commuting distance of one of the corporate office locations listed. Relocation assistance may be provided.


Key job responsibilities
Safety & Compliance
- Supervise the implementation and management of Amazon's safety programs and standards across all internal and external project teams during the planning and preconstruction phases of a project
- Interface and coordinate with Authorities Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) to ensure regulatory compliance, smooth permitting execution, and timely approvals
- Review noise, traffic, and environmental studies; understand zoning, planning, fire code, and building code requirements for assigned projects

Preconstruction & Project Management
- Independently manage difficult, cross-functional industrial preconstruction projects from site selection through design completion, permitting, and contract execution
- Lead site selection and validation, scope development, and design management — coordinating with design teams to develop site plans and composite floor plans in compliance with Amazon's design standards and operational requirements
- Manage multiple concurrent large industrial projects across various locations simultaneously
- Keep scope under control and accelerate progress by driving crisp, timely decisions, identifying and clearing blockers, and escalating appropriately
- Identify and resolve upstream issues proactively to support a clean handoff to the Construction Manager; remain a key support resource for the construction team throughout the project lifecycle
- Assess project performance through Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) for safety, quality, cost, schedule, and sustainability
- Minimize disruptions and proactively mitigate risks; plan ahead to prevent problems before they happen

Budget, Schedule & Contract Management
- Develop and manage project budgets and costs; own comprehensive schedule management and cashflow forecasting across assigned preconstruction projects
- Perform conceptual estimating and pricing reviews for scope inclusions and exclusions; negotiate the cost of work with developers, general contractors, and design consultants
- Contribute to the selection of external vendor partners and manage vendor procurement; oversee professional service providers to ensure their skills and competencies meet project requirements
- Review and analyze design and construction contracts, related exhibits, and lease agreements; provide detailed analysis of technical matters and site-specific deal structures and terms
- Partner with the Transaction team and developers to optimize schedule and strategy for entitlements and long-lead procurement
- Identify and solve factors that may impede a successful permitted project handover to Amazon stakeholders; make trade-offs between time, quality, and resources

Stakeholder & Vendor Management
- Work with internal and external teams — including Real Estate, Design Engineering, Entitlements, Construction, Finance, Launch/Startup, architects, engineers, permitting agencies, developers, and landlords — to secure resources, scope infrastructure builds, set priorities and milestones, and drive delivery to meet deadlines
- Drive results through communicating, weighing risks, making decisions, leading, and influencing; competently represent project and technical information to diverse audiences
- Maintain good working relationships with stakeholders and vendors; lead constructive dialogue to resolve and prevent project issues
- Act as the primary escalation point for project team members; own and track issues to ensure they are addressed, documented, and resolved

Communication & Reporting
- Prepare and present project status and risk reports; provide clear, concise summaries for projects under your ownership to leadership and management teams
- Translate technical documents and information into end-to-end narratives with detailed risk analysis for leaders and customers
- Run preconstruction meetings effectively — putting the right people in the room, checking progress, and driving high-level alignment and consensus
- Communicate budgets, schedules, project status, and priorities clearly to internal teams and external partners; trusted to present decisions to leaders up to 2-3 tiers above level
- Utilize Amazon's information systems to record and update schedule, budget, and other key project developments
- Represent Amazon's interests in weekly Architect, Owner, and Contractor (AOC) meetings; provide input on root causes and corrective actions

Process Improvement & Innovation
- Optimize preconstruction processes and implement improvements in procedures and playbooks to improve project efficiency and delivery
- Look for opportunities to improve operational excellence and influence the team to determine where to iterate and make improvements
- Seek sustainable, environmentally responsible solutions throughout the preconstruction process in alignment with Amazon's building practices
- Adapt to constant change and innovation; find adaptable solutions for an evolving business

A day in the life
Each day, you represent GES NA Design & Construction as Amazon's owner during the preconstruction phase — navigating uncertainty, proactively unblocking project barriers, and influencing the best project decisions. You are tactical with some strategic components, working independently and interacting with leadership to resolve issues. Your day may include:
- Coordinating with architects, engineers, and design consultants on design document development, scope changes, and project status
- Reviewing site plans, composite floor plans, and design documents for compliance with Amazon's standards and operational requirements
- Negotiating contract terms with developers, contractors, and consultants while driving adherence to schedules and budgets
- Coordinating with AHJ on permitting status, zoning, fire code, and building code requirements
- Preparing and presenting project status and risk reports for leadership
- Partnering with Real Estate and Transaction teams on entitlement strategy and long-lead procurement
- Providing estimating support, interpreting drawings, contributing to budgets, and reviewing lease exhibits
- Updating Amazon's project management systems with current budget, schedule, and status information
- Supporting the Construction Manager on active construction projects with preconstruction expertise

About the team
At Amazon, the GES North America Design & Construction team is a diverse group of engineers, construction managers, and preconstruction professionals who deliver the physical infrastructure behind Amazon's logistics network. We are employee owners who take pride in delivering high-quality, innovative facilities — on time and on budget — for our internal customers and the communities we serve. We are committed to being Earth's best employer and to building a more sustainable future through every project we deliver.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Architecture, Construction Management, Engineering, or a related field
- 5+ years of experience as an Architect, Engineer, Construction Manager, Development Manager, Owner's Project Management Representative, or in a related commercial development or construction discipline
- 5+ years of project management experience from design phase through implementation and operation, including negotiating construction, procurement, and labor contracts
- Experience within packaging, processing, or logistical facilities with complex equipment, or comparable experience
- Position includes travel up to 60% (Nationwide). Travel involves air travel to regional airports and driving to site locations. A valid driver's license is required due to project assignments in areas with limited public transportation and rideshare options.

Preferred qualifications

- Advanced degree or certification in Architecture, Engineering, Construction Management, or Business Administration
- Experience operating across at least two disciplines within the construction industry (e.g., General Contracting, Owner's Representation, Commercial Development, Engineering & Design, or Owner's Project Management)
- Demonstrated capability in planning, design review, implementation, and project management/control of new structures and enhancement of existing facilities
- Experience managing multi-disciplinary design incorporating industrial automation, robotics, or similar
- Strong influencing and negotiating skills
- Demonstrated success communicating project requirements to diverse audiences (e.g., senior management, peers, fire marshals, utility providers, public officials, vendors)
- Knowledge of Building Information Modeling (BIM)
- CMIT/CMAA or PMP certification or equivalent

title: Pre-Construction Manager, GES NA, Design and Construction
descriptionHtml:
As a Preconstruction Manager within Global Engineering Services (GES) North America (NA) Design & Construction (D&C), you are Amazon's owner's representative during the preconstruction phase — responsible for independently managing difficult, cross-functional industrial building projects from site selection through design completion, permitting, and contract execution across your assigned region. Preconstruction services refers to the planning of a construction project before actual construction begins.

You will partner with internal and external stakeholders to ensure scope, budget, and schedule definition are established, including timely receipt of building and site permits. You are responsible as the project manager to lead planning, design, and preconstruction projects — including new built-to-suit industrial buildings, tenant improvements, extensions of existing facilities, and renovation projects — supporting Amazon's logistics network infrastructure.

You work independently within your assigned region, using your knowledge of construction and project management concepts to decide which actions to take to complete projects, and seeking guidance as needed on strategic components. You are tactical with some strategic components, utilizing well-defined processes and best practices to facilitate delivery of high-quality results. You make trade-offs between time, quality, and resources to keep projects on track.

Key competencies of this position include ensuring that contracted resources deliver work product in support of project durations, permitting, key performance indicators (KPIs), and quality documentation; managing project teams (developers, design engineers, professional consultants); influencing internal teams (Design Engineering, Amazon Robotics); contract management governance; conceptual estimating and budget oversight; and managing multiple large industrial projects in various locations simultaneously. Translating technical documents and information into clear, concise narratives with detailed risk analysis for leaders and customers is essential.

This opportunity combines construction engineering, planning, project management, real estate development, design validation, site visits, understanding of local building and fire code issues, utilities, sustainability, multi-disciplinary design management, and contract management. The Preconstruction Manager is responsible for the planning and design of scope, budget, and schedule prior to handing off to the Construction Manager — focusing on taking ownership to resolve upstream issues and supporting the construction team throughout the process.

This role requires 60% regional travel on a yearly basis. When not traveling, you must have availability to work from a corporate office. Candidates should either live near or be willing to relocate within a reasonable commuting distance of one of the corporate office locations listed. Relocation assistance may be provided.


Key job responsibilities
Safety & Compliance
- Supervise the implementation and management of Amazon's safety programs and standards across all internal and external project teams during the planning and preconstruction phases of a project
- Interface and coordinate with Authorities Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) to ensure regulatory compliance, smooth permitting execution, and timely approvals
- Review noise, traffic, and environmental studies; understand zoning, planning, fire code, and building code requirements for assigned projects

Preconstruction & Project Management
- Independently manage difficult, cross-functional industrial preconstruction projects from site selection through design completion, permitting, and contract execution
- Lead site selection and validation, scope development, and design management — coordinating with design teams to develop site plans and composite floor plans in compliance with Amazon's design standards and operational requirements
- Manage multiple concurrent large industrial projects across various locations simultaneously
- Keep scope under control and accelerate progress by driving crisp, timely decisions, identifying and clearing blockers, and escalating appropriately
- Identify and resolve upstream issues proactively to support a clean handoff to the Construction Manager; remain a key support resource for the construction team throughout the project lifecycle
- Assess project performance through Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) for safety, quality, cost, schedule, and sustainability
- Minimize disruptions and proactively mitigate risks; plan ahead to prevent problems before they happen

Budget, Schedule & Contract Management
- Develop and manage project budgets and costs; own comprehensive schedule management and cashflow forecasting across assigned preconstruction projects
- Perform conceptual estimating and pricing reviews for scope inclusions and exclusions; negotiate the cost of work with developers, general contractors, and design consultants
- Contribute to the selection of external vendor partners and manage vendor procurement; oversee professional service providers to ensure their skills and competencies meet project requirements
- Review and analyze design and construction contracts, related exhibits, and lease agreements; provide detailed analysis of technical matters and site-specific deal structures and terms
- Partner with the Transaction team and developers to optimize schedule and strategy for entitlements and long-lead procurement
- Identify and solve factors that may impede a successful permitted project handover to Amazon stakeholders; make trade-offs between time, quality, and resources

Stakeholder & Vendor Management
- Work with internal and external teams — including Real Estate, Design Engineering, Entitlements, Construction, Finance, Launch/Startup, architects, engineers, permitting agencies, developers, and landlords — to secure resources, scope infrastructure builds, set priorities and milestones, and drive delivery to meet deadlines
- Drive results through communicating, weighing risks, making decisions, leading, and influencing; competently represent project and technical information to diverse audiences
- Maintain good working relationships with stakeholders and vendors; lead constructive dialogue to resolve and prevent project issues
- Act as the primary escalation point for project team members; own and track issues to ensure they are addressed, documented, and resolved

Communication & Reporting
- Prepare and present project status and risk reports; provide clear, concise summaries for projects under your ownership to leadership and management teams
- Translate technical documents and information into end-to-end narratives with detailed risk analysis for leaders and customers
- Run preconstruction meetings effectively — putting the right people in the room, checking progress, and driving high-level alignment and consensus
- Communicate budgets, schedules, project status, and priorities clearly to internal teams and external partners; trusted to present decisions to leaders up to 2-3 tiers above level
- Utilize Amazon's information systems to record and update schedule, budget, and other key project developments
- Represent Amazon's interests in weekly Architect, Owner, and Contractor (AOC) meetings; provide input on root causes and corrective actions

Process Improvement & Innovation
- Optimize preconstruction processes and implement improvements in procedures and playbooks to improve project efficiency and delivery
- Look for opportunities to improve operational excellence and influence the team to determine where to iterate and make improvements
- Seek sustainable, environmentally responsible solutions throughout the preconstruction process in alignment with Amazon's building practices
- Adapt to constant change and innovation; find adaptable solutions for an evolving business

A day in the life
Each day, you represent GES NA Design & Construction as Amazon's owner during the preconstruction phase — navigating uncertainty, proactively unblocking project barriers, and influencing the best project decisions. You are tactical with some strategic components, working independently and interacting with leadership to resolve issues. Your day may include:
- Coordinating with architects, engineers, and design consultants on design document development, scope changes, and project status
- Reviewing site plans, composite floor plans, and design documents for compliance with Amazon's standards and operational requirements
- Negotiating contract terms with developers, contractors, and consultants while driving adherence to schedules and budgets
- Coordinating with AHJ on permitting status, zoning, fire code, and building code requirements
- Preparing and presenting project status and risk reports for leadership
- Partnering with Real Estate and Transaction teams on entitlement strategy and long-lead procurement
- Providing estimating support, interpreting drawings, contributing to budgets, and reviewing lease exhibits
- Updating Amazon's project management systems with current budget, schedule, and status information
- Supporting the Construction Manager on active construction projects with preconstruction expertise

About the team
At Amazon, the GES North America Design & Construction team is a diverse group of engineers, construction managers, and preconstruction professionals who deliver the physical infrastructure behind Amazon's logistics network. We are employee owners who take pride in delivering high-quality, innovative facilities — on time and on budget — for our internal customers and the communities we serve. We are committed to being Earth's best employer and to building a more sustainable future through every project we deliver.

- Bachelor's degree in Architecture, Construction Management, Engineering, or a related field
- 5+ years of experience as an Architect, Engineer, Construction Manager, Development Manager, Owner's Project Management Representative, or in a related commercial development or construction discipline
- 5+ years of project management experience from design phase through implementation and operation, including negotiating construction, procurement, and labor contracts
- Experience within packaging, processing, or logistical facilities with complex equipment, or comparable experience
- Position includes travel up to 60% (Nationwide). Travel involves air travel to regional airports and driving to site locations. A valid driver's license is required due to project assignments in areas with limited public transportation and rideshare options.

title: Senior Principal Engineer , AWS Billing
descriptionHtml:
How cloud customers experience billing — from the pricing they see, to the costs they manage, to the bills they pay — is foundational to how they trust and grow with AWS. Today, that experience is ready for a transformation: one that brings the commercial simplicity of amazon.com to the cloud, in near real-time, across every customer segment. Are you ready to define the technical strategy that makes that possible?



About the Team

AWS Billing is responsible for processing all AWS revenue — computing millions of bills daily and reliably handling billions of usage records per second across every AWS service, customer, and partner worldwide. Our systems ensure that financial data is fully auditable, accurate, and timely, while simultaneously adapting to evolving pricing models, contract structures, and regulatory environments.

We are at an inflection point. Small customers need pricing simplicity, cost predictability, and real-time visibility into their usage — so they can use AWS without fear of surprise costs. Large enterprise and government customers need commercial flexibility, configurable pricing, and democratized cost management. New opportunities are emerging to externalize our billing and pricing capabilities as a platform, and to support new pricing models that give AWS the commercial agility required to stay competitive. Increasingly, the systems we build will also need to serve autonomous agents interacting with billing, pricing, and cost data in fundamentally different ways than humans do today. These challenges are not met well by any cloud provider today, so there is a lot to invent.

Key job responsibilities

Define and own the multi-year technical strategy for billing architecture, partnering with engineering leaders and scientists across the organization to guide the next generation of billing systems — more composable, more adaptable, and built to evolve at the velocity the business requires.
Drive architectural decisions that span multiple organizations across AWS service teams, Marketplace, Sales, and Finance, ensuring alignment on how billing systems transform from batch-oriented financial processing into a real-time platform.
Provide technical guidance across billing and commerce teams, increasing productivity and effectiveness through deep knowledge of distributed systems, real-time processing, enterprise architecture, and generative AI technology.
Ensure the quality of architecture and design across billing systems by decomposing complex problems into straightforward, scalable solutions, with a focus on performance optimization and engineering practices that enable systems to scale seamlessly.
Mentor engineers and the broader community on advanced distributed systems challenges, helping develop technical talent across billing engineering teams while maintaining a pragmatic focus on business outcomes.


A day in the life
You will balance understanding the nuances of how customers — from startups to the world's largest enterprises — interact with AWS billing and cost management, while shaping the architectural vision that makes those experiences seamless. On any given day, you may lead a design review for a next-generation pricing engine, align with partner teams on integration patterns for a new AWS service launch, or work hands-on with engineers to prototype a real-time billing pipeline. You will navigate competing stakeholder priorities while maintaining a high bar for accuracy, performance, operational resilience, and system efficiency. You will also play a key role in shaping how the engineering organization leverages AI to accelerate development, testing, and delivery across the billing platform.

Basic qualifications


Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field
15+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
Experience designing, building, and operating large-scale distributed systems in a multi-tiered, service-oriented environment
Experience defining and driving multi-year technical strategy across multiple engineering teams

Preferred qualifications


Master's degree or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field
Experience with high-volume data processing systems, real-time computation, or financial/billing systems at scale
Experience modeling complex pricing, contractual, or regulatory business rules in software
Familiarity with generative AI technologies and their application to software development workflows
Experience influencing technical direction across organizational boundaries without direct authority
