title: Instandhaltungstechniker:in Elektrotechnik
descriptionHtml:
Das Wartungs- und Instandhaltungsteam (Reliability Maintenance Engineering Team oder RME-Team) ist für unseren Betrieb von fundamentaler Bedeutung – es sorgt dafür, dass unsere technischen Systeme und Anlagen laufend funktionieren. Als Instandhaltungstechniker:in bist Du für die Wartung und Instandhaltung unserer förder- und haustechnischen Anlagen sowie Produktionsanlagen zuständig. Du hilfst, die höchsten Sicherheitsstandards im Arbeitsschutz zu gewährleisten und Maschinenausfallzeiten zu verhindern. Unser technisches Team stellt eine hohe Verfügbarkeit der technischen Anlagen sicher und verbessert die Qualität unserer Geräte.

Key job responsibilities
- Ausführung präventiver Wartungsmaßnahmen an einer breiten Vielfalt von Geräten an unseren Standorten
- Durchführung von Reparaturen und Fehlerdiagnosen
- Verwendung neuester Tools zur Maximierung der Geräteeffektivität
- Einhaltung aller Arbeitsschutzrichtlinien und -praktiken
- Unterstützung der Entwicklung und des beruflichen Fortschritts von Auszubildenden am Standort
- Arbeit an Projekten zur kontinuierlichen Verbesserung und Einführung von Best Practices an verschiedenen EU-Standorten

A day in the life
Als Instandhaltungstechniker:in bist Du vor Ort in einem unserer Logistikzentren tätig, um schnell auf technische Störungen reagieren zu können. Du führst eine Reihe geplanter präventiver Wartungsmaßnahmen an Geräten durch, um für ihren sicheren Betrieb zu sorgen.

Außerdem reagierst Du als Instandhaltungstechniker:in unverzüglich auf Störungen und Ausfälle. Du untersuchst die Ursachen, findest so schnell wie möglich Lösungen und wendest sie an. Zudem machst Du Vorschläge für langfristige Verbesserungen.

In Zusammenarbeit mit leitenden Kolleg:innen nimmst Du tägliche Wartungsaufgaben wahr und kommunizierst mit Dienstleistern, falls Du externe Expertise benötigst. Du arbeitest in rotierenden Schichten, damit wir rund um die Uhr unsere Standorte unterstützen – und dafür sorgen, dass Amazon weiterhin in dem Tempo liefern kann, für das wir bekannt sind.

About the team
Mit der Erfüllung unserer Kundenbestellungen (Customer Fulfillment oder CF) fing für Amazon alles an. Das Customer Fulfillment Team hat sich mittlerweile von einem Team von Buchhändler:innen hin zu einem hocherfahrenen globalen Team gewandelt, das täglich mehr als 1,5 Millionen Bestellungen bearbeitet. Das Team bildet die Grundlage unseres Geschäfts und hat uns bei der Verbreiterung in neue Regionen und Dienstleistungen geholfen. Mithilfe aufkommender Technologie sind wir stetig auf der Suche nach Möglichkeiten, eine größere und bessere Produktauswahl anzubieten – die schnell und erschwinglich geliefert wird.
Die CF-Teammitglieder sorgen als allererste dafür, dass unsere Kund:innen ihre Bestellungen mit der Geschwindigkeit erhalten, für die wir bekannt sind. Wir arbeiten in Fulfillment-Centern, die das Herzstück von Amazons dynamischem Betriebsnetz bilden. Unsere Fullfilment-Center werden manchmal auch als die „erste Meile“ (First Mile) bezeichnet – hier starten die meisten Amazon-Pakete ihren Versandweg. Wir unterstützen die Verwaltung eines dynamischen Bestands und ermöglichen schnelle Zustellungen rund um die Uhr.
In unseren Fulfillment-Centern sind vielfältige Mitarbeitergruppen beschäftigt. Es gibt zahlreiche Möglichkeiten für Menschen mit den verschiedensten Fähigkeiten. Einige von uns arbeiten mit physischen Produkten. Andere analysieren Daten und helfen unternehmensweit dabei, intelligente Entscheidungen zu treffen.

- Abgeschlossene elektrotechnische Berufsausbildung, anerkannt durch die Industrie- und Handelskammer (IHK) oder Handwerkskammer (HWK) oder Nachweis eines erfolgreich abgeschlossen Hochschulstudium im Ingenieurwissenschaftlichen Bereich (Maschinenbau / Elektrotechnik oder artverwandt) einer deutschen Hochschule oder anerkannte ausländische Hochschulabschlüsse (BA, B. Sc., MA, M. Sc., Dipl.-Ing.)

- Fortgeschrittene Deutschkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift

- Erfahrung in der Arbeit mit Druck- und Applikationsmaschinen

It’s driven by Operations Managers who bring the team together to push excellence in safety, quality and productivity across our sites. At your site, you’ll lead other managers and create the operational plan that helps your teams meet their targets. This role is all about driving operational excellence to create the Amazon of tomorrow.

Shift: Yes (late shift or night shift)

- An attractive compensation package including Restricted Stock Units (through Amazon.com, Inc.)

title: DLS Case Manager
descriptionHtml:
Application deadline: Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis

At Amazon we believe that every day is still day one. We are working to be the most customer-centric company on earth. To get there, we need exceptionally talented, bright, and driven people. If you’d like to help the Disability Leave Services (DLS) team build a best-in-class professional services program to deliver leave of absence, disability and accommodation services to Amazon employees, applicants, job seekers and candidates globally, this is your chance to make history by joining our team. DLS Provides services 7 days a week, 24 hours a day to assist employees as they go through qualifying life events.

The DLS Case Manager provides case management for all types of leave of absence and disability life events. The DLS Case Manager is highly skilled in answering questions, understanding the employee’s situation, applying the appropriate benefits, responding to changing circumstances and needs, and paves the way for a connected and trusted case management experience. Case Managers are the single point of contact for an employee throughout an entire leave of absence or disability event.

This is an individual contribution (IC) role with no direct reports.

This is a seasonal position to cover temporary needs of the organization. Extensions and/or conversions to a permanent role are subject to business needs and employee delivery.

• Identify and solve problems that may arise, sometimes with limited information

descriptionHtml:

You will work across a broad range of technologies, translating business objectives into well-architected technical strategies that are secure, reliable, cost-optimized, and built to scale.

This role offers the opportunity to serve as a trusted technical advisor, guiding customers through critical decisions around platform adoption, migration, and modernization. You will bring both depth and breadth of knowledge to every engagement, balancing short-term needs with long-term architectural goals. If you are a curious, self-starter who enjoys collaborating across teams and making a tangible impact on how customers build for the future, we want to hear from you.

title: Sr. Product Manager Tech - AWS, Global System Integration
descriptionHtml:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. We keep the cloud running: the data centers and all the power, cooling, networking, and structural systems behind them.

Within that, the Global System Integration team builds the next generation of data center products. We are accountable for cost per megawatt, construction cycle time, on-time launch, design error rates, embedded carbon, and labor moved off site.

As a Sr. Product Manager - Technical, you own the business case for a data center product or platform. You define the problem worth solving: the cost target, the customer need, and the limits the design must meet. You help the team make real tradeoffs, and you stay accountable from first concept to the final megawatt delivered.

Key job responsibilities
- Own the business case for each product or platform you carry, defining the cost target, customer need, constraint set, and measure of success.
- Set and defend the constraint box Engineering solves within, drawing the cost, schedule, sustainability, and buildability limits from the business case.
- Govern design change, the largest controllable cost driver, by being the test every proposed change passes or fails on whether it earns its cost and schedule hit against the case.
- Own the full chain from design decision to delivered megawatt.
- Prioritize across the portfolio when new demand arrives, deciding what gets staffed and what slips, naming the cost of leaving a product understaffed, and tying every staffing ask to a specific product and tier so the tradeoffs stay explicit and documented.
- Author and defend the business case in the operating plans, reviews, and strategy papers that release capital, and turn repeatable product judgment into decision-support mechanisms the organization can run without you.


A day in the life
You start by checking the products you own against their cases: is cost on target, are dates holding without burning buffer, are design errors trending down. In a design review, you judge not the engineering but whether a proposed change earns its cost and schedule hit and whether anyone has signed off the departure. When new demand lands, you decide what it displaces and write that tradeoff down so it is traceable. You draft a business case for an operating-plan review, coach a PM through theirs, and close an open sign-off before it re-opens first principles.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree
- Experience owning/driving roadmap strategy and definition
- Experience with feature delivery and tradeoffs of a product
- Experience contributing to engineering discussions around technology decisions and strategy related to a product
- Experience managing technical products or online services
- Experience in representing and advocating for a variety of critical customers and stakeholders during executive-level prioritization and planning

Preferred qualifications

- Master's degree
- Experience bridging technical and business teams to collect and refine requirements, prioritize incoming work requests, and ensure all committed work is delivered on time
- 5+ years of product or program management, product marketing, business development or technology experience

title: EHS Specialist
descriptionHtml:
Join Amazon’s mission to become Earth’s safest place to work! At Amazon, we’ve set the ambitious goal to become the benchmark of safety excellence across all industries in which we operate. As a Workplace Health & Safety Specialist (WHSS), you'll be at the forefront of transforming workplace safety culture at one of the world's most innovative companies. Your expertise and dedication will directly protect employees, ensuring they return home safely to their families every day. You'll facilitate new approaches to safety, combining technology with human-centered solutions to create an environment where safety and productivity thrive together. title: SNR Reliability Maintenance Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Our Reliability Maintenance Engineering (RME) team is central to Amazon's commitment to innovation. As Amazon evolves and adapts, this team makes sure that the tools and technologies we use do as well. As a Senior RME Technician, you'll help us stay one step ahead, adopting the latest technologies and identifying new and efficient ways of working. In this role, you’ll pay close attention to our processes to help maintain our high standards, and you’ll put in place upgrades to take that standard even higher.

Key job responsibilities
- Demonstrate best practice on using equipment safely and monitor teams to ensure everyone follows the correct processes
- Keep track of equipment performance through visual checks, condition-based monitoring, and preventative maintenance tasks and schedule additional servicing when required
- Supervise technicians on shift to support their development and act as the first point of contact for Reliability Maintenance Engineers
- Solve issues in equipment to reduce downtime for operations so they can process packages as quickly as possible
- Support in finding ways to continually improve systems and standardise processes across the EU network

A day in the life
In every shift, you’ll be leading a team to make sure everyone has the equipment they need and that it’s running properly. That involves monitoring processes so that regulations and policies are followed and ensuring that preventative maintenance is carried out to increase equipment uptime.

With everything you observe on your shifts, you’ll suggest improvements to make our systems more efficient and productive and then implement those improvements across an EU-wide function. You’ll also be monitoring processes with tools like Scada to guarantee their performance, as well as working closely with your line manager to assist with admin tasks.

This role is located at one of our operational sites. You’ll work shift patterns, which may include some weekends and nights. As you develop your experience within this exciting part of Amazon, you’ll be well-placed to progress into more senior roles.

About the team
Our Reliability Maintenance Engineering or RME team keep our equipment performing at its best. We're a technically minded team, made up of excellent team players and guided by experienced leaders. We work together to maintain, troubleshoot and repair equipment across our global network of fulfilment centres. Some of our people are leaders, who oversee the team as they work on exciting technology – some of which only exists at Amazon.

From installing automated packaging systems to overseeing the general maintenance of a site to repairing key distribution equipment, our team handles most aspects of Amazon’s technical side. This includes keeping buildings legally compliant, so everyone is safe, and our sites are operating at maximum efficiency. There are lots of opportunities for progression, both within the RME team and more widely across Amazon.

Everything we do focuses on reducing downtime in Amazon’s crucial operations sites, so customers get their orders on time. We often work during early or late hours to carry out maintenance with minimal disruption, including night shifts. If we spot a better way to do something, we have the skills and the opportunity to develop and introduce completely new processes or cutting-edge tech like Amazon Robotics and our Complex Item Sorter.

Basic qualifications

- NVQ Level 3 in Mechanical, Electrical or Mechatronics, or completed a 4-year UK certified apprenticeship
- Work a flexible schedule/shift/work area, including weekends, nights, and/or holidays
- Relevant experience in a technical leadership role
- Relevant experience working in both electrical and mechanical disciplines
- Relevant experience in automation or material handling equipment environments
- Advanced proficiency in verbal and written English

Preferred qualifications

- Experience working in a multi-contractor and multi-site working environment
- Understanding of PLC based controls systems and statutory compliance requirements
- Experience using computerised maintenance management systems to plan proactive maintenance and record reactive tasks
- A degree preferably in a technical discipline or operations

descriptionHtml:
Amazon Web Services (AWS) Infrastructure Operations is growing rapidly, with new data center facilities coming online to support expanding machine learning and core cloud computing workloads. We are looking for a Cluster Operations Leader to help us keep pace with that growth by leading the teams responsible for the safety, security, availability, scaling, efficiency, and cost management of Amazon data center clusters and colocation operations within an assigned region.

Infrastructure Operations consists of two core functions: Data Center Operations (DCO) and Data Center Engineering Operations (DCEO). DCO manages server-level platforms supporting Amazon Retail and AWS, while DCEO handles mechanical, electrical, and controls systems for critical environments. A physical security team also works closely with these functions to protect people, assets, and customer data. As Cluster Operations Leader, you will build and lead high-performing teams across both functions, combining strategic oversight with hands-on technical problem-solving to deliver reliable, efficient infrastructure at scale. You will also explore the analytical use of AI agents to increase operational productivity and accelerate capacity delivery for business priorities. This role gives you direct exposure to the latest data center infrastructure and cloud technologies while you manage large-scale operations teams — a combination that positions you for continued growth within AWS.

Key job responsibilities
- Build, hire, and develop operations managers and their teams across compute and engineering operations, ensuring the right talent and team structure to support facility growth
- Design and execute the operational strategy for new data center and colocation expansions, including preventive maintenance, corrective maintenance, and change management programs
- Lead incident response for safety, security, and availability events, driving root-cause analysis and long-term corrective actions
- Identify and implement process improvements, including the analytical use of AI agents, to increase operational productivity and reduce costs
- Partner with engineering, supply chain, and capacity planning teams to align infrastructure delivery with machine learning and core cloud computing demand

A day in the life
You will split your time between strategic planning sessions with your peer managers in engineering and capacity planning, and operational reviews with your direct reports who run day-to-day compute and engineering operations. Mornings may involve reviewing incident reports and maintenance metrics with your DCEO and DCO leads, while afternoons shift to working with cross-regional partners on expansion timelines or evaluating AI-driven productivity tools with your team. When an availability event occurs, you step in to coordinate the response and ensure rapid resolution.

About the team
Our Infrastructure Operations team keeps AWS running by owning the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment inside every AWS data center. We are in a period of significant facility growth driven by increasing demand for machine learning and core cloud computing capacity, and this role is central to making sure that growth translates into reliable, efficient operations for our customers. We are a collaborative group of engineers, operations managers, and technical specialists who take pride in solving hard problems together and continuously raising the bar on operational performance. You will gain hands-on experience with emerging infrastructure and cloud technologies as the team scales, building expertise that grows alongside the business.

- Experience in management of datacenter operations, facility engineering operations, information technology critical environment facilities, advanced high volume manufacturing, datacenter build-outs and scaling, or similar fields
- Demonstrated track record in delivering complex analytical and quantitative projects through verbal and written communication.
- Proven ability to hire, develop and manage high-performing geographically distributed technical teams

Preferred qualifications

- Experience with Continuous Improvement and Six Sigma methodologies
- Knowledge of information technology infrastructure domains such as compute server platforms, storage server platforms, server components, network devices, technologies and architectures, IT service delivery principles and best practices

title: Manager, Software Development, Accounting Insights (Transportation Financial Systems)
descriptionHtml:
If you want to apply machine learning and generative AI to a problem where accuracy has a dollar value, this is the role for you. Transportation Financial Systems (TFS) builds the technology that records, reconciles and posts the accounting for Amazon's transportation invoices and payments across 16+ transportation modes. Today, month-end close depends on people tracing breaks across ten or more systems, one case at a time. The Accounting Insights team replaces that with software. We detect anomalies in financial data with machine learning, find the root cause of a break with generative AI, produce explanations and insights for controllers and accountants, and automate the standard operating procedures (SOPs) that run the close. You will lead a team of engineers, own the roadmap with product management and Accounting partners.

Key job responsibilities
What will you own?

You will manage a team of engineers and grow them through long-term technical problems their team solves.
You will own the technical roadmap for your area with TFS Product Management, Accounting and Controllership partners.
You will own operational excellence for your services: operational load, security, resiliency and compliance at Amazon scale.
You will set the bar for taking AI into a controlled financial process, with audit evidence, approval steps and separation of duties built in.

What interesting engineering problem will you solve?

You will build machine learning models that detect anomalies in reconciliation, balance and posting data before close, with precision you can measure.
You will build generative AI agents that trace a break to its owning system and team and propose a permanent fix, with human confirmation before it is submitted.
You will build a generative AI assistant that answers balance and variance questions from reconciled figures and attaches the supporting evidence.
You will automate close SOPs as versioned, auditable procedures that AI helps author and run, replacing spreadsheets and individual knowledge.

What large scale program opportunities will you have?

You will own the partner relationship with Accounting, Controllership and Audit, and influence their roadmap as well as yours.
You will work with principal product managers and business leaders to prioritize work and deliver it with quality.
You will make sure open issues and debated topics reach the right forums, so your team's roadmap stays protected.

What Think Big exists for you?

You can move month-end close from a monthly investigation to a continuous, automated certification.
You can turn each one-off root-cause investigation into a permanent fix, so the same class of break stops recurring.

Basic qualifications

- 8+ years of leading the definition and development of multi tier web services experience
- 3+ years of engineering team management experience
- 7+ years of engineering experience
- Experience partnering with product or program management teams
- Knowledge of engineering practices and patterns for the full software/hardware/networks development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, certification, and livesite operations
- Experience designing or architecting (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in communicating with users, other technical teams, and senior leadership to collect requirements, describe software product features, technical designs, and product strategy
- Experience in recruiting, hiring, mentoring/coaching and managing teams of Software Engineers to improve their skills, and make them more effective, product software engineers

title: Security Incident Response, Security Engineer, US Amazon Dedicated Cloud Security
descriptionHtml:
The AWS Security Incident Response team is looking for a Security Engineer to help protect the AWS infrastructure that our national security customers rely on. You will join a growing team that handles incident response in AWS GovCloud and U.S. Amazon Dedicated Cloud (ADC) regions, along with other security requirements specific to our government customers.

You will analyze logs, investigate and respond to security events, support forensic investigations, and help build the tools that let the team work faster and at greater scale. You'll work with engineers across AWS to contain issues and stop them from happening again, and you'll learn to explain risks clearly to different audiences. You do well under pressure and can think like both an attacker and a defender.

This position requires that the candidate selected be a US Citizen and must currently possess and maintain an active TS/SCI security clearance with polygraph.

Key job responsibilities
- Monitor security telemetry, and triage and investigate alerts in GovCloud and U.S. ADC regions.
- Support incidents from detection through containment, eradication, recovery, and after-action review.
- Perform log analysis and support forensic investigations.
- Build and improve scripts, detections, and tools that help the team work faster.
- Document findings and communicate them clearly to team members and stakeholders.
Participate in a regular on-call rotation.

Your day starts with a review of overnight security alerts across GovCloud and U.S. ADC regions. You triage the queue, separate noise from real threats, and dig into a suspicious login pattern. title: Software Development Engineer, Autonomous Fleet Services
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Robotics Autonomous Fleet Services (AFS) is building the intelligence that turns autonomous robots into fleets that work together. Our software orchestrates thousands of robots across some of the most complex logistics operations in the world, so that every robot, every task, and every minute counts. We are growing and seek a talented, enthusiastic, and motivated Software Development Engineer to help build our Fleet Management system.

The Fleet Management team builds the brain of the fleet: the system that sees everything happening on the floor, decides what every robot does next, and keeps operations running as conditions change around it. As an SDE on this team, you will own significant components of that system, from the services that turn arriving work into tasks to the logic that assigns and re-assigns those tasks as robots, floor space and deadlines shift. You will design and build features end to end, take them through code review and launch, and carry them in production once they are live. You will contribute to design reviews for systems other teams depend on, and grow into the calls that decide how the fleet behaves under load and under failure. The systems you help build will scale to thousands of robots working safely and efficiently alongside people, and grow as Amazon's robotics footprint expands across the globe.

The successful candidate is a hands-on builder with solid experience designing, building and operating scalable, highly available distributed systems in production. You are comfortable with ambiguity: taking a problem stated in terms of floor outcomes, asking the questions that sharpen it, and shipping incrementally without disrupting live operations. You reason from measured behavior rather than intuition, and you expect to be held to what the data says. Experience in areas such as distributed systems, task allocation and scheduling, resource management, event-driven architectures, and operating production services is desired. Familiarity with robotics, logistics, or warehouse automation is a plus.

title: Controls Technician, Controls Deployment Service
descriptionHtml:
As a member of the Global Controls Team, you will collaborate with highly motivated operators, engineers and technicians in the data center industry to maintain and optimize critical infrastructure systems. You will be responsible for troubleshooting and maintaining the Building Management System (BMS) and Electrical Power Monitoring System (EPMS) while developing new processes and standards that drive innovation in the controls space.

AWS data centers utilize sophisticated industrial control systems to automatically operate mechanical equipment, maintaining optimal temperature and pressure conditions throughout the facilities. These systems integrate and monitor multiple critical components, including generators, uninterruptible power sources, diesel generators, electrical switchgear, power distribution units, variable frequency drives, automatic and static transfer switches, air-cooled and water-cooled chillers, pumps, cooling towers, heat exchangers, Computer Room Air Handlers (CRAHs), and air economizers. Within this industrial control system infrastructure, the BMS serves as the primary control platform for all mechanical systems within the data center, while the EPMS functions as the primary monitoring platform for all electrical systems. This position offers the opportunity to work with cutting-edge technology in mission-critical environments while contributing to the reliability and efficiency of AWS's global infrastructure.

Amazon does not sponsor for immigration, including for H-1B, TN, and other non-immigrant visas, for this role.

Key job responsibilities
Primarily work in and support multiple data centers by deploying, servicing, and upgrading BMS and EPMS systems.

Mentor and train Facilities team members on the operation and control of BMS and EPMS systems.

Manage small to medium-sized projects and programs.

Perform point-to-point checkouts between field devices and controllers.

Perform first-line diagnostics, troubleshooting, and maintenance of programming code and hardware associated with BMS and EPMS in data centers.

Execute provisioning processes for servers, controllers, industrial PCs, and network configurations, including communication testing between third-party devices and controllers or servers.

Install, replace, configure, and calibrate sensors.

Read and interpret electrical schematics and control panel drawings with a basic understanding of closed-loop controls, field sensor scaling, and functions typically performed by industrial controllers.

Supervise low-voltage electrical contractors performing wiring and installation of field devices in compliance with AWS requirements.

Provide commissioning and systems-level testing support.

Create red-lined drawings and documentation of systems.

Follow change management processes to generate work requests and methods of procedures.

Participate in factory witness tests at vendor or panel builder facilities.

Perform root cause analysis during testing and commissioning.

Ensure personnel on site utilize proper safety methodology.

Perform service activities including monitoring and reviewing ticketing systems, conducting root cause analysis, and prioritizing tasks.

Actively manage service agreements including vendor labor scheduling, quality assurance, and financial invoice review.

Participate in material handling tasks such as lifting, carrying, or moving up to 50 lbs of equipment, and utilize OSHA-standard safety equipment including limited weight-bearing work platforms, ladders, step stools, and personal protective equipment (PPE) such as safety harnesses.

Perform other tasks as assigned by manager.

You might diagnose a controller communication loss, calibrate instruments feeding inaccurate data to operators, or supervise vendors performing quarterly maintenance. Basic qualifications

- Associate's degree
- High school or equivalent diploma
- Associate’s degree, trade school certification, or other certified training in a related technical field with [Year_1] years of relevant industrial Controls or HVAC controls experience, OR [Year_2] years of relevant industrial or HVAC controls experience in lieu of a degree.
- Basic understanding of Industrial controls system, knowledge of meters, devices, sensors, relays and troubleshooting utilizing standard hand tools, digital metering, or calibration/diagnostic equipment in a data center, hospitals, large commercial complex, water, power, oil & gas or similar industries.
- [Year_3] years of experience working with low voltage controls, wiring, networking signals, electrical and mechanical systems, computers and operating systems.

descriptionHtml:

The AWS Throttling Service is a managed service for distributed rate limiting that protects AWS services from unexpected traffic spikes. It gives service owners near infinite throttle scaling, a more efficient throttling client, and better safety for throttle rule configuration and updates. Customers of AWS Throttling have better price-performance, more accuracy, and increased flexibility in tuning more complex throttling decisions. The AWS Throttling platform supports throttle rule analysis and traffic insights visible in the console, along with partner integrations such as Service Quotas in visibility mode.

title: Vehicle Design Engineer, Prime Air Vehicle Design, Modelling, & Test
descriptionHtml:
Our Prime Air Drone Vehicle Design, Modelling, and Test team within Flight Sciences is looking for a Vehicle Design Engineer to help us rapidly configure, design, analyze, prototype, and test innovative drone vehicles and vehicle subsystems. You'll model internal subsystems, major structural elements, and the OML of the vehicle. Your designs will feed into our suite of multi-disciplinary optimization (MDO) tools to help size the vehicle and mature the design. How do you get items to customers quickly, cost-effectively, and—most importantly—safely, in less than an hour? And how do you do it in a way that can scale? Check out more information about Prime Air on the About Amazon blog (https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/transportation/amazon-prime-air-delivery-drone-reveal-photos).

title: Onsite Medical Representative
descriptionHtml:
Join Amazon’s mission to become Earth’s safest place to work! At Amazon, we’ve set the ambitious goal to become the benchmark of safety excellence across all industries in which we operate. The Amazon Workplace Health & Safety (WHS) team sets the strategic direction to provide resources, best practices, and safe environments to proactively manage the health and wellbeing of our workforce. To support these goals, Amazon is seeking an experienced and dynamic Onsite Medical Representative (OMR) to join our team. In this position, you will work closely with the WHS Site Manager, WHS Specialist, and occasionally the Injury Prevention Specialist (IPS). This includes attending weekly associate safety committee meetings, greeting all new hires for the site or through daily one-on-one interaction. Additionally, the OMR will participate in weekly case management review meetings as necessary. As an OMR, you will independently assess and administer first aid as well as offer guidance to Amazon Associates (AAs) on both occupational and non-occupational injuries or illnesses. You should be passionate about learning and advocating health and wellness principles to consistently support AAs on a daily basis. You will refer care to outside medical providers as needed, and learn about OSHA regulations, risk, and analysis. The OMR will function as a part of the larger team onsite, assisting with all first aid needs and support safety operations as needed.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:
- Provide first aid support and make referrals to outside medical providers as necessary.
- Minimize the AA risk of injury through awareness, education, and proactive engagement.
- Maintain all records of care provided to AAs.
- Coordinate and maintain the workers’ compensation and return to work programs for AAs with work-related injuries.
- Provide daily activity logs and end of shift reports.
- Engage with AAs and leadership on operations floor to provide coaching regarding observed at-risk work habits.
- Maintain a clean working environment and ensure appropriate medical supply inventory is maintained.
- Participate in training and certification to facilitate first aid, CPR and AED certifications classes.
- Maintain all first aid, CPR, AED credentials.
- Work flexible shifts which could include days, nights, holidays, and/or weekends.
- Assist with random saliva drug testing protocols.
- Maintain effective care delivery in emergencies and assist emergency response at the site.

Additional Job Elements include:
- Lift up to 49 pounds and frequently push, pull, squat, bend, and reach
- Stand/walk for up to 12 hours during shifts
- Work in an environment where the noise level varies
- Work in an environment that is subject to variable temperatures and weather (delivery stations include outside loading departments)
- Continuously climb and descend stairs (applies to sites with stairs)

For those that do not have an adult First Aid, CPR, AED certification from the American Heart Association or American Red Cross, must obtain within 3 weeks of start date.

Basic qualifications

- High school or equivalent diploma
- Current valid Basic Life Support (BLS) certification by an approved emergency cardiac care (ECC) provider; AND must have one of the following:
- Current valid Emergency Medical Technician (EMT) OR Paramedic Certification from the Department of Health OR the National Registry of Emergency Medical Technicians (NREMT); OR
- Current active Athletic Trainer Certification, by either the Board of Certification (BOC) or equivalent State Certification.

Preferred qualifications

- Certified to teach first aid, CPR, and AED training from American Heart Association or American Red Cross
- Proficient in Microsoft Office
- Experience with an industrial wellness program
- Experience managing musculoskeletal disorders, ergonomics, and coaching on body mechanics
- Demonstrated work experience with OSHA regulations and Workers Compensation
- Proficient in digital recordkeeping
- In the last year, six months job experience in the Military as a Combat Medic (U.S. Army), Field Medic (U.S. Army), Healthcare Specialist (U.S. Army), Hospital Corpsman (U.S. Navy), or Aerospace Medical Service Technician (U.S. Air Force)

title: Controls Integration Engineer, One MHS | Systems Integration and Flow
descriptionHtml:
The Controls Integration Engineer defines how automated material handling systems operate and owns the site-specific setup of the controls application software that runs them, assembling and configuring standard code for each site's conveyors, sorters, and automated work cells. For an assigned project, the engineer leads technical execution end to end: authoring the functional specifications, defining test criteria, and delivering tested, reviewed code and documentation ready for field deployment. The engineer solves difficult technical problems with visible risks or roadblocks, bringing clarity to implementations where the business problem is understood but the solution is not fully designed. The engineer mentors the engineers on the project, reviews every deliverable for quality and downstream readiness, and builds close partnerships with third-party vendors and cross-functional teams. The engineer is also the primary handoff contact to the field team and carries field lessons learned back to upstream design teams. The goal is to take risk out of every project before it reaches the field and give the field team everything it needs to bring the site up.

Key job responsibilities
Application Development and Delivery
Own application deliverables for the assigned project from planning through handoff.
Assemble and configure the site's controls application software from standard code libraries, adapting it where the project requires.
Partner with design teams to resolve open functional questions and drive decisions to closure.
Contribute to design reviews with partner teams, bringing the controls and system function perspective.
Testing and Validation
Define test criteria for emulation, digital twin, and Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT) in partnership with simulation, equipment, and design teams.
Lead emulation and digital twin testing, verifying that system flow meets design intent.
Participate in FAT and Site Acceptance Testing (SAT) as the system function expert.
Build the site's commissioning test cases from the standard test case library, in partnership with the field team.
Cross-Team Partnerships
Build strong partnerships with cross-functional teams and third-party vendors, leading site-level coordination to resolve technical issues and unblock progress.
Define functional requirements for third-party interfaces and drive gaps to resolution with third-party teams.
Communicate status, risks, and decisions clearly to project stakeholders.
Serve as the primary partner to the field team from planning through handoff.
Site Handoff and Post-Handoff Support
Deliver a complete, documented handoff package for each project.
Train the field team on each subsystem before handoff.
Partner with the field team on root cause analysis and corrective action for issues found in the field.
Continuous Improvement and Mentorship
Document issues, resolutions, and lessons learned, and feed them back to upstream design teams to improve future projects.
Improve team procedures, templates, and tools based on project experience.
Mentor engineers through hands-on guidance and deliverable review.
AutoStore-Specific Commissioning Duties:

Commission and validate AutoStore grid infrastructure, robot fleet initialization, port configurations, and charging systems
Troubleshoot robot navigation faults, bin handling errors, and port throughput issues
Analyze system logs, datasets, and diagnostic outputs to identify trends, anomalies, and root cause of system failures
Monitor and optimize system performance using diagnostic tools (PowerBI, Databricks, AutoStore controller software)
Support grid modifications, expansion projects, and firmware/software upgrades
Conduct advanced root cause analysis on system failures and performance deviations
Validate end-to-end material flow from AutoStore grid through conveyance to outbound operations
Collaborate with AutoStore distribution partners, customers, and internal teams to ensure successful deployments and minimal downtime
Interpret system telemetry, performance metrics, and monitoring dashboards to drive continuous improvement

- Experience with networking fundamentals including hands-on experience with load balancers, switches, routers, etc.

- Travel up to 50% of the time
- Willingness to travel up to 50% for on-site commissioning and deployment support.
- Hands-on experience with industrial communication protocols such as Ethernet/IP, Profinet, EtherCAT, or Modbus TCP.

- Experience developing or testing application software for industrial automation systems using IEC 61131-3 platforms such as Codesys, Rockwell Logix (Studio 5000), Siemens TIA Portal, Beckhoff TwinCAT, or equivalent.

- 5+ years of experience in systems development engineering, controls application development, or industrial automation.

Preferred qualifications

- Familiarity with object-oriented programming concepts in an IEC 61131-3 environment (e.g., structured function blocks, reusable control architectures).
- Experience supporting large-scale commissioning projects such as automated warehouses, conveyor and sorter systems, or complex manufacturing environments.

title: Product Manager, Technical III, External Services, AWS Training and Certification
descriptionHtml:
AWS Applied AI Solutions (AAIS) is building toward a future where every business innovates with Amazon AI teammates. To get there, we build AI solutions that improve human capabilities and transform entire business functions. We create end-to-end products that surprise and delight out-of-the-box, making complex things easy and hard things possible, with no cloud experience required. We start with customers who embrace the future and build bridges to meet the rest where they are. We pursue ambitious opportunities with conviction, and we are looking for builders who share that mindset.

Are you excited about defining a new category of software, AI teammates that help people learn and grow in the flow of their work? Do you want to shape how millions of professionals build skills, earn certifications, and get better at their jobs every day? Do you want direct and immediate impact on the way people and AI learn together?

As part of the AWS Training and Certification team, we are building AI learning teammates: agentic systems that don't just answer questions or hand out courses, but work alongside people, notice where they are getting stuck, and turn everyday tasks into moments of learning. These teammates bring the right guidance, practice, and credential right into the tools and tasks they already use. This is a new product space where the right experience is still being invented, and we are looking for a product leader who partners deeply with design to define it.

As a Senior Product Manager - Technical, External Services, you will partner with design and lead the development of AI learning teammates, owning the product vision, requirements, and roadmap from concept through go-to-market. You will champion the needs of learners and the organizations that train and certify them, and translate ambiguous, open-ended problems into clear product definitions and detailed business requirements documents. You will work hand-in-hand with design, engineering, science, learning scientists, and operational stakeholders to prioritize the roadmap and spearhead the definition of new capabilities.

This role sits where product, learning, and design meet. A great learning teammate is built on more than a strong model and solid systems. It depends on trust, on clear interaction patterns, and on how it feels to be coached while you work. You will co-own the end-to-end experience with design. That spans how a teammate joins a team, how it surfaces learning in the flow of work, how it recognizes mastery and guides someone toward certification, and how people stay in control of their own development.

The successful candidate must have exceptional problem solving skills, strong business judgment, and demonstrated experience leading cross-functional teams. We are looking for a proven ability to execute both strategically and tactically, and someone who is excited to take on new, ambiguous projects that will be industry defining. This position requires a solid technical background, and the candidate should be customer-focused with a passion for learning, AI, agents, and the future of how skills are built.

AWS Training and Certification helps people and organizations build the cloud and AI skills they need to be successful, from foundational learning through role-based certifications recognized across the industry. As a member of this team, you'll support the development and management of AI-powered learning experiences that reach learners worldwide, including the agentic learning teammates that will define the next decade of how people grow their skills.

Key job responsibilities
- Partner with design to define and own the end-to-end experience for AI learning teammates, from onboarding and interaction patterns to how learning is delivered in the flow of work.
- Define product requirements and author business requirements documents that align engineering, design, science, learning scientists, and leadership around a shared vision for each capability.
- Own the roadmap for one or more learning teammate product areas, making trade-off decisions across competing priorities, customer commitments, and technical investments.
- Represent the product externally with enterprise customers, translating their workforce development and certification needs into product direction and measurable adoption goals.
- Drive cross-team alignment to ensure teammate capabilities are composable and reusable across the learning portfolio, partnering with learning science and certification stakeholders to keep in-the-flow experiences grounded in proven learning principles.

A day in the life
You might start your morning in a design review, working through the interaction model for how a teammate offers a quick coaching moment the instant someone hits a task they haven't done before. By midday, you are reviewing skill-progression and certification-completion metrics and preparing a decision narrative for leadership on a proposed new capability. In the afternoon, you connect with learning scientists and engineering to pressure-test whether an in-the-flow learning experience is effective and feasible this quarter, then close out by refining requirements for the next capability and drafting a narrative that will guide customer-facing conversations.

About AWS
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Inclusive Team Culture Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship & Career Growth We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

title: Hardware Development Engineer, OneMHS - Electrical and Controls Engineering Architecture and Design
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking an experienced and highly motivated Hardware Development Engineer to serve as a technical authority for industrial controls network architecture and controls hardware within Amazon's global fulfillment center network. This role will define, standardize, and evolve the EtherCAT-based controls architecture used across material handling systems. You will focus on network topology, device selection, functional safety integration, scalability, and operational excellence. As part of OneMHS (One Material Handling Systems), you will help transform how Amazon designs, builds, and operates its material handling capabilities through standardized, high-performance controls hardware.
The ideal candidate has a proven track record in industrial network design, controls hardware integration, and device selection for complex material handling systems, including tote/parcel conveyance and sortation. You will work closely with Controls Software, WWDE, Operations Engineering, strategic suppliers, integration partners, and cross-functional teams to deliver robust, maintainable controls architectures.
This role requires deep technical expertise to create architecture standards and approved component baselines that guide vendor designs and multi-year roadmaps. It also requires the tactical execution to review designs, resolve integration issues, and improve the clarity and quality of project deliverables.

Key job responsibilities
EtherCAT Network Architecture & Topology
- Define and maintain the OneMHS EtherCAT controls architecture, including topology, ring and cable-redundancy design, segmentation, and device-order rules
- Develop architecture diagrams, and network topology drawings, and establish network design limits such as device counts per segment, cycle-time and latency budgets, and safety-connection capacity
- Define addressing, naming, and identification standards for devices, ports, and cables
- Establish network diagnostics, fault isolation, and troubleshooting practices for operations and maintenance teams
Device Selection, Qualification & Component Standards
- Select, specify, and qualify controls hardware for the architecture, including industrial PCs, couplers, I/O, MDR controllers, VFDs, IO-Link masters and devices, safety devices, scanners, sensors, and controls power supplies
- Own the approved component list, including exact part numbers, firmware/hardware revisions, and device profiles
- Evaluate new and alternate components for technical fit, compliance (e.g., UL, Class 2/LVLE), cost, availability, and lifecycle risk
- Partner with suppliers on technical requirements, certification status, product roadmaps, and obsolescence management
- Develop substitution and change-approval criteria for vendors and integration partners
Functional Safety Integration
- Define the integration of safety devices and safety-over-fieldbus (e.g., FSoE) into the controls architecture
- Establish safety-controller allocation, safety-zone, and E-stop integration rules in coordination with Safety and Controls teams
- Support compliance with applicable functional safety standards (e.g., ISO 13849, IEC 62061)
Hardware Development, Prototyping & Validation
- Build and maintain test benches and lab environments to validate devices, topologies, and failure modes
- Lead prototype testing, interoperability testing, and production-readiness validation of new hardware and architectures
- Support factory acceptance testing, site acceptance testing, and commissioning of controls hardware
OneMHS Program Specifications
- Author and maintain controls architecture specifications, device integration requirements, and cabling standards
- Define vendor deliverables for controls hardware, including device schedules, topology drawings, and bills of material
- Review integrator and OEM designs for compliance with OneMHS architecture and component standards
- Drive continuous improvement of specification templates and documentation for scaled deployment
Standards & Code Compliance
- Ensure controls hardware designs comply with NEC/NFPA 70, NFPA 79, UL 508A, and applicable IEC standards
- Serve as subject matter expert on industrial networking, controls hardware, and low-voltage controls requirements
- Conduct design reviews and audits to identify compliance gaps and safety risks
- Stay current with EtherCAT Technology Group guidance, industry standards, and regulatory changes
Technical Collaboration & Knowledge Sharing
- Mentor junior and mid-level engineers and designers
- Lead design reviews for controls architecture and hardware at site and program levels
- Collaborate with Controls Software, Operations, Facilities, Construction, WWDE, and Safety teams
- Build consensus across stakeholders, suppliers, and integration partners on architecture decisions

A day in the life
Collaborate with Controls Software, integration partners, and suppliers to define and refine the EtherCAT architecture for upcoming fulfillment center projects. Review vendor topology drawings and device schedules, evaluate a new device for inclusion in the approved component list, and work through an integration question with a supplier's engineering team. Validate a new topology or device in the lab before it reaches the field, and support a site team troubleshooting a commissioning issue.
Develop mechanisms that make controls hardware implementations repeatable across multiple simultaneous projects while maintaining the highest standards of safety, reliability, and performance.

About the team
One MHS is the central material handling systems organization within Amazon's global fulfillment center network. Our engineering teams design and deliver state-of-the-art power, hardware, and controls systems that keep the world's supply chains moving. We are committed to excellence, safety, and the professional growth of every team member.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree or above in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Systems Engineering, or related fields
- 4+ years of experience in industrial controls hardware design, industrial network architecture, or automation hardware development
- Experience designing and deploying industrial Ethernet or fieldbus networks (e.g., EtherCAT, EtherNet/IP, PROFINET)
- Experience selecting, specifying, and integrating industrial field devices such as I/O, drives, sensors, and safety devices
- Experience creating or reviewing electrical and controls drawings, network diagrams, and device schedules
- Knowledge of NEC/NFPA 70, NFPA 79, and UL 508A as applied to control panels and field wiring

Preferred qualifications

- Master's degree in electrical engineering or a related field
- Hands-on EtherCAT experience, including topology design, cable redundancy, distributed clocks, configuration (ESI/ENI), and diagnostics
- Experience with safety-over-fieldbus (e.g., FSoE, CIP Safety, PROFIsafe) and functional safety standards (ISO 13849, IEC 62061, IEC 61508)
- Experience with IO-Link devices and masters
- Experience with conveyor and sortation equipment, including MDR, VFDs, and barcode scanning systems
- 3+ years of PLC, IPC, or SCADA integration experience
- Experience with low-voltage controls power distribution, including Class 2/LVLE requirements and UL listings
- Experience owning component standards, approved vendor lists, or bills of material for a program
- Experience with supplier qualification, lab validation, reliability testing, and obsolescence management
- Familiarity with OT network security standards (e.g., IEC 62443)
- Experience working with material handling OEMs and controls integration partners
- Experience managing multiple projects and priorities in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment
- Experience using data and metrics to support decisions
- Excellent written and oral communication, problem-solving, and organizational skills

Amazon is looking for a Principal Public Policy leader to drive strategy, build consensus, and advance business goals through thoughtful policy engagement. In this role, you will own the development and execution of advocacy strategies across complex policy domains, engaging senior stakeholders in government and industry to influence outcomes that matter. You will tackle ambiguous, high-impact challenges that span multiple organizations, turning policy complexity into opportunity. If you are a strategic thinker who thrives on navigating nuance, building networks of influence, and delivering results at scale, we want to hear from you.

- Develop and lead policy strategies that advance Amazon's business objectives, identifying and owning positions on external policy issues informed by deep subject matter expertise and broad policy context.

- Drive cross-organizational alignment by creating key business documents, briefing memos, and policy position papers for leadership review, ensuring informed decision-making at the most senior levels.

We engage policymakers and stakeholders to ensure that the regulatory environment supports innovation and benefits customers. title: Senior Power Development Manager (Technical Infrastructure Program Manager), Global Ops Enterprise Services
descriptionHtml:
Power availability is no longer a background variable — it is the binding constraint on where and how fast Amazon can grow its real estate network. Amazon WWOps Real Estate is looking for a Senior Power Development Manager (TIPM) to own power due diligence, utility engagement, and infrastructure strategy across the industrial real estate portfolio. You will embed power intelligence upstream in the site selection process, build repeatable frameworks that replace bespoke assessments, and develop strategic utility relationships that support Amazon investment plans and capacity availability. You will define how power development operates at portfolio scale and shift it from a reactive bottleneck into a proactive input that accelerates network delivery. Along the way, you will build a rare skill set that spans grid economics, real estate development, and capital strategy — a combination that is increasingly sought after across industrial infrastructure.

Key job responsibilities
- Own portfolio-wide power due diligence — load letter requests, substation capacity analysis, service territory research, and interconnection feasibility — to make power intelligence a scalable input to site selection.
- Build and maintain strategic utility relationships across priority markets, moving from transactional inquiries to partnerships that provide advance visibility into grid investment plans and capacity availability.
- Evaluate upstream infrastructure constraints such as interconnection lead times, feeder loading, transformer capacity, and distribution upgrade requirements to identify and de-risk capacity-constrained sites early in the pipeline.
- Translate complex utility and grid data into real estate economics, delivery timelines, and investment decisions for stakeholders across real estate, engineering, operations, design and construction, and transactions.
- Design repeatable processes, templates, and market intelligence tools that standardize power development across the portfolio and reduce assessment cycle time.

A day in the life
Your week alternates between external utility engagement and internal cross-functional coordination, with heads-down analytical work filling the gaps. One morning you might be on a call with a utility interconnection team negotiating service timelines for a capacity-constrained market; that afternoon you are presenting a portfolio-level power risk summary to directors across real estate and operations. Between meetings, you are interpreting substation data, modeling interconnection feasibility, or building the trackers and templates that make the next site evaluation faster. The cadence is deal-driven and portfolio-driven, with no sprint ceremonies or ticket queues. You operate with high autonomy as the dedicated owner of power development, self-organizing across dozens of concurrent site inquiries and using your judgment daily to decide where your time creates the most portfolio impact.

About the team
Amazon's Global Realty Energy and Power team sits at the intersection of utility engineering, real estate development, and energy market strategy. We are changing how the company secures and delivers electrical infrastructure across one of the world's largest industrial real estate portfolios, moving from transactional utility engagement to strategic infrastructure positioning. Our work directly determines whether Amazon can secure the grid capacity it needs, when it needs it, in the markets that matter most. Growth on this team comes through direct leadership engagement — regular one-on-ones, real-time feedback on your work, and sponsorship into cross-functional forums where senior leaders see your contributions firsthand. The role is scoped as a launchpad: build the capability, prove the model, then grow into energy strategy leadership, real estate development management, infrastructure program leadership, or deeper technical specialization in power markets. If you want to build a new capability from the ground up and shape how Amazon approaches power development, we would like to hear from you.

Basic qualifications

- 5+ years of program management or technical project management experience
- Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Energy Systems, Power Engineering, or a related technical discipline
- Experience managing concurrent due diligence or project workstreams across a multi-site portfolio with competing priorities and aggressive timelines
- Experience in utility coordination, electrical infrastructure design, power development, or energy project delivery within large-scale utility, industrial, logistics, or data center environments
- Experience with utility easements, real property rights, and right-of-way documentation — including review, analysis, and coordination through resolution

Preferred qualifications

- Master's degree in Electrical, Mechanical, Power Engineering, or a related field
- Working knowledge of ISO/RTO market structures (PJM, ERCOT, CAISO, MISO, NYISO, ISO-NE, SPP) and their implications for large commercial load acquisition and utility procurement strategy
- Hands-on experience with load request and managing the demand/load side interconnection process
- Experience with utility rate structures, demand response programs, power purchase agreements, or energy procurement
- Experience in industrial or logistics real estate, data center infrastructure, or large-scale operational environments

title: Video Editor & Media Manager, Amazon Leo Marketing
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Leo is Amazon’s low Earth orbit satellite network, built to deliver fast, reliable broadband to people and places beyond the reach of existing networks. From families and small businesses to schools, hospitals, and entire communities, we’re working to connect the world in ways that weren’t possible before. We just created a new brand. Now comes the fun part.

We’ve spent years building the technology and creating the Amazon Leo brand from the ground up. Now we’re bringing it to life. And we’ve got some incredible ingredients to work with: rockets launching into space, satellites orbiting hundreds of miles above Earth, innovative technology, and, most importantly, the people and communities whose lives will change when they get connected. There’s no shortage of great stories to tell. We just need the right people to help us tell them.

We’re looking for a Social Video Editor who’s equal parts storyteller, craftsman, and creative problem solver. Someone who can find a great story in hours of raw footage, knows how to make people stop scrolling, and brings their own creative instincts to every project.

This is a dual role, split evenly between creating social-first video content and helping us build the Digital Asset Management (DAM) systems that power our creative team. You’ll work across consumer, business, and government audiences around the world, helping shape how Amazon Leo looks, feels, and tells stories. If you love great storytelling, obsess over the details, and get excited about building something new, we’d love to hear from you.

Key job responsibilities
• Create compelling, social-first video content for Amazon Leo, including influencer collaborations, branded content, product storytelling, behind-the-scenes videos, and short-form social campaigns.
• Edit and craft engaging stories through pacing, music, sound design, motion graphics, color correction, and creative finishing. Bring strong editorial instincts and attention to detail to every project.
• Bring the Amazon Leo brand to life through creative use of Aurora particles, Krypton Purple, typography, motion, and sound. Find fresh and unexpected ways to use these elements to tell stories that feel unmistakably Amazon Leo.
• Adapt creative content for different social platforms, audiences, and formats, balancing platform trends and best practices with a consistent brand identity.
• Collaborate with Creative Directors, Social, Marketing, and production partners to develop and execute engaging video content for consumer, business, and government audiences.
• Transform complex technology and technical subjects into accessible, entertaining stories. Find the human moments that make people care about what we’re building.
• Partner with Social and Marketing teams to understand content performance and identify opportunities to improve future creative work.
• Help develop, organize, and manage Amazon Leo’s Digital Asset Management (DAM) system, supporting a growing global library of video, photography, animation, audio, and finished creative assets.
• Maintain consistent media management practices, including metadata, tagging, naming conventions, folder structures, version control, and project archiving.
• Support efficient workflows for ingesting, organizing, reviewing, approving, distributing, and retrieving creative assets across internal teams and external production partners.
• Maintain accurate asset information, including usage rights, permissions, and licensing details, to support secure and appropriate content sharing.
• Identify opportunities to improve post-production and asset management workflows, including exploring AI-assisted creative tools, automation, and new technologies.
• Manage multiple editing and asset management projects simultaneously, balancing creative quality, organization, and deadlines.
• Make outrageously cool content.

A day in the life
Your morning starts with a fresh batch of footage from a creator who’s been putting Amazon Leo to the test. You’ve got hours of material, a few great moments, and an opportunity to tell a story that people actually want to watch. You jump into the edit, find the hook, experiment with music and pacing, and start turning raw footage into something worth sharing.

Next, you’re working with our creative and social teams on a new campaign. We’ve built an entirely new visual identity, and now we get to play with it. Aurora particles that bring connectivity to life. Krypton Purple, inspired by the technology powering our satellites. Golden Hour, capturing the warmth of the best moments in our customers’ lives. A distinct motion language, typography, and sonic identity. These aren’t just brand guidelines. They’re creative tools for finding new ways to tell stories.

Maybe you’re using Aurora particles to visualize a connection traveling across the world. Maybe you’re taking footage from a customer documentary and turning it into a compelling 30-second social story. Or maybe you’re working with an influencer to find a completely unexpected way to show what satellite internet makes possible. The challenge is to make it feel authentic, entertaining, and unmistakably Amazon Leo.

After lunch, you switch gears. Our library of footage, photography, animations, and finished content is growing fast. You’re helping build and manage our Digital Asset Management system, keeping everything organized, searchable, and ready for the next project. Because when you’re creating content around the world, finding the right shot shouldn’t take longer than editing it.

By the afternoon, you’re reviewing cuts with a Creative Director, collaborating with designers on a new animation, or experimenting with a social trend to see how it might work for our brand. We believe in cinematic storytelling, even when the finished video is only 15 seconds long. Sometimes the best story is a rocket launching into space. Sometimes it’s a quiet moment with someone getting connected for the first time. The trick is knowing which moments matter.

We’re building a brand that’s equal parts innovative technology and human connection. We want our work to feel thoughtful, surprising, and occasionally a little weird. We don’t want to make content just to fill a calendar. We want to make things people choose to watch.

And we want you to help us figure out what that looks like next.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree
- 5+ years of driving compelling creative strategy and execution at an agency or in-house creative team experience
- Experience developing digital campaigns for O&O channels that have global scale
- Experience managing multiple projects and meeting aggressive deadlines
- Knowledge of Adobe Creative software, primarily Premiere, After Effects, Photoshop/Indesign at an advanced level
- Experience with high-volume, high-velocity, large-scale file management (workflow orchestration, file-movement, permission management, etc.)
- Have an online portfolio demonstrating strong visual design skills and advertising experience across a range of media and platforms, along with work that reflects your design process
- Experience with Digital Asset Management (DAM) systems, media libraries, or professional post-production asset management workflows.

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in influencer, affiliate marketing
- Experience with asset management, design workflows, or partnering with creative teams
- Experience conveying complex technical concepts to both technical and business audiences
- Experience with online content, multimedia, analytics and impact measurements
- Experience building workflow automation and scripting (Python, AppleScript, or similar) to streamline handoffs, eliminate repetitive editorial tasks, and accelerate project turnarounds
- Experience building custom shortcuts, macros, NLE extensions, or integration panels that enhance editing capabilities
- Experience designing and managing automated ingest, proxy generation, transcoding, and delivery pipelines to remove manual media management bottlenecks
- Experience developing, implementing, or improving Digital Asset Management (DAM) systems, including iconik, Bynder, Frame.io, Wiredrive, or similar platforms

We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Do you have a background in electrical power systems and working with operations or program management teams? Are you excited to work on the world’s largest cloud computing infrastructure? In this role, you will own a global program to design and build power infrastructure that meets the highest bar for reliability and robustness, including reporting on reliability metrics across AWS’s global footprint.

You will engage with electric utilities across AWS’s global footprint to specify and contribute to the design of reliable transmission and distribution power infrastructure. You will manage multiple projects and evaluate the impacts of design considerations in medium and high voltage electric systems on existing and future data center operations.

The ideal candidate will possess a strong electrical engineering background, coupled with experience in data center program management. They will have a demonstrated ability to think strategically about business, product, and technical challenges, with the skill-set to successfully lead complex projects with a diverse group of internal and external stakeholders. By establishing and growing business and technical relationships, and managing the day-to-day interactions with these partners, this candidate will be responsible for ensuring the critical electrical infrastructure that serves AWS meets the highest standard for reliability and availability.


Key job responsibilities
Key job responsibilities
• Own program management for the global power reliability program
• Specify requirements for high and medium voltage systems that supply AWS data centers
• Manage technical elements of the interconnection of AWS data centers to the electric grid by working with utilities and local AWS operations and engineering teams across the globe
• Work with engineering teams at utilities and design firms to put forth innovative solutions to meet AWS requirements
• Support the development and execution of a comprehensive energy and utilities strategy for AWS data centers
• Drive process improvement to streamline execution of strategic initiatives and technology solutions
• Lead the development of metrics to ensure the most impactful delivery goals are formulated to meet program goals, including defining KPI's/SLA's used to drive high impact business decisions and reporting to senior leadership.
• Establish cadence to review overall program performance with internal and external stakeholders

About the team
Why AWS
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Diverse Experiences
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply.
